stories.title: Dhirendra Shastri depicted as Kansa in Mathura:Shown being struck by Lord Krishna; people say an apology will not save him
stories.summary: In Mathura, a poster depicted Bageshwar Dham head priest Pandit Dhirendra Shastri as Kansa, with Lord Krishna shown beating him. Every year, the Kansa Vadh Mela is held in Mathura's Rangeshwar area, featuring a variety of tableaux. On Thursday, the Mathur Chaturved Parishad's tableau depicted Dhirendra Shastri as Kansa. Mathur Chaturved Parishad president Rajan Pathak said, "There is no difference between Krishna and Ram. If you use abusive language about any god, do not assume that you can escape by apologising." At the Kansa Vadh Mela, children and elderly people beat an 18.5-foot-tall effigy with sticks. It is believed that when Lord Krishna and Balaram killed Kansa, the people of Braj were also present with them. This tradition has continued ever since. See 3 pictures... Read what Dhirendra Shastri had said about Lord Ram and Krishna Dhirendra Shastri had commented on Shri Krishna during the Shri Ram Katha being held in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh. A video of the remarks emerged on 10 October (Sunday). He had said: "Just look at even one picture of your Thakurji. Even when he stands, he is bent at three places. One foot over the other, bending at the waist in places, and playing the flute with his neck tilted. Our Lord, on the other hand, stands completely straight. Even his name is straight. Our Lord walks straight and looks straight as well. Your Lord's name is crooked, he walks crooked and stands crooked. Lifting a mountain is not a big deal. A disciple of our Lord made an entire mountain fly. Even the abode of our Lord is straight-Ayodhya; while your Lord's is Vrindavan!" Mathura's sadhus and saints expressed their displeasure over the statement and had demanded that Dhirendra Shastri apologise. However, as the controversy intensified, Dhirendra Shastri released a video clarification and said, "Many people misunderstood what I said. We are ourselves devotees of Thakurji and Braj." "We also narrate the Shrimad Bhagwat Katha and sing the praises of Thakurji. We had no intention of distinguishing between Lord Ram and Lord Krishna." What Dhirendra Shastri said in his clarification Pandit Dhirendra Shastri further clarified his statement, saying, "Just as the sakhis reproach Shri Ram, the gopis reproach Thakur Shri Krishna, poet Binduji Maharaj reproaches Thakurji, and Braj's saint Kokil Sai Ji reproaches Raghunath Ji, we too recited a verse in that spirit. It is a very popular verse by a saint: 'Playing the flute is just a game, but picking up the bow is not.'" We were explaining that very verse. However, instead of watching the full video, many people watched only half of it and branded us anti-Krishna. We are not anti-Krishna. Shri Krishna is our Thakurji. We ourselves repeatedly raise our voice for Krishna Janmabhoomi. His name is also part of our name. Our life exists because of him. Dhirendra Shastri said, "If our statement, explanation or sentiment has hurt anyone's feelings, we apologise. Please do not misinterpret our statement and present it in an exaggerated manner. We have not tried to divide society or God. Why would we divide God?" Ram and Krishna are one and the same. There is no difference between them. We said this emotionally. Even so, we ask all of you to understand our feelings. 'Playing the flute is a game; shooting a bow is not' Dhirendra Shastri had said, "Playing the flute is a game, but shooting a bow is not. All those of you seated here who worship Thakurji, today even your Thakurji is being hailed." He then pointed towards the artist playing the flute and said, "Listen, what does your Thakurji do? Play the flute? So playing the flute is hardly a big deal. Look, even this person here is playing it. Play it, play it. Go on, go on." After this, the flautist played a tune on the flute for some time. Dhirendra Shastri asked the people attending the religious discourse, "How many of you worship Lord Ram? Raise your hands. Yes! You people will be overjoyed today." ‘Grazing cows is a game; making monkeys dance is not’ Dhirendra Shastri had also referred to Lord Krishna herding cows and lifting a mountain. He had said, "People will say that our God herds cows. Anyone can herd cows. Herding cows is a game too; making monkeys dance is not." He then referred to Lord Krishna lifting Govardhan Hill. He had said, "You will say that our God can lift a mountain. Is that such a big deal? A disciple of our God flew away with an entire mountain." He was referring to Hanuman, a devotee of Lord Ram. Anger among Mathura's saints: read who said what- Dinesh Falahaari said- Even Ravana's arrogance did not last Dinesh Falahaari Maharaj, the petitioner in the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi temple-mosque case in Mathura, expressed his displeasure over Dhirendra Shastri's remarks. He said that Ram is Brahman and Shri Krishna is Yogeshwar. Our Krishna Kanhaiya is loved by the people of Braj. It is inappropriate to make remarks about him. Whether it is Dhirendra Shastri or anyone else, the people of Braj will not forgive him. Even Ravana's arrogance did not last, so who are you? Sadhvi says: Krishna is beloved by every resident of Braj Sadhvi Indulekha said that Shri Krishna is our revered deity. Dhirendra Shastri's remarks will not be tolerated at all. Krishna is beloved by every resident of Braj. Therefore, Dhirendra Shastri should apologise for his remarks. "Bageshwar Sarkar must apologise, or we will not remain silent" Pandit Rajesh Pathak said that no objectionable remarks about Shri Krishna could be tolerated, even in jest. History bears witness that whenever a sadhu, saint or storyteller has made an inappropriate comment about Shri Krishna, the people of Braj have opposed it. Bageshwar Sarkar's remarks will also be strongly opposed. If he does not apologise, the people of Braj will not remain silent. 2 years ago, Pandit Pradeep Mishra made remarks and later rubbed his nose on the ground Earlier, storyteller Pandit Pradeep Mishra had made controversial remarks about Radha Rani in Omkareshwar on 9 June 2024. He had said, "Radha Rani is not among Lord Shri Krishna's 108 chief queens and 1,600 wives. Radha's husband's name was Anay Ghosh, her mother-in-law's name was Jatila and her sister-in-law's name was Kutila. Radhaji was married in Chhata." He had also said that Radhaji was not from Barsana but lived in Rawal. Her father had a court in Barsana, which she visited once a year. Saints and people from Braj had protested after a sermon by Pradeep Mishra went viral. The sharpest reaction came from Premanand Maharaj. He said, "What do you know about Ladli Ji? What do you know at all? If you had spoken after consuming the dust from a saint's feet, such words would never have come from your mouth." After the controversy escalated, Pradeep Mishra visited the Barsana temple on 29 June 2024. He apologised at the temple for his remarks about Radha Rani's birth and marriage, rubbing his nose on the floor and offering a full prostration.

stories.title: Azam Khan reaches SP office, says 'I am still alive':Targets Owaisi with beard remark; says he does not like Hyderabadi biryani
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan reached the party's district office in Rampur on Thursday, the second day after his release from prison. He said, "Whatever happened to me was extremely bad. What worse could happen now? All the buildings that have been constructed here should also be demolished by bringing in bulldozers." Regarding the allegations against him, Azam Khan said, "I am still alive." Azam also took a dig at AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi. He said, "Hyderabadi biryani" is not liked in our area. People here prefer eating "pulao" and mutton biryani. He is a barrister, not a "maulana". Merely growing a beard does not make someone a "maulana", just as growing a beard does not make someone a "sadhu". Referring to Owaisi's rally in Rampur, he said, "My house was just four steps away. There was a free telephone. You could have asked my wife about my well-being. You could have paid a visit. That was not a prayer; it was medicine for my enemies." Read Azam's five major statements 1- In our organisation, positions and words have their own dignity Azam said that positions and words have their own dignity and propriety in our organisation. Referring to SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, he said that Yadav had been a Member of Parliament five times. He is the Chief Minister's son and has himself served as Chief Minister. Therefore, positions and words are accorded full respect in our organisation. 2- Congress is no longer what it used to be On the Congress-Samajwadi Party alliance, Azam said, "This is not the old Congress. The leadership today is different." However, he also said, "If any agreement has been reached between the two parties, it is a good thing." 3- The CBI's credibility has deteriorated severely Azam Khan said, "All constitutional institutions should safeguard their own dignity. The CBI's credibility has deteriorated severely. The agency should protect its reputation, because it is bringing disgrace to the country around the world." 4- Last time, it was an 'election of loot and plunder' Azam said that nothing happened in the election; rather, it was entirely an "election of loot and plunder". "I am its biggest victim myself. When Rampur was looted for the first time, police officers chased people with country-made pistols. Bolts were fastened on the outside of houses, and the police and PAC were deployed in the lanes to prevent people from voting." If the INDIA bloc had united and taken this issue seriously at the time, the election results in Kundarki, Sambhal, Haryana and Bengal would not have turned out this way. He alleged that the alliance leaders had not taken the incident seriously enough. 5-My membership was terminated and elections were held within 15 days Azam said that several cases had been filed against him, one of which was a "hate speech" case. His Assembly membership was terminated in this case. New elections were announced within just 48 hours, after which the elections were held within a period of one week to 15 days. However, the decision on his appeal came 15 days after that. Azam gets relief from Supreme Court, will remain out of jail SP leader Azam Khan will remain out of jail. The Supreme Court granted him major relief on Thursday. The ED had filed a petition in the Supreme Court challenging the interim bail granted to him by the Allahabad High Court. The court dismissed the petition within five minutes of the hearing beginning. It said, "This is an interim order, so we do not want to interfere in it. The High Court's observations will have no bearing on the final verdict." In fact, the Allahabad High Court granted interim bail to Azam in the money-laundering case linked to the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust on 17 November. It said that the circumstances of the case showed that the action had been taken with malicious intent. Azam had been released from Dasna jail on Wednesday Azam was subsequently released from jail and reached Rampur at 10 p.m. on Wednesday night. On 31 October, the Enforcement Directorate arrested Azam just 40 minutes after he was released from Rampur jail. He had been lodged in Ghaziabad's Dasna jail ever since. Even before Azam reached home, a stream of supporters had gathered to meet him. The people present outside his residence said they had complete faith in the court. They hoped that Azam Khan would continue to receive relief in the future. Now read what Azam's supporters said Samajwadi Party leader Anuradha Chaudhary, who has contested the election from Swar-Tanda, said, "What greater happiness could there be than the Supreme Court dismissing the petition filed by the Enforcement Directorate regarding her bail? The people sitting in our country's institutions should think about the fact that they must not become anyone's slaves." 'We trusted the courts and will receive relief in the future too' Jeeshan Malik said, "We wholeheartedly thank the Supreme Court for its verdict. We had complete faith in the courts, and will continue to have it." Sulaiman said that he considered it a major relief for Azam Khan. "We had hoped that one day we would receive justice from the court, and today justice has been delivered to us." An elderly supporter said that the entire country was happy about Azam Khan's release and the Supreme Court's decision. Supporters have been enthusiastic since he returned home. Now, find out how the Supreme Court granted relief to Azam The judge reprimanded the ED, saying, "The sky would not fall." The Supreme Court had asked the High Court to decide the case expeditiously On 5 November, the Supreme Court sent Azam's petition to the Allahabad High Court and asked it to decide the matter of interim relief at the earliest. During the hearing, the High Court raised questions about the ED's arrest procedure. The bench of Justice Rajiv Gupta and Justice Devendra Singh said that the rules had not been followed when Azam was arrested at the prison gate. Azam was therefore ordered to be released on furnishing one personal bond and two sureties for the same amount. After coming out of jail, Azam said, "There will be a revolution, not an election" The Samajwadi Party leader was released from Dasna jail at 7 pm on Wednesday. As soon as he came out of the jail, he kissed his elder son Adeeb on the forehead. After reaching Rampur, Azam told the media, "There will be no election, but a revolution. There will be no change, but a surge." He said, "People will no longer fight in the name of religion or caste; the fight will instead be over issues. People like us were ready to die for the Constitution and the law, and we were, are and will remain ready. The ED officials should repair their image and reform themselves. They should neither ruin the country nor themselves." Taking a dig, Azam said, "If someone who gets chickens, buffaloes and goats stolen can be an ED accused and builds a university, then I pray that one such person is born in every street." "If the ED, CBI and IT had existed during the time of Madan Mohan Malaviya and Sir Syed Ahmad Khan, they too would have been in jail. I thank the judiciary. My belief has now grown stronger that the country is free, but the Constitution is imprisoned." His troubles may still increase in this case On 10 September, UP Vigilance registered a case against five people, including Azam, over irregularities in the sale of the State Haj Committee's land. The Vigilance investigation has confirmed that the land sale caused the committee a revenue loss of ₹2.08 crore in total. It is alleged that rules were ignored and the position was misused in the sale of the land to benefit a private firm. The government ordered an investigation into the matter on 3 May 2024. Azam has not yet been questioned in the case. Legal experts say Azam can be arrested in this case, but the Vigilance Department will need the government's permission to arrest a former minister, which it has not received yet. However, that possibility currently appears remote because the High Court has granted Azam bail. The ED's petition was also dismissed by the Supreme Court. Know the case in which the ED arrested Azam The ED's action is linked to the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University and the Jauhar Trust associated with it. The agency is investigating the alleged misuse of funds and materials meant for government construction work, the purchase of land and the source of funds used to build the university. According to the ED, an investigation was launched on the basis of 26 FIRs registered at the Azeem Nagar police station in Rampur. The agency alleged that funds and construction materials linked to government contracts were used to build the university campus. The investigation valued the construction of 59 buildings and the land acquired through 114 sale deeds at ₹499.09 crore. According to the agency, only ₹72.63 crore could be accounted for through legitimate sources. The remaining ₹426.46 crore was described as alleged proceeds of crime. On this basis, the ED provisionally attached university land and buildings worth approximately ₹426.46 crore on 28 October.

stories.title: Akhilesh says, 'Don't welcome me with bulldozers':Child crushed to death by JCB in Gorakhpur, CM Yogi to visit family
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav asked party workers not to welcome him with bulldozers in future. On Wednesday, the 14-year-old son of a BJP leader died after being hit by a JCB during the PDA rath yatra in Gorakhpur. Akhilesh said- "I would ask my Samajwadi colleagues not to welcome anyone with bulldozers in future. We are not competing with anyone. The truth is that a bulldozer has no brain; it is driven by the driver." On Thursday, Chief Minister Yogi attacked the Samajwadi Party over the incident. He said, "An innocent child was made a victim at the Samajwadi Party's road show. He had come to study. After all, what was his fault? The Samajwadi Party's road show was a display of mafia rule and hooliganism." The Chief Minister warned that those creating chaos and indulging in mafia activity on the roads would be wiped out. Yogi will also meet the victim's family today. The accident occurred near Jharkhandi Mor at around 2:30 p.m. on Wednesday. Student Aryavardhan was walking towards the crossroads to pick up his sister when he was hit and injured by a JCB. He was taken to hospital, where he died. An FIR has been registered at the AIIMS police station against 66 people, including the JCB driver and the organiser. Akhilesh says politics is being played over the accident Akhilesh Yadav wrote on X, "We are all deeply hurt by the death of the innocent child in the accident. We express our deepest condolences to the bereaved family. We have already asked our people to meet the family and provide them with all possible assistance." Those politicising this unfortunate incident should remember how they mistreated and threatened the grieving mother of the young man who died in the Lucknow fire. The public has seen through the pretence of those putting on a show of mourning. Video released, questions raised over CM's allegations Releasing a video, Akhilesh Yadav wrote on X, "It is clearly visible that there was neither a roadshow nor a rally at the site of the incident. Despite this, the Chief Minister is blaming others for the accident." He said that politicising the matter was also an injustice to the bereaved family. He demanded a probe into the incident at the highest level. Yogi says: Innocent boy was made a victim at SP roadshow CM Yogi targeted the Samajwadi Party over the incident during a programme on Thursday. He said, "The SP held a roadshow yesterday. They made a minor boy a victim of their roadshow. He was killed. He had come to study. After all, what fault was there of that innocent 12-13-year-old?" The CM said that before 2017, forest mafias, mining mafias and cattle mafias were active in the state. If you want to see what the mafia looks like, you should look at the Samajwadi Party's roadshow yesterday. They made an innocent person their victim. See the height of their shamelessness: they remained silent. There was not even a single word of sympathy. Yogi said that just as a dog's tail can never be straightened, these goons and mafias can never mend their ways. They will only be brought into line through the use of force. He also directed the administration to take strict action against those spreading anarchy. Rajbhar said-You went and got yourselves disgraced; did you create mayhem on the roads? Cabinet minister and Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party president Om Prakash Rajbhar targeted Akhilesh Yadav in a post on the social media platform X. He wrote, "My friend Akhilesh Yadav ji! Did you get yourself disgraced in Gorakhpur? Did you unleash mayhem on the roads? Amid this mayhem, your goons killed an innocent child in Gorakhpur." Rajbhar went on to write that a 13-year-old child had to lose his life because of his men who were jumping around on the road. "The bulldozer in your roadshow claimed Aryavardhan's life. It is true that not everyone can handle a bulldozer." He demanded a high-level inquiry into the matter and that those involved in the incident be charged with murder. Rajbhar also accused Akhilesh Yadav of not expressing grief or condolences after the incident. Sanjay Nishad enquired about the family's well-being over the phone Dr Sanjay Kumar Nishad, national president of the Nishad Party and a Cabinet Minister in Uttar Pradesh, also enquired about the victim's family over the phone. Expressing deep sorrow over the incident, he said, "The Nishad Party never engages in politics over dead bodies." Dr Sanjay directed the MLA to immediately meet the victim's family, offer condolences and provide all possible assistance. Now, here is how the accident happened... Student was hit by a JCB during a roadshow on Wednesday Aryavardhan, the son of BJP leader Omkar Singh, allegedly died after being hit by a JCB deployed to welcome Akhilesh Yadav during his PDA Rath Yatra in Gorakhpur on Wednesday. He was a Class 10 student at Kendriya Vidyalaya Nandanagar. His family said Aryavardhan was heading towards the crossroads at around 2:30 p.m. on Wednesday to pick up his sister. During this time, he was seriously injured after being hit by the JCB. He was taken to AIIMS, where doctors declared him dead. After the accident, his family members and BJP workers blocked the Gorakhpur-Deoria road at Jharkhandi Mor. The road remained blocked for around one and a half hours. The family had demanded action against the JCB driver and the organisers of the roadshow. On the basis of Omkar Singh's complaint, an FIR has been registered at the AIIMS police station against 66 people, including the JCB driver and Samajwadi Party leaders. Now learn about BJP leader Onkar Singh Onkar Singh is the district co-convenor of the BJP's Election Commission Liaison Department. He is originally from Rajdhani village in the Chauri Chaura area of Gorakhpur. His family currently lives in the Awas Vikas Colony in Jharkhandi. Onkar Singh's grandfather, Shiv Sampat Singh Shrineth, was also involved in politics. His family included his wife, Archana, daughter Samriddhi and two sons, Aryavardhan and Kirtiwardhan. His elder son, Aryavardhan, died in the accident on Wednesday. DM assures action DM Deepak Meena said that the family's demands had been taken seriously. Action would be taken in accordance with the rules. The concerned officials would also be given necessary instructions regarding the demand to install a speed breaker near Jharkhandi Gate. SSP Dr Kaustubh said that an FIR had been registered in connection with the accident. The roles of the JCB operator and the organiser are being investigated. Legal action will be taken against those found guilty based on the facts that emerge during the investigation.

stories.title: Posters projecting Raja Bhaiya as CM appear at Ram Katha:Dhirendra Shastri's Katha enters final day; Golden Baba arrives wearing 6 kg gold
stories.summary: The final day of Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri's Shri Ram Katha is being held today in Benti, Pratapgarh. Golden Baba has also arrived for the event. He is wearing around 6 kg 50 grams of gold jewellery. Hyderabad MLA T. Raja Singh also attended the event. He said, "In Hyderabad, Raja Bhaiya is called the gun-wielding Raja Bhaiya." Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Maurya, Finance Minister Suresh Khanna, MLA Aditi Singh and Rakesh Pratap Singh have also attended the event. So far, five helicopters have arrived at the Ram Katha today. Large numbers of people are gathering not only in Benti but also in the surrounding towns to listen to the Katha. A sound system has been installed in Manikpur town, around 15 kilometres from the venue. People are listening to the Katha there. A similar arrangement has been made in Kunda. A market with around 100 shops has been set up at the venue. Crowds of people are shopping at the stalls. Groups of young people were seen carrying posters and banners with political messages on the roads around the religious discourse tent. The posters called for Kunda MLA Raghuraj Pratap Singh, popularly known as Raja Bhaiya, to be made Uttar Pradesh chief minister and Yogi to be made prime minister. On Friday, Bageshwar Dham's Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri will hold his divine court at Raja Bhaiya's Benti Palace.

stories.title: 2 lakh small fish released into Ganga:Initiative to increase Chitala population; river ranching programme held at Sant Ravidas Ghat
stories.summary: Two lakh fish found a new home in the Ganga on Thursday as part of a river ranching programme held at Sant Ravidas Ghat to protect the river's biodiversity and increase the declining fish population. During the programme, one lakh Rajyameen Chitala and one lakh Indian major carp fingerlings were released into the Ganga. Efforts to increase the Chitala population The main objective of the Fisheries Department's initiative is to promote the conservation and propagation of Chitala fish in the Ganga. According to department Deputy Director Suresh Kumar, efforts are being made through river ranching to increase the fish population in the river and strengthen the aquatic ecosystem. A larger fish population will strengthen the food chain The chitala fish is an important part of the Ganga's aquatic ecosystem. Its increasing numbers are expected to strengthen the river's natural food chain and biodiversity. The release of Indian major carp fingerlings will also boost fishery resources. This could benefit the livelihoods of fishermen and fish farmers in the future. The chital fish's unique appearance: a distinct identity shaped by its knife-like body The chitala fish is a highly attractive and distinctive freshwater fish. It is also known as the Indian knifefish or featherback. It has been granted the status of Uttar Pradesh's state fish. Its body is long, broad and flattened on both sides, giving it the appearance of a knife blade. A hump-like protrusion behind its head is its distinctive feature. Its silver colour and dark spots on the body enhance its beauty. Its lower and tail fins are connected, enabling it to swim in both forward and backward directions. It can grow up to four feet long.

stories.title: Brij Bhushan lifts former rival Ramdev in his arms:Baba stops him from touching his feet, hugs him; Raja Bhaiya looks surprised
stories.summary: Former MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and Baba Ramdev, once arch-rivals, appeared in a completely different manner. The occasion was a katha by Baba Bageshwar held at Raja Bhaiya's Raj Bhavan in Pratapgarh. The two warmly greeted each other. Brij Bhushan smiled as soon as he saw Ramdev and bent down to touch his feet. Baba Ramdev held his hand, helped him up and embraced him with a laugh. Meanwhile, Brij Bhushan held Ramdev by the waist and lifted him up. Raja Bhaiya, who was standing nearby, was taken aback by the sight. Saints and police officers present at the venue burst out laughing. The incident took place on 17 November, and its video emerged on Thursday (19 November). The four-year dispute between Brij Bhushan and Ramdev was resolved on 23 September this year. In fact, Acharya Balkrishna, president of Patanjali Yogpeeth, had sent Brij Bhushan a ₹50 crore defamation notice for calling Patanjali ghee fake. Brij Bhushan had said he was ready to go to jail but would not seek bail. See the pictures- Brij Bhushan returned to the stage and listened to the discourse alongside Ramdev Baba Ramdev reached Kunda after the Shri Ram Katha organised in Gonda. Meanwhile, he came face to face with Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, who was returning from the event. After their meeting, Brij Bhushan was about to leave for Gonda, but at Ramdev's request, he returned to the stage. The two then sat together and listened to the discourse. Now, here is what the dispute between the two was about 1. 2022: Dispute began after Patanjali ghee was called fake In November-December 2022, Brij Bhushan called Patanjali's desi ghee fake and advised people to keep cows and buffaloes at home. He also announced a campaign against adulteration. Acharya Balkrishna objected to this, sent him a legal notice and asked him to apologise. 2. 2025: Brij Bhushan questioned accountability after the sample failed On 27 November 2025, the Pithoragarh court imposed a fine of ₹1.40 lakh on the company and the sellers after a sample of Patanjali ghee failed in a 2020 case. Brij Bhushan questioned why a report that should have been issued within 2-4 hours came four years later, asking who would be held responsible for those who fell ill after consuming the ghee in the meantime. 3. September: Patanjali files ₹50 crore defamation case On 21 August, Brij Bhushan commented on Ramdev's Swadeshi movement, bringing the controversy back into the spotlight. Patanjali Foods filed a ₹50 crore defamation case against Brij Bhushan, accusing him of tarnishing the company's image. The case was heard in the Madhya Pradesh High Court on 15 September. Brij Bhushan said he was ready to go to prison if convicted but would not seek bail. 4. 23 September: Four-year-old dispute resolved after meeting Amid the legal battle, the two met on 23 September and ended the dispute. Ramdev said Brij Bhushan's misunderstandings had been cleared up and that he did not want to pursue the matter further. Brij Bhushan also said, "We have always respected saints and Sanatan, and we also respect the work you do for the country."

stories.title: 68,500 teacher recruitment candidates protest outside RLD office:Sweep premises with brooms in Lucknow to register protest; police lift and remove demonstrators
stories.summary: On Thursday, 68,500 teacher recruitment candidates staged a protest outside the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) office in Hazratganj. The candidates symbolically protested by sweeping outside the office and raised slogans. Police who arrived to remove the protesters forcibly picked them up and removed them from the site. See two pictures of the protest... Symbolic protest by sweeping the ground The candidates said the demonstration was organised under the "Dastak Do Abhiyan" and "Gorilla Gherao" campaigns. They said they had been fighting for a long time for their demand for appointments, but no one was listening to them. In protest, they tried to draw the government's and the party's attention by sweeping outside the RLD office. Demand to convey their concerns to the Centre through Jayant Chaudhary The protesters said that RLD chief Jayant Chaudhary is part of the central government. Therefore, he should convey the candidates' demands to the central government so that the issue of the recruitment of 68,500 teachers can be resolved. The candidates said they had already raised their demands with several political parties and leaders, but no solution had been found so far. Police forcibly removed them Police arrived at the site as the protest outside the office intensified. The police took action to remove the candidates. During this, the protesters were forcibly picked up and taken away. The candidates said their agitation would continue until their demand for appointment was met.

stories.title: Rohini alleges Chandrashekhar paid ₹5 crore for her murder:Claims cars follow her in UP; announces show of strength in Lucknow on November 26
stories.summary: Rohini Ghawari, former girlfriend of Azad Samaj Party chief and Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad, has said that her life is under threat. In a post on the social media platform X, she claimed that Chandrashekhar had paid a shooter ₹5 crore to have her killed. Rohini alleged that wherever she goes in Uttar Pradesh, some vehicles follow her. She also accused Chandrashekhar's supporters of misbehaving with her in Aligarh. In her post, Rohini said that the matter had now gone too far. Some people from the Meerut region met her and warned her about the threat. They said the conversation could not be held over the phone, so they met her in person and advised her to remain alert. Targeting the administration, she also said that honest people are not provided security, while brokers are given protection. Rohini said her family members were very worried. She said Chandrashekhar would be responsible if anything happened to her. She said the matter was being investigated and that the truth would soon come before the entire country. Court hearing on 26 November; verdict on Rohini's claim awaited Rohini Ghawari has filed a petition against Chandrashekhar in Delhi's Rouse Avenue Court under provisions including rape and other charges. The matter was scheduled for a hearing on 16 November, but the next date was fixed for 26 November due to a holiday. Rohini claims that she presented sufficient evidence in court and hopes the verdict will go against Chandrashekhar. She said an FIR would be registered against him and that he would have to go to prison. However, the court verdict is still awaited. Earlier, Rohini had announced that if Chandrashekhar contests the Hastinapur Assembly seat, she will contest against him. Two major events in Lucknow on 26 November Chandrashekhar Azad and AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi will hold a joint rally at Ramabai Ambedkar Maidan in Lucknow on 26 November. The two parties have formed the Social Change Front to contest all 403 Assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh. The rally aims to draw a crowd of more than five lakh people. Rohini Ghavari will also arrive in Lucknow on the same day. She will attend a Valmiki community conference at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan as the chief guest. According to Rohini, around five thousand people will attend the event, which will be held on Constitution Day. The event will call for the implementation of sub-categorisation within Dalit reservation, or reservation within reservation. Separate reservation for the Valmiki community and demand for 10 tickets from every party Rohini said the Jatav community had received the greatest benefit from Dalit reservation, while the Pasi, Sonkar and Valmiki communities remained relatively deprived. She said there was therefore a need to sub-categorise reservation and secure these communities their rights. He said that a resolution would be passed at the conference demanding that all political parties give the Valmiki community at least 10 Assembly tickets each. Several members of the community, including Ram Singh Valmiki and Ramesh Valmiki, are also expected to attend the programme.

stories.title: 14,929 candidates appear for Assistant Professor exam at 18 centres:623 teachers on duty across both shifts; first shift concludes
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission's Assistant Professor Selection Examination-2026 is being conducted at 18 examination centres in Varanasi. The first shift has ended, and candidates have begun arriving at the centre for the second shift. A total of 14,929 candidates will take the examination in both shifts on 19 November. The examination will be held from 9:30 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. and from 2:30 p.m. to 4:30 p.m. One teacher will be assigned for every 24 candidates in the examination. A total of 293 teachers in the first shift and 330 in the second shift will be responsible for invigilation. In all, 623 teacher duties will be assigned across both shifts. The examination is being conducted over two days, 19 and 20 November. A total of 31,467 candidates will appear on both days. 7,016 candidates in first shift, 7,913 in second A total of 7,016 candidates will take the examination in the first shift on 19 November. For this, 293 teachers will be assigned duty. Meanwhile, 7,913 candidates will appear in the second shift. 18 centres set up from Cantonment to Maidagin Centres have been set up in different parts of the city for the examination. These include Bharatiya Shiksha Mandir Inter College, Besant Theosophical Higher Secondary School, Shri Ramakrishna Vidya Mandir Inter College, RP Rastogi Inter College, AO Muslim Inter College, PM Shri Government Queens Inter College, CM Anglo-Bengali College, Harishchandra Intermediate College and Uday Pratap Inter College. The centres are located in different areas, including Cantonment, Englishia Line, Sigra, Lahurabir, Bhelupur, Maidagin and Bhojubeer. The examination will be held in two shifts The examination will be held on 19 and 20 November. It will be conducted in two shifts on both days. The first shift will run from 9:30 a.m. to 11:30 a.m., and the second from 2:30 p.m. to 4:30 p.m. Today, 19 November, is the first day of the examination.

stories.summary: A commotion broke out in Sambhal on Thursday during the 'Sanatan Padyatra'. The sants, who were taking out the procession without permission, broke through the barricades and pushed past the police personnel. Officials are trying to reason with them, but the saints are adamant about proceeding towards the Shahi Jama Masjid. After nearly two hours of efforts, the saints relented and agreed to stop the march. On 19 November 2024, Rishiraj Giri, the mahant of Kaila Devi Dham, filed a petition in court claiming that the Jama Masjid was the ancient 'Harihar Temple'. To mark two years since this, the mahant took out the march. The organisers claimed that more than 10,000 saints and devotees took part in it. They are demanding that the Harihar Temple be freed. stories.title: IPS officer Jasvir Singh reinstated after 8 years:Had been suspended since 2019 for questioning police during an interview
stories.summary: Senior 1992-batch Uttar Pradesh IPS officer Jasvir Singh has been reinstated after nearly eight years. Jasvir Singh, an ADG-rank officer, had been suspended since 14 February 2019. His prolonged suspension remained a topic of discussion within the police department and administrative circles. He has now been reinstated after the necessary procedures were completed at the government level. Why was he suspended and what was the reason? In January 2019, Jasvir Singh was posted as ADG (Rules and Manuals). During this period, he gave an interview to an English news portal. In it, he made several remarks about the way the police functioned, the encounter policy and the posting of officers. After the interview came to light, the government deemed it a violation of the All India Services (Conduct) Rules. He was subsequently served a notice and asked to respond. According to the government order, when he was asked to respond in the matter, he did not report for duty from 4 February 2019 without the permission of any competent authority or prior notice. He was suspended on 14 February 2019 for violating service rules and remaining absent from duty without permission. Jasveer Singh is from Punjab According to the official civil list of the Uttar Pradesh Police, Jasveer Singh is originally from Hoshiarpur district in Punjab. He was born on 15 January 1968. His father's name is Arjan Singh. He studied for a BE in civil engineering in Punjab. He then passed the UPSC examination and became an IPS officer of the 1992 batch. He was allotted the Uttar Pradesh cadre and joined the police service on 5 September 1993. He does not attract much attention in his personal life. He is also very interested in music. Jasveer has held several senior posts in Uttar Pradesh Over a career spanning more than three decades, Jasveer Singh has served as police chief in several key districts of Uttar Pradesh and held senior positions at the police headquarters. Why did the suspension last for 8 years? Under the All India Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1969, an IPS officer can initially be suspended for 60 days. After that, a review committee headed by the chief secretary reviews the suspension every three months. If the suspension is to continue for more than six months, the state government must inform the Union Ministry of Home Affairs or the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT). Approval must also be obtained as required under the rules. According to experts in police and administrative matters, the All India Services rules do not prescribe a fixed maximum period for suspension. However, it is considered highly unusual for an officer of the ADG rank to remain suspended for seven to eight years. During the suspension, the officer is paid a subsistence allowance. In the initial months, this amounts to 50% of the basic salary. If the investigation is prolonged, it can be increased to 75%. How was he reinstated after eight years? After his suspension, a departmental inquiry against Jasveer Singh continued. During this period, proposals related to his departmental inquiry were also sent to the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC). Meanwhile, Jasveer Singh wrote to the Home Department and the UPSC, demanding that his case be investigated by another state. He also filed an application with the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) over his prolonged suspension and matters related to his service. As part of the administrative process, all aspects of the case were considered during the departmental inquiry and review committee meetings. After considerable time had passed during the inquiry, it was decided, in accordance with the rules, to end his suspension and reinstate him. All eyes are now on which department he will be assigned to after his reinstatement.

stories.title: 12-year-old student dies after falling from hostel building:Bihar girl falls from fourth floor of Varanasi boarding school at 5 am
stories.summary: A 12-year-old student died after falling from the fourth floor of a hostel at a boarding school in Varanasi on Thursday morning. The deceased, identified as Sneha Mishra, was a resident of Bihar. The incident took place at around 5 am at the school in Samneghat, triggering panic on the campus. Following the incident, Lanka police and senior officials reached the spot and began an investigation. The circumstances that led to the girl's fall are not yet clear. Was staying with two other students According to police, they received information that a girl had fallen from the rooftop of Gyan Deep Academy and Hostel, located in Lane No. 3 of Shivprasad Gupta Colony. Lanka police took her to the trauma centre, where doctors declared her dead. Police have informed the girl's father, Tarkeshwar Mishra. Police said Sneha was staying at the hostel with two other students. They have also questioned school manager Tribhuvan Singh and hostel warden Preeti Mishra. A forensic field unit was called to the spot for an investigation. ACP says CCTV footage is being examined ACP Bhelupur Gaurav Kumar said police reached the spot and began an investigation as soon as they received information about the incident. DCP Kashi Gaurav Baswal also inspected the scene. CCTV footage from cameras installed at the hostel is being examined to establish the circumstances leading to the incident.

stories.title: Boyfriend dies by suicide in Lucknow jail:Body found hanging from towel in bathroom; girlfriend had fallen from hotel's 10th floor
stories.summary: Avnish Jaiswal, alias Dev, the boyfriend accused in the Samreen murder case in Lucknow's Sushant Golf City, died by suicide by hanging himself in jail on Thursday. His body was found hanging in the jail bathroom with the help of a noose made from a towel. As soon as the incident came to light, Jail Superintendent Ritwik Priyadarshi and a police team reached the spot. The officials inspected the scene and launched an investigation. See 3 pictures... Sameen died after falling from the hotel's 10th floor In fact, 24-year-old Sameen died after falling from the 10th floor of Hotel Celestial Manoyr on 14 October. On the day of the incident, she was staying at the hotel with her boyfriend, Avneesh Jaiswal. The two checked into the hotel at around 12 p.m. At around 6:30 p.m., Sameen fell from the hotel's 10th floor. Avneesh fled the scene after her death. Surrendered in court two days later Avnish, who was accused in the case involving Sameen's death, had been absconding since the incident. Two days after the incident, he surrendered in court and was subsequently sent to jail. On Thursday, his body was found hanging from a noose in the jail bathroom. The jail administration and police are currently investigating the incident.

stories.title: Azam to remain out of jail, setback for ED:Supreme Court dismisses petition; said yesterday, 'The sky will not fall'
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan will remain out of jail. The Supreme Court gave him major relief on Thursday. The Enforcement Directorate had petitioned the Supreme Court against the interim bail granted to him by the Allahabad High Court. The court dismissed the petition within five minutes of the hearing beginning. It said, "This is an interim order, so we do not want to interfere in it." The Allahabad High Court's observation "will have no bearing on the verdict". On 17 November, the Allahabad High Court had granted Azam Khan interim bail in the money-laundering case linked to the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust. It said the circumstances of the case indicated that the action had been taken with ulterior motives. Azam Khan was subsequently released from jail and reached Rampur at around 10 p.m. on Wednesday night. On 31 October, the Enforcement Directorate arrested him just 40 minutes after he was released from Rampur jail. He had been lodged in Ghaziabad's Dasna jail since then. The judge reprimanded the ED when it approached the Supreme Court on Wednesday against Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan's interim bail. The judge said, "What is the hurry? Let Azam remain on bail; the sky will not fall." The ED was seeking an immediate hearing in the case. The ED's lawyer, ASG S. V. Raju, told the court that the Allahabad High Court had passed the order in haste. He said, "We did not even get enough time to file a complete response. It was more like a final order than an interim one. Therefore, this matter should be heard immediately." When the bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said the matter would be heard later, ASG Raju said, "Please stay his release until then, otherwise he will come out of jail." The bench immediately rejected the request. High Court had questioned the arrest procedure On 5 November, the Supreme Court sent Azam Khan's petition to the Allahabad High Court and asked it to decide the matter of interim relief promptly. The case was subsequently heard by a bench of Justice Rajiv Gupta and Justice Devendra Singh in the High Court. The High Court said that the prescribed legal procedure was not followed during Azam Khan's arrest at the gate of Rampur Jail on 31 October. It granted him interim bail on the condition that he furnish a personal bond and two sureties of the same amount. Five key points from the High Court's ruling 1. Questions raised over arrest at the jail gate: According to the High Court, Azam Khan was arrested right at the jail gate at 7:10 p.m. on 31 October after being granted bail in the PAN card case. The court termed the action prima facie mala fide. 2. Grounds for arrest not provided in writing: The court said that the grounds for Azam Khan's arrest were not communicated to him in writing at the time of his arrest. The place, date and time were also left blank in the arrest memo. 3. Documents were not sent in the message to his sister: a WhatsApp message was sent to Azam Khan's sister at 9:10 p.m. on 31 October, followed by an email at 9:19 p.m. According to the High Court, documents related to the grounds of arrest were not sent with either message. 4. No evidence of videography of the arrest: The ED had claimed that the arrest was videographed, but the High Court said the agency had not produced any video or photograph. The remand application also made no mention of videography. 5. Interim bail until the next hearing: The High Court granted Azam Khan interim bail on the condition that he furnish a personal bond and two sureties for the same amount. The ED was given one week to respond, while Azam Khan was given 10 days to file his response. The next hearing in the case is scheduled for 10 December. Find out which case the ED arrested Azam in ED has attached property worth ₹426 crore The ED's action is linked to Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University and the Jauhar Trust associated with it. The agency is investigating the alleged misuse of funds and materials meant for government construction works, the purchase of land and the source of the funds used in the construction of the university. According to the ED, the investigation was launched on the basis of 26 FIRs registered at the Azeem Nagar police station in Rampur. The agency alleged that funds and construction materials linked to government contracts were used to build the university campus. An investigation valued the construction of 59 buildings and the land acquired through 114 sale deeds at ₹499.09 crore. According to the agency, only ₹72.63 crore could be accounted for from legitimate sources. The remaining ₹426.46 crore was described as alleged proceeds of crime. On this basis, the ED had provisionally attached university land and buildings worth around ₹426.46 crore on 28 October. Azam came out of jail after 11 months, arrested 15 minutes later On 29 October, the Allahabad High Court suspended the 10-year sentences of Azam Khan and his son, Abdullah Azam, in two PAN card cases and granted bail to both. They were subsequently released from Rampur Jail. Azam Khan walked out of jail at around 7 p.m. on 31 October, after 11 months in custody. Around 15 minutes later, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) arrested him in a money-laundering case and took him to Ghaziabad. The ED's special PMLA court first remanded him to judicial custody until 14 November and then extended it until 26 November. Azam's lawyers had described the action as political vendetta Senior advocates Kapil Sibal and Imran Ullah represented Azam Khan. They argued that action had been taken in a 2019 case nearly seven years later. New cases were being filed one after another to keep Azam Khan in jail. The lawyers also said that the arrest procedure and remand order were erroneous. Meanwhile, the ED's counsel, ASG SV Raju and Zoheb Hossain, argued that the officials had tried to hand over the documents to Azam Khan outside the jail, but he had refused to accept them. A panchnama was then prepared in this regard. The next day, Azam Khan accepted the documents in court while registering his objection. Wife says - Had faith in Allah Sweets are being distributed at Azam Khan's residence in Rampur after he was granted interim bail. His wife, Tanzim Fatima, said she had faith in Allah. Some forces did not want Azam Khan to remain out of jail. There is an atmosphere of happiness among the family and supporters after he was granted bail. Azam Khan was sent to Rampur jail on 17 November 2025 in the PAN card case. The Supreme Court's decision on the ED's petition challenging his interim bail will now be significant. Could Azam's release create problems for the BJP? Read on ... Azam Khan has been sentenced to 10 years in the PAN card case, while Abdullah Azam has been sentenced in the PAN card and fake birth certificate cases. Both have also been disqualified as members of the Legislative Assembly. Under Section 8(3) of the Representation of the People Act, a person sentenced to two years or more cannot contest elections for six years after completing the sentence. Bail alone does not end this disqualification. A stay on the sentence from a higher court is necessary to contest an election. However, Azam's release before the 2027 Assembly elections could prove significant for the Samajwadi Party. Understand its political impact in 3 points... 1. He will become the SP's star campaigner Despite being unable to contest the election, Azam Khan can campaign for the SP. His speeches are expected to boost the morale of party workers in Muslim-majority constituencies in western Uttar Pradesh. 2. Taking on the Owaisi challenge Azam's return could help the SP prevent the division of Muslim votes. The party will have its old and outspoken face to take on the challenge posed by Owaisi's AIMIM. 3. The organisation will be strengthened in western Uttar Pradesh Azam has influence in western Uttar Pradesh, including the Rampur and Moradabad divisions. His return could help fill the vacuum in the Samajwadi Party's minority leadership created by his absence. Akhilesh may give him responsibility for coordinating the party's seats in western Uttar Pradesh. What will be the BJP's next move? After Azam's release, the BJP may target the Samajwadi Party on issues of law and order and corruption. Senior journalist Jaigam Murtaza said Azam's release could reactivate the Samajwadi Party's local organisation in Rampur and neighbouring districts. This could affect the political contest in the 2027 election.

stories.title: Kashi to host first-ever drone show at Dev Deepawali:Tourists can watch laser show from Ganga's opposite bank; 10 lakh visitors expected
stories.summary: Varanasi is gearing up for Dev Deepawali, which will be celebrated on November 24 on the occasion of Kartik Purnima. More than 10 lakh devotees and tourists are expected to visit the city this year. Around 11 lakh earthen lamps will illuminate the ghats along the Ganga. Ganga Aarti, a laser show, fireworks and a drone show for the first time will be among the major attractions. The district administration, police and Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham have made extensive arrangements for the event. Special Ganga Aarti at eight major ghats Special Ganga Aarti will be organised at eight prominent ghats: Namo Ghat, Gayghat, Panchganga Ghat, Dashashwamedh Ghat, Sheetla Ghat, Kedar Ghat, Tulsi Ghat and Assi Ghat. The rituals will feature Vedic chants, conch-shell blowing and large ceremonial lamps as devotees offer prayers to the River Ganga. 11 lakh lamps to illuminate Varanasi's ghats District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar said a large number of people are expected to visit Varanasi this year, as in previous years. Devotees will take a holy dip in the Ganga in the morning and participate in the lighting of lamps, Ganga Aarti and cultural programmes at the ghats in the evening. Around 11 lakh lamps will be lit across the ghats, while Ganga Aarti will also be performed at all the ghats. A laser show will be organised at Chet Singh Fort. He said organisers are also planning to include a drone show alongside fireworks for the first time. The DM said the celebrations would highlight Kashi's cultural heritage, religious significance and traditions. Security arrangements have been strengthened in view of the expected crowds. As a large number of boats and barges operate on the Ganga, the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and water police will be deployed. Fire safety arrangements have also been made to prevent incidents at the ghats, where lakhs of lamps will be lit. 4,000 police personnel to be deployed for over 10 lakh visitors Police Commissioner Mohit Agarwal said more than 10 lakh people are expected to reach Varanasi for Dev Deepawali. A comprehensive security plan has been prepared, with sector-based and zonal arrangements. Around 25 IPS officers, 50 Provincial Police Service (PPS) officers and nearly 4,000 police personnel will be deployed during the celebrations. He said people usually watch Dev Deepawali from the permanent ghats on the Varanasi side before taking boats or barges onto the river. This year, arrangements are also being made on the Ramnagar and Chandauli sides. The riverbank on the opposite side is being levelled, and designated enclosures are being created for visitors to stand and watch the celebrations. According to the Police Commissioner, four major attractions will feature this year: the laser show, fireworks, drone show and Ganga Aarti. The drone show will be organised in the middle of the Ganga for the first time, allowing people on both banks to watch it. He added that Chet Singh Fort is more clearly visible from the Ramnagar side. Visitors watching from there will get a better view of the programme. Floating lane system for boats, life jackets mandatory A floating lane system is being introduced this year to regulate boat and barge movement on the Ganga and prevent accidents. Police Commissioner Mohit Agarwal said separate lanes would be created in the river, with a divider in the middle, similar to a road. Boats will move in one direction on one side and return from the other. He made it clear that wearing life jackets would be compulsory for everyone travelling by boat. Action will be taken against those who violate the rule. Overloading of boats will not be allowed. Police personnel equipped with breath analysers will also be deployed, and action will be taken against boat operators found navigating under the influence of alcohol. Traffic plan aims to limit walking distance to 1 km A traffic management plan has also been prepared to handle the large crowds expected during Dev Deepawali. The Police Commissioner said adequate parking arrangements had been made, with an effort to ensure that visitors do not have to walk more than one kilometre to reach the event venues. People from neighbouring districts can also visit Varanasi in their private cars without any restrictions. However, the entry of goods vehicles into the city will remain prohibited on Dev Deepawali. Special arrangements at Kashi Vishwanath Dham Satyam Mishra, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple, said preparations at the temple complex had been completed. Duties have been assigned to the entire team, while cleaning and decoration work has begun. General facilities for devotees near the ghat area have also been expanded. End-to-end barricading has been installed inside the Dham to manage crowds and ensure smooth movement. Wheelchairs, drinking water and medical facilities will be available for senior citizens and specially-abled devotees. Lamps will also be lit inside the temple complex, and preparations for fireworks have been completed. The CEO said Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham receives an average of around 1.5 lakh devotees daily on normal days, while the number exceeds two lakh on weekends. Between two lakh and 2.5 lakh devotees are expected to visit the Dham on Dev Deepawali.

stories.title: Varanasi woman secures 5th rank in Uttarakhand PCS-J:Appeared for mains with fever and diarrhoea; aims to clear court backlog
stories.summary: "The day I was scheduled to travel by train for the mains examination, I developed a high fever and suffered from diarrhoea. Despite my condition, I appeared for the Uttarakhand PCS-J mains. I cleared the examination and secured fifth rank." These are the words of Shreya Singh, a resident of Bajardeeha in Varanasi, who secured fifth rank in the Uttarakhand PCS-J examination despite appearing for the mains while suffering from fever and diarrhoea and made her family and the city proud with her achievement. She is currently teaching first-year students at the Faculty of Law, Banaras Hindu University (BHU). Shreya credits her success to God, her spiritual guru, parents and teachers. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, she said she had reached the interview stage in Rajasthan and appeared for judicial service examinations in Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, but could not secure a selection. At several points, she considered giving up her preparation. Read the report... Father encouraged her to apply despite just four vacancies Shreya completed her graduation in 2020 and then began preparing for competitive examinations. During this period, she also qualified for NET-JRF. She completed her LLM from BHU in 2021 and subsequently started appearing for judicial and administrative service examinations in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh. She reached the interview stage in Rajasthan but did not make it to the final selection. Repeated setbacks left her disappointed, and she sometimes thought of giving up. However, she decided to keep trying. Shreya said she had never applied for the Uttarakhand PCS-J examination before. There were only four vacancies for the general category, so she was reluctant to apply. "I wondered what difference applying would make when there were so few seats. But my father insisted that I should give it a try. I was initially reluctant, but eventually filled out the form at his insistence. Today, I have secured fifth rank in the same examination," she said. Chose the eagle over the peacock in interview Shreya recalled a question from her interview that she still remembers. A psychologist asked her to choose between a peacock and an eagle. "I was slightly surprised by the question, but I chose the eagle. When asked why, I explained that an eagle is known for its focus on its target, while a peacock is known for its beauty. I want to remain focused on my work and goals," she said. Her answer was appreciated by the interview panel. Wants to reduce the burden of pending court cases Shreya said her aim in joining the judicial services is not simply to secure a position. She wants to contribute towards reducing the backlog of cases in the judiciary. "Cases in courts often take a long time to reach the hearing stage. Further delays only increase people's difficulties. I will try to contribute towards reducing this problem," she said. Parents did not put pressure on her to marry Shreya's mother, Maya Singh, said the family was delighted with her daughter's achievement. She recalled that Shreya was at BHU on the day the results were announced. That morning, she had told her family that her result was expected and asked them to share the good news with her. "We were hopeful that she would clear the examination because her papers had gone well. At around 3.30 pm, when we checked the result, tears came to our eyes. We first remembered our spiritual guru and then, with tears of joy, messaged Shreya that she had been selected," Maya Singh said. She added that people often asked the family when they planned to get their daughter married. "Our answer was always that we would not think about her marriage until she became financially independent. Now that she has been selected, we will consider it," she said. Father is a doctor, mother a meditation expert Shreya belongs to Badi Patiya in the Bajardeeha area of Bhelupur, Varanasi. Her father, Dr Ravindra Pratap Singh, is a retired Ayurvedic medical officer. Her mother, Maya Singh, is a zonal and centre coordinator with the Ram Chandra Mission. Her elder brother, Shashank Singh, works as a manager at the Jimmy Paul Tata Group after completing his BTech. Her other brother, Mayank Singh, holds an MBA degree and works as the head of department at LPCPS in Lucknow. Shreya said her family had always supported her throughout her journey. Despite being their only daughter, her parents never put pressure on her regarding either education or marriage. She credited her achievement to the support and blessings of her family, spiritual guru and teachers.

stories.title: Mother, two daughters burnt alive in house fire in Shamli:Husband and two sons escape unhurt; cylinder blast suspected
stories.summary: A woman and her two daughters were burnt alive after a fire broke out at their home in Shamli around midnight on Wednesday (18 Nov), while the entire family was asleep. A short circuit in the kitchen is suspected to have triggered a cylinder explosion, following which the fire engulfed the house within seconds. The blast caused the ceiling of a room to collapse, leaving the mother and her daughters with no chance to escape. Husband and two sons escape unhurt The woman's husband and their two sons, who were sleeping in an adjoining room, narrowly escaped. A CCTV camera installed at a neighbouring house captured the cylinder explosion. The husband and two sons woke up after hearing screams and rushed to the room. They tried to extinguish the fire but could not rescue the three as the flames had spread rapidly. Bodies recovered after two-hour rescue operation By the time the police and fire brigade reached the spot, all three had died. After a two-hour rescue operation, firefighters recovered the burnt bodies of the mother, Shahida (32), and her daughters, Adan (13) and Mahira (11), from beneath the collapsed roof debris. Their bodies had been reduced to skeletons. The incident took place in Babri police station limits, around 35 km from the district headquarters. See 2 pictures… Here is a step-by-step account of the incident According to police, Sajid (35) lives in Kaidi village with his wife, two daughters and two sons. Their house has two rooms, a kitchen and a hall. His wife, Shahida (32), and their daughters, Adan and Mahira, used to sleep in the room adjoining the kitchen. Sajid slept in the other room with his two sons. A hall and courtyard separate the two rooms and the kitchen. Around midnight on Wednesday, a fire broke out in the kitchen and spread to Shahida's room. As the flames engulfed their room, Shahida and her daughters began screaming for help. Hearing their cries, Sajid and his sons rushed towards the room, but the fire had already become intense. They immediately alerted the police. Police fail to douse fire, fire brigade brings blaze under control Station House Officer Rajendra Kumar said Babri police reached the spot after receiving information through Dial-112. The fire brigade was also alerted. Police personnel, along with local residents, tried to extinguish the fire but failed because of the intensity of the flames. The fire brigade team later arrived and brought the blaze under control. By then, the bodies had been completely burnt. According to the SHO, preliminary investigations suggest that a cylinder explosion may have caused the fire. However, the exact cause will be established only after a detailed investigation.

stories.summary: Several areas of Gorakhpur will face a five-hour power cut on Thursday due to ongoing road widening work and the shifting of electricity lines. Power supply will remain suspended from 11 am to 4 pm in areas served by five electricity substations across the city. The affected areas include localities connected to the 11 kV Shiv Nagar and Ramjanki Nagar feeders of the Raptinagar Old Substation. Electricity supply will also be disrupted in areas covered by the 11 kV Rail Vihar and Karim Nagar feeders of the Raptinagar New Substation. Similarly, the following areas will face power cuts: Power supply to resume after 4 pm Electricity department officials said power supply would be restored in all affected areas after 4 pm, once the work is completed. The department has advised residents to store water in advance and complete essential electricity-related work before the scheduled shutdown to avoid inconvenience.

stories.title: 5 friends killed in road accident:6 went out for tea on 2 bikes; car hit them amid dense fog, 2 critically injured
stories.summary: Five friends were killed and two others seriously injured in a road accident in Balrampur. The six friends had gone out for tea on two motorcycles at around 11 pm on Wednesday when a four-wheeler hit both bikes. The collision was so severe that both motorcycles were badly damaged. All the riders were thrown 5-10 feet away. Bodies were scattered across the road as people screamed for help. The driver sped away after the collision. Police reached the spot after receiving information and took all the injured to hospital, where doctors declared five of them dead. The two injured were referred to a higher medical centre. The accident took place around 11 pm in Aksibarhara village under the Utraula police station area, about 40 km from the district headquarters. The deceased have been identified as Guufran (18), Salim (21), Rahmat (30), Taufiq (19) and Mohammad Farooq (20). All were residents of Balrampur. According to police, dense fog caused the accident. See pictures of the accident... Six friends went out for tea; accident occurred on the way SP Martand Prakash Singh said the initial investigation revealed that all the youths were residents of Chhapar Talwa, Gaurivandeeh village. Three people were travelling on each motorcycle. They decided to go out for tea at around 11 pm and headed towards Utraula market. Visibility was extremely low due to dense fog on the Balrampur-Utraula road. Some pedestrians suddenly came in front of one motorcycle. While trying to avoid them, the rider lost control and the bike skidded. Their friends on the second motorcycle, who were following them, stopped to help the fallen riders. Just then, a speeding four-wheeler arrived and ran over them before fleeing the scene. The bodies have been sent for post-mortem examination, and the families have been informed. The injured are undergoing treatment. Police are examining CCTV footage and trying to identify the vehicle.

stories.title: CM to launch UP's first forestry university today:₹491-crore project across 124 acres to add fifth university to Gorakhpur's educational institutions
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will lay the foundation stone for Uttar Pradesh's first Forestry and Horticulture University on Thursday (November 19) at Bhariwaisi in the Campierganj tehsil of Gorakhpur. The university will be built across around 124 acres at an estimated cost of ₹491 crore. With this project, Gorakhpur will have five universities, including two institutions dedicated to specialised fields. The district already has Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, Madan Mohan Malaviya University of Technology, Mahayogi Gorakhnath University and the state's first Mahayogi Guru Gorakhnath AYUSH University. The AYUSH University and the proposed Forestry and Horticulture University are unique institutions in the state because of their specialised courses and areas of study. The new university is expected to strengthen Gorakhpur's position as an educational hub while promoting environmental conservation and sustainable development. University to offer courses in forestry and wildlife conservation According to Gorakhpur Divisional Forest Officer Shubham Singh, the university will offer undergraduate (BSc), postgraduate (MSc), PhD and diploma courses in several specialised subjects. These will include: The government has also proposed horizontal reservation for graduates of the university in recruitment to the Uttar Pradesh State Forest Service and Regional Forest Officer posts. Hostels for 895 students and 401 residential units According to District Magistrate Deepak Meena, around 50 hectares (123.55 acres) of land have been identified for the project. The campus will have modern facilities, including: The project aims to promote higher education, research and innovation in forestry, agroforestry, horticulture and environmental conservation. It is also expected to create career opportunities for students across Uttar Pradesh and other parts of North India. CM to inaugurate and lay foundation stones for 55 projects During his visit to Gorakhpur on Thursday, Yogi Adityanath will also inaugurate and lay foundation stones for 55 development projects worth more than ₹792 crore. These include 16 projects worth ₹621.05 crore for which foundation stones will be laid. The Chief Minister will also inaugurate 39 completed projects worth ₹171.13 crore. The ₹491-crore Forestry and Horticulture University is among the major projects for which the foundation stone will be laid. CM to hold public interaction in the evening Yogi Adityanath is scheduled to visit Gorakhpur for two days. After laying the university's foundation stone in the morning, he will attend a public interaction programme organised by the BJP at the Kachahari Club ground in the evening. The programme will be held for the Gorakhpur City Assembly constituency. Party workers are expected to attend, where the Chief Minister will listen to their concerns and address the gathering.

stories.title: Fog grips UP as temperatures fall below 10°C:Muzaffarnagar records lowest at 9.5°C; speed limits reduced on five expressways
stories.summary: Cold weather has intensified in Uttar Pradesh following snowfall in the hills. Dense fog is affecting several parts of the state during the early morning and night, reducing visibility to such an extent that vehicles cannot see beyond 10 metres in some areas. Due to poor visibility, speed limits have been reduced on several expressways to prevent road accidents. The restrictions apply to the Agra-Lucknow, Purvanchal, Bundelkhand, Gorakhpur Link and Ganga Expressways. In the past 24 hours, Muzaffarnagar recorded the lowest minimum temperature in the state at 9.5°C. Atul Kumar Singh, a meteorologist in Lucknow, said the impact of Cyclone Akvan, which has formed over the Bay of Bengal, is moving northwards from the southern parts of the country. Cloud movement, intense cold and fog are expected to increase after the next 24 hours. By how much have speed limits been reduced on the expressways in Uttar Pradesh? Take a look How will Cyclone Akvan affect Uttar Pradesh? According to meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh, the impact of Cyclone Akvan over the Bay of Bengal is gradually moving towards northern India. Cloud cover, cold conditions and fog are likely to intensify after the next 24 hours. Satellite images from the India Meteorological Department (IMD) indicate that the cyclone is still active over the sea, but its influence has reached the plains of Odisha and Jharkhand. The impact is expected to remain limited in western Uttar Pradesh due to westerly winds. However, increased moisture in the air could bring significant changes to weather conditions in the Purvanchal region over the coming days. Night-time cold intensifies in Uttar Pradesh, mercury drops to 9.5°C in Muzaffarnagar Daytime temperature in Uttar Pradesh approaches 30°C Speed limits reduced on five expressways To prevent road accidents during winter and dense fog, the Uttar Pradesh Traffic Police has reduced speed limits on five expressways. The restrictions will remain in force from November 15, 2026, to February 15, 2027, between 8 am and 8 pm every day. stories.summary: Statements have begun over the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Nishad Party national president Sanjay Nishad indirectly targeted his NDA ally and Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party president Om Prakash Rajbhar. He said, "The Ataraulia Assembly seat belongs to the Nishad Party. It belonged to us yesterday and will remain ours today." Sanjay Nishad said, "We are all NDA allies, but some people are labouring under a misunderstanding. They want to contest elections from just one seat, leaving the entire state aside. We will clear up their misunderstanding." After Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan took a dig at Hyderabadi biryani, the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen responded by distributing biryani in Etawah. Party leaders put up posters of Owaisi and distributed biryani packets to around 500 people. Azam Khan had taken a dig at Owaisi's rally in Rampur on 19 November. He had said that Hyderabadi biryani was not liked in our area. People here preferred eating pulao and mutton biryani. The Samajwadi Party and Congress will hold a meeting in New Delhi on 23 and 24 November to discuss the division of Assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh. For this, SP president Akhilesh Yadav has formed a four-member committee comprising national principal general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav, state president Shyam Lal Pal, MP Rajiv Rai and MP Iqra Hasan. From the Congress, Priyanka Gandhi, K.C. Venugopal, Uttar Pradesh state president Aradhana Mishra, Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam and working president Imran Masood will take part in the talks.

stories.title: Meat alcohol served at prayer meeting in Amethi:Children’s notebooks say, 'Jesus is the only God, come to him'
stories.summary: Six women and four men were served meat and alcohol at a prayer meeting in Amethi, Uttar Pradesh. Around 35 people attended the meeting, most of them women and children. The meeting was held at a house where religious conversion activities were allegedly taking place. Children's notebooks found there had the line, "Jesus is the only God; come to him." Police detained six women and four men in connection with the incident. The case took place under the Kamaruali police station area at around 3 pm on Sunday. Read the full story... They had come from three states to conduct the prayer meeting Mahant Gurubaksh Das of Baba Ganga Das Kuti said in his complaint, "I learned at around 1 p.m. on Sunday that a prayer meeting was being held at a house on Sindurwa Road. The house belongs to Rajkumar and his wife, Suryakala. People from Maharashtra, Uttarakhand, Odisha and Azamgarh were present at the spot." Feast of meat and alcohol served Mahant Gurubaksh Das said, "Those people were luring women from families belonging to the Scheduled Caste community and others and encouraging them to convert to Christianity." Bibles and promotional material related to Christianity were also found in the house. Shoes and slippers, food plates and disposable glasses were lying in the veranda of the house. Accused of carrying out religious conversions by offering inducements Pawan Tiwari of the RSS's Jagdishpur unit said that the police were informed after information about religious conversion activities was received. Such activities take place here every year between November and December. These people try to convert poor and needy people by offering them inducements. Children's notebooks carried the message: Come to Jesus Pawan said, "Religious conversions have been taking place continuously from village to village. We had busted a racket the last time as well, in which the principal here was also involved. This time, these people have come from Mumbai. It should be stopped completely. Some children's notebooks also carried religious messages. They said, 'God is only Jesus; come to Jesus.'" Meanwhile, Royal Rodrix, who had come from Mumbai for the prayer, denied the allegations of carrying out religious conversions. He said, "We had come only to pray and meet Suryakala." SP Sarvanan T. said: A Skoda car was recovered from the spot and a Bible from inside the house. The people detained are residents of Maharashtra, Uttarakhand, Azamgarh and Amethi, among other districts. The case is being investigated.
