stories.title: Bageshwar Baba's kathas increase in UP after Akhilesh's protest:Five lined up in 20 days, compared with two in 18 months; will Thakur influence backfire
stories.summary: Raghuraj Pratap Singh, popularly known as Raja Bhaiya, organised a Ram Katha in Kunda, Pratapgarh. Leaders from the Thakur community and influential political figures from eastern Uttar Pradesh shared the stage. Raja Bhaiya was projected as a face of Hindutva. The message was that Thakur leaders in UP had united under his leadership. The gathering of around 5 lakh people over the three-day event surprised everyone. The UP Assembly election is due to be announced in two months. Before that, 12 such religious discourses are scheduled to take place. Five of these will be held by Dhirendra Shastri, the head of Bageshwar Dham. This means he will be seen in different districts of UP for 20 of the next 40 days. It is well known that his discourses often feature strong views on Sanatan Dharma and Hindutva. There are now two kinds of discussions around these events. One view is that they are an attempt to shift election issues towards Hindutva and Sanatan Dharma. Another section believes that the prominence of one community at these events could backfire. What is the truth? We explain it in today's Sunday Big Story... Kunda in UP is identified with Raghuraj Pratap Singh, popularly known as Raja Bhaiya. However, the Ram Katha in Kunda suddenly made headlines across the country. Even more widely discussed was the show of organisational strength by Raja Bhaiya in arranging the event. The reason was that Dhirendra Shastri had compared Lord Ram and Lord Krishna last month, following which he faced opposition. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav went so far as to say, "He has hurt the sentiments of both the Yaduvanshis and the Raghuvanshis. He will not be allowed to enter either Braj or Awadh... His programmes should also be cancelled." The opposition to Dhirendra Shastri was seen as opposition to Sanatan Dharma. As a result, when the head of Bageshwar Dham, Dhirendra Shastri, delivered the Ram Katha from 17 to 19 November, lakhs of people attended every day. The tent, spread over 56,000 square feet, was packed with people, while twice as many were seated outside. The Katha was scheduled to take place from 2 pm to 6 pm every day, but it did not last the full four hours on any of the three days. This was because several prominent leaders from UP and other states kept arriving as guests. They were also given an opportunity to speak from the stage. Notably, more than half of the leaders who attended the Katha belonged to the Thakur community. From the stage, Raja Bhaiya was described as a prominent face of Sanatan Dharma and Hindutva. His supporters also projected him as the Chief Minister of UP and Yogi Adityanath as the Prime Minister, putting up banners to this effect. Dhirendra Shastri to hold Kathas in UP for 20 days next month Before delivering the Ram Katha in Kunda, Bageshwar Dham head Dhirendra Shastri had held only two such events in UP. The first was in Gorakhpur in 2024 and the second in Meerut in March 2025. This means he had not held a Katha in UP for the past one-and-a-half years. Now, five such events are suddenly scheduled to take place across the state. These will be completed over around 20 days. The first Katha will be held in Gonda from 3 to 6 December, organised by BJP MLA Bawan Singh. In Jhansi, BJP MLA Ravi Sharma will organise a Katha from 11 to 13 December. Another event is proposed in Mathura from 15 to 19 December, organised by a local saint. BJP MLA Dr Rajeshwar Singh will organise a Katha in Lucknow from 21 to 25 December. Another Katha is scheduled to take place in Agra from 27 to 29 December. These dates have been uploaded on the website of Bageshwar Dham Sarkar. This means Dhirendra Shastri's Kathas will be held across western UP, Awadh, Bundelkhand and Purvanchal. Attempt to shift election discourse towards Hindutva through Kathas Senior Lucknow-based journalist Rajkumar Singh says, "The BJP has always created a religious atmosphere just before elections. It has also benefited from this. Earlier, it used to talk about the Ram temple. Now that its construction has been completed, it is talking about building a Krishna temple. Kathas are the best medium to take this issue to people in every village. The way Hindutva, Sanatan Dharma and the party's ideology are being discussed from the Katha stage makes it clear that the purpose of these events is to gain electoral benefits. However, it is difficult to say at this stage whether the people attending these events will vote for the party." Rajkumar Singh adds, "There is also a possibility that these events could cause damage. During the Ram Katha in Kunda, statements such as 'our dominance will continue' were made from the stage, accompanied by people raising their hands. Leaders from one caste were seen more prominently on the stages. This can create negative feelings among people from other castes sitting in the audience." On the back foot over Ram temple donation theft, BJP turns to the Krishna issue Another senior Lucknow-based journalist, Alok Pathak, says, "The BJP gives prominence to religious issues during elections. Following the case involving the theft of donations at the Ram temple, that issue can no longer be used, so the Krishna temple is being brought into focus. There is a lot of talk about building a Krishna temple during these Kathas. However, the Krishna temple issue may not gain traction because it does not have the same connection with the public as the Ram temple. These events may benefit Hindutva, but it seems less likely that any particular party will benefit from them." Alok says, "Another thing that is becoming apparent is that this is Team Yogi, which is using these Kathas to demonstrate its strength. Messages are also being sent through these events to those within the BJP who want to see Yogi removed."

stories.title: Man's head severed in rotavator accident:Body mangled as he tried to climb onto tractor while ploughing field in Lucknow
stories.summary: A 20-year-old man died after getting caught in a rotavator in Lucknow. He was climbing onto a tractor while the field was being ploughed when he came under the rotavator. In the accident, Luvkush's head was half severed and his body was mutilated. He had gone with his cousin to a villager's field, taking the tractor. The police took the body into custody. The incident took place in the Sarojininagar area on Saturday evening. Read the full report He had gone ploughing with his uncle Ramvilas, a resident of Meeranpur Pinvat, lives with his family. He works in farming. His family comprises his wife, Archana, sons Luvkush and Kaushal, and daughter Maya. Luvkush used to drive a tractor. On Saturday evening, he was ploughing the field of Manohar Lal, a fellow villager, with his uncle Kundan, 24, son of Jamuna Prasad. Kundan was driving the tractor, while Luvkush was in the field. During this, he began climbing onto the tractor from the rear. He came under the rotavator after slipping As Luvkush was climbing onto the tractor, his foot suddenly slipped and he fell directly under the rotavator. Before Kundan could understand what had happened and stop the tractor, Luvkush was caught in the rotavator and died on the spot. Family members broke down after seeing the body Half of Luvkush's head was severed, and his body was mutilated. After the incident, Kundan abandoned the tractor and fled the scene. As soon as the family members learnt about the accident, they reached the field. They broke down after seeing Luvkush's mutilated body there. The family members were inconsolable. Police reached the scene after being informed, inspected the site and took the body into custody before initiating the process of sending it for a post-mortem examination.

stories.title: Raja Bhaiya's wife speaks out over distance from family:'I am his wife'; says she and daughters were not allowed home during Ram Katha
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh strongman MLA Raghuraj Pratap Singh, popularly known as Raja Bhaiya, was the subject of an emotional Facebook post by his wife, Bhanvi Singh, in which she expressed her pain over family relationships. She said she had wished to sit with Raja Bhaiya and perform prayers during the auspicious occasion of the Ram Katha, with the entire family taking part in the religious ceremony. But that did not happen. Bhanvi Singh wrote, "The same woman because of whom I was thrown out of my own home so many years ago is the reason why, even on a sacred occasion such as the Ram Katha, my two daughters and I were not allowed to return to our home. It is difficult to express this pain in words." Peethadhishwar of Bageshwar Dham, Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, held the Shri Ram Katha at Benti Raj Bhavan in Kunda, Pratapgarh, from 17 to 20 November. Bhanvi Singh had expressed her wish to attend it, but she was not invited to the Katha. 'Could not return home even on such a sacred occasion' Bhanvi Singh began her post by expressing gratitude to the person who had shared an emotional song along with a photograph of her and Huzoor. She wrote, "The affection and sense of belonging you expressed by adding such an emotional song to the photograph of Huzoor and me truly touched my heart. I am sincerely grateful for your selfless love and respect." She then mentioned her desire to attend the Ram Katha. Bhanvi wrote that she wanted to sit with Raja Bhaiya and offer prayers at the sacred Ram Katha, and for her entire family to be part of the religious event together. But that did not happen. In her post, she wrote, "Unfortunately, because of the same woman who led to my being thrown out of my own home several years ago, my two daughters and I were not allowed to return to our home even on an auspicious occasion as sacred as the Ram Katha today. It is difficult to express this pain in words." 'I am his wife; I do not accept this distance between us' Bhanvi Singh also spoke about her marital relationship with Raja Bhaiya. She made it clear that she is Raja Bhaiya's wife and, as his wife, does not accept any distance between them. Referring to her religious beliefs regarding marriage, she wrote that in Sanatan Dharma and its traditions, marriage is not merely a social bond but a sacred vow spanning seven lifetimes. Divorce has never been part of her religious beliefs. Through this statement, Bhanvi has expressed her perspective on her marital relationship. She also indicated that she still considers the relationship equally sacred and wants the family to be united again. Describes people's love as a blessing In her post, Bhanvi Singh also mentioned the people who have been writing messages in her support on social media. She said she was deeply moved by reading their beautiful, affectionate and emotional comments. She wrote, "The affection and love with which everyone is wishing for me to return to my own home and family is no less than a blessing for me." According to Bhanvi, this affection and sense of belonging from people mean a great deal to her. She thanked everyone who had expressed respect and sympathy towards her. Prayed for love and unity in the family again At the end of her post, Bhanvi Singh prayed to God that one day truth, righteousness and the sanctity of relationships would prevail. She prayed that love, peace and unity would be restored in her family. While her post reflects her unfulfilled desire to attend the Ram Katha and the pain of staying away from her family, it also reveals her unwavering faith in her marital relationship with Raja Bhaiya. Through her words, Bhanvi has conveyed that she hopes the family will live together again and that unity will return to their relationships.

stories.title: Sub-Inspector dies in Lalitpur hours after messaging daughter:‘Inspector could stage my encounter or poison my food’
stories.summary: A 52-year-old RPF sub-inspector died in Lalitpur. At around 3 a.m. on Saturday, fellow employees took him to the medical college, where doctors declared him dead. His daughter reached the medical college after being informed of her father's death. She accused officers from the department of harassing him. The daughter said her father had sent a WhatsApp message at night, accusing his senior inspector of either having him killed in an encounter or mixing poison into his food. Joined the RPF in 2019 after retiring from the Air Force Rakesh Kumar Sinha lived at H-46, Lane Number 2, Raj Nagar, Palam Colony, New Delhi. He was the fifth of four brothers and two sisters. He has two daughters, who live in Delhi. Rakesh's wife died four years ago. Rakesh Sinha had retired from the Air Force. In 2019, he was appointed as a sub-inspector in the RPF. Around four months ago, he was transferred from Jhansi to Lalitpur. Sent message to daughter, levelled allegations against inspector Following her father's death, Rakesh's daughter Shikha arrived in Lalitpur on Saturday afternoon. Shikha said, "At around 9 p.m. on Friday, my father sent me a message on WhatsApp. He wrote, 'Look at the result of honesty. A passenger complained about the woman who was asking for money. The inspector could not do anything in the matter and became angry.'" "The inspector magnifies minor mistakes and threatens to take action against me. He could have me killed in an encounter or even poison my food." Shikha said her father had mentioned departmental stress in the message. He used to say the station was a hub of bribery Rakesh's brother-in-law, Anand Sinha, said he was very honest. He would often say that Lalitpur station was a hub of bribery. He did not like the atmosphere there. He wanted nothing to do with bribery. According to Anand, people from the department would tell him to get along with others. Rakesh feared that if he did not agree with them, he would be mistreated. RPF station house officer Arjun Diwasar refused to comment on the matter. However, the cause of his death will become clear only after the post-mortem report is released.

stories.title: Dhirendra Shastri says, ‘I bow to the people of Braj’:I have come to the city of my beloved Banke Bihari Thakurji
stories.summary: After his remarks on Lord Krishna, Bageshwar Dham Peethadhishwar Dhirendra Krishna Shastri arrived in Mathura for the first time on Saturday. Laughing, Dhirendra Shastri said, "We have come to the city of our beloved crooked and twisted Thakur Ji... Banke Bihari Ji. We bow down by rubbing our noses at the feet of all the people of Braj." Dhirendra Shastri said, "A person's stature becomes great only when, as a Sanatani, they put service first. There are also some people who call themselves Sanatanis but are not truly so. Stay away from such seasonal frogs." Today, we came to Banke Bihari for two or three reasons. First, it was Babuji's birth anniversary; second, the daughters' weddings at Gauri Gopal; and third, we wanted to have darshan of Banke Bihari Ji. Because, at present, he was the most viral and trending. After having darshan of Banke Bihari, Dhirendra Shastri led the chants: "Victory to crooked Thakur Ji... Victory to Hanuman Ji with the crooked leg... Victory to Thakur Ji with the crooked leg... As long as we live, we will continue to pamper our beloved Thakur Ji in this way." 'You have opposed Baba Bageshwar-when will you come to Mathura now?' Dhirendra Shastri targeted those trolling him on social media. He said, "You have opposed Baba Bageshwar and posted extensively against him. When will you take to the field for Banke Bihari now? When will you come to Mathura-Vrindavan? When will you step forward to erase the stain on Mathura? In the coming days, we will also reside in Braj. Some people had become devotees of Krishna for a few days, but they are no longer visible." Dhirendra Shastri said that they were going to seek the blessings of Shri Banke Bihari Ji. "We belong to Bihari Ji. We sing of his grace and undertake padyatras for him. After having darshan of Banke Bihari, we will pray for the good sense of those who troll us. May God ensure that those who have become Krishna devotees on social media for a few days become true devotees and work for Hindus." Will not allow Hindus to divide or be wiped out Dhirendra Shastri said, "We live for Hindus and will continue to live for Hindus. We will continue to work for Hindutva and Hindustan. We will not let Hindus be divided, nor will we let Hindus be wiped out. We will ensure Hindu unity." When the media asked Dhirendra Shastri whether opposition leaders were alleging that he was campaigning for the BJP in the 2027 Assembly elections, he said, "We are saints and have nothing to do with politics." He said, "We are not campaigning for anyone; we are campaigning for Lord Hanuman. We are promoting Sanatan and spreading the idea of Hindutva. There are Hindus in all the political parties in this country, which means we are campaigning for all the parties." We will not stop working for Hindu unity even if we have to endure abuse and face bullets Dhirendra Shastri said, "Our resolve is simple: if Hindus do not survive, how will India survive? If Hindus do not unite, if Sanatanis do not unite, how will our temples, shrines and pilgrimage sites survive? Hindu unity means bidding caste divisions farewell: we are all Hindu brothers. Those who work against this will naturally need some excuse or another to troll us. I pray to Lord Banke Bihari that he grants all of them wisdom." "We have endured abuses so far, and even if we have to face bullets, we will not abandon the work of Hindu unity. As long as there is life in this body, it is dedicated to the nation and Sanatan." After offering prayers at Banke Bihari, he said - Now turn Sanatan's chariot towards Mathura After offering prayers at Banke Bihari, Dhirendra Shastri said, "We keep coming to Thakur Ji's temple. We prayed to Thakur Ji. Now we say that those who trolled us should come to Bihariji like us. They should join us in addressing the stain left by Aurangzeb in Krishna Janmabhoomi, Mathura. Let all of us, and all Sanatani residents of Braj, work together to find a way to erase that stain. Now turn Sanatan's chariot towards Mathura, otherwise you are not Sanatani but Tanatani." Know which statement by Dhirendra Shastri sparked controversy Shastri had said, "Your Thakurji is bent at three places" Dhirendra Krishna's remarks about Lord Krishna sparked controversy. Comparing Lord Ram with Lord Krishna, he said: "Just look at a single photograph of your Thakurji. Even when he stands, he is bent at three places. One foot over the other, sometimes with his waist bent, and playing the flute with his neck tilted. Our Lord stands completely straight. Even his name is straight. The way he walks is straight, and he looks straight as well. Your Lord's name is also bent, he walks bent and even stands bent. Lifting a mountain is not a big deal. A disciple of our Lord lifted an entire mountain and carried it away. The abode of our Lord also has a straight name-Ayodhya, while your Lord's is-Vrindavan!" Shastri said, "Many people misinterpreted what I said" However, as the controversy grew, Dhirendra Shastri released a video clarifying his remarks. He said, "Many people misunderstood what I said. We ourselves are devotees of Thakurji and Braj. Whenever we pray to Thakurji, we say that we should be granted a place to live in Braj." "We also recite the Shrimad Bhagwat Katha and sing the praises of Thakurji. We had no intention of distinguishing between Lord Ram and Lord Krishna." In fact, Dhirendra Shastri had commented on Lord Krishna during the Shri Ram Katha being held in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh. After a video of the remarks emerged on 10 October (Sunday), the sadhus and saints of Mathura expressed their displeasure. They had asked Dhirendra Shastri to apologise.

stories.title: Bride calls off wedding after garland exchange:Firozabad woman accuses groom of spending 30 minutes with another woman in his room
stories.summary: The bride refused to go ahead with the marriage after the jaimala ceremony in Firozabad, alleging that the groom had called another woman into his room and spent around half an hour with her. Argument breaks out at marriage hall The allegation triggered a heated argument and a commotion between the two families at the marriage hall. Later, the bride, dressed in a red bridal outfit with mehndi on her hands, reached the police station and demanded action against the groom. The groom, however, denied the allegations. The incident took place in the jurisdiction of the Uttar police station. Aakash, 26, and Kajal, 24, were scheduled to get married at Gopal Marriage Home on the night of 20 November. The jaimala ceremony had already taken place when the incident occurred. The bride and groom were in a room when Aakash called another woman inside and asked Kajal to leave. According to Kajal, the groom then remained in the room with the woman for around half an hour. She and her family members objected to his behaviour, triggering an argument between the two families. As the dispute escalated, Kajal refused to go ahead with the wedding. Bride reaches police station in bridal outfit, refuses to marry Kajal later reached the police station wearing her red bridal outfit, with mehndi on her hands. She told the police, "I am from Etah district. My parents had come to Firozabad for the wedding." She said Aakash was a resident of Dwarakapuri, which falls under the jurisdiction of the Uttar police station, and that was why the wedding was being held there. However, after the jaimala ceremony, she decided to call off the marriage over his behaviour. "I no longer want to marry Aakash. Strict action should be taken against the groom. What happened to me should not happen to another girl," Kajal said. Groom denies allegations, says woman was his friend's sister After the bride, Aakash also reached the police station wearing a turban and sherwani. He denied the allegations and claimed that he had done nothing wrong. "The woman who came to meet me was my friend's sister. She works in Gurugram and lives in Kasganj," Aakash said. He added that she had attended the wedding and had come to inform him that she was leaving. "I had not closed the door or asked the bride to leave the room. The cameraman had asked her to step out," he said. Wedding guest says woman was left inside room, door locked Seema Rathore, who attended the wedding, said everything was normal initially and the photography was under way when the groom asked the bride to leave the room. "After this, two boys left a girl inside the room and went away. The door was then locked from the inside and remained shut for a long time. However, I do not know what happened inside the room," Seema said. Police call both families to station, try to resolve dispute After receiving information about the disturbance, the police called both sides to the North police station. Station House Officer Ravi Tyagi spoke to the families and tried to resolve the matter. For now, the bride remains firm on her decision not to marry, while the groom has dismissed the allegations against him as false.

stories.title: Police drag groom away by his collar from wedding pavilion:He was marrying for the second time, wife caught him with the bride
stories.summary: In Etah, police grabbed the groom by the collar and dragged him away from the wedding pavilion. He was marrying for the second time without a divorce. His first wife, who arrived with the police, stopped the wedding. The first wife alleged that their divorce case had been pending in court for three years. The groom was marrying again to receive the ₹1 lakh available under the Chief Minister's Mass Marriage Scheme. The incident took place at around 1:30 on Saturday during a Chief Minister's Mass Marriage Scheme ceremony. See two pictures... Husband seen with bride in wedding pavilion Akash (28) lives with his family in Meera Sarai village under Marhara police station. He works as a painter. The family includes two sisters, Khushbu (24) and Khushi (22), and three brothers, Vikas (26), Praveen (18) and Manjeet (14). Akash married Soni (27), from Chaman Nagariya village under Aliganj police station, on 14 November 2021. His wife alleges that Akash often assaulted her after their marriage. A divorce case between the two has been pending in court for about three years. Soni said, "My friend was due to get married at the Chief Minister's mass marriage ceremony. I had come to attend it. I saw Akash sitting with the bride in the wedding pavilion. His family members had also arrived." Police pulled him away from the wedding pavilion and took him to the police station Soni said, "I immediately informed the police. My divorce case is pending in court. Aakash is getting married again without the divorce being finalised. The police arrived, stopped the wedding, grabbed him by the collar and dragged him to the police station." Husband demanded a Bullet motorcycle Soni said, "Aakash assaulted me and drove me out of the house. He demands dowry. He wants a Bullet motorcycle. He says he will not keep me with him until he gets the vehicle. He also threatens to kill me." Kotwali in-charge Dharmendra Pawar said: This is a case involving a man who was already married getting married for the second time at a mass wedding ceremony. The accused has been taken into custody.

stories.title: 'Don't spare the Vice-Chancellor':Farmer dies by suicide, accuses Gorakhpur University VC of taking over his land
stories.summary: A farmer in Bareilly took his own life after consuming poison. Before his death, he wrote a three-page suicide note accusing Professor K.P. Singh, vice-chancellor of Deen Dayal Upadhyaya University (DDU) in Gorakhpur, of fraudulently taking over his land. The suicide note names four people-Ankit, Arun Kumar, Ratan and Srivastava-and includes their mobile numbers. The farmer wrote, "These five or six people have ruined my life." In the suicide note, the farmer told his sons: "These people are responsible for my death. They have looted lakhs of rupees from me. Tell the police and do not let them go. The vice-chancellor of Bareilly University is behind my death; he had the deed for our land registered through fraud. The Baheri CO calls us and threatens to have the land seized. Please do not spare any of them." In the suicide note, the farmer wrote: "This was all the time I had with you. Who wants to die? If I had told you, everyone would have said the next day that I was mad. We bought the land; we did not encroach on it." He concluded: "Ankit is the most guilty of all." See 3 pictures... Now read the full incident in sequence... Sardar Bhagwan Singh, who lived in Pachpeda village in Bahedi, was 55 years old. His father had moved here from Punjab and settled in 1992. Bhagwan Singh has two sons and two daughters. One son, Bhajan Singh, lives in New Zealand and works in the hospitality sector. His other son, Bhag Singh, is a lawyer at the Bahedi court. His wife is Gurdeep Kaur. According to his son Bhag Singh, they bought the land from Gurnam Singh and others in 1995 through registered sale deeds. There was a dispute over around 12 acres of the total 24 acres of land under plot number 519. The family had built a house on this land and lived there. They also farmed it. The family alleges that the land consolidation process had been completed in 1965. However, in 2015, their names were removed from the land records on the orders of the Consolidation Officer. A petition was filed in the Allahabad High Court against this in 2019. Despite the matter being sub judice, former Rohilkhand University Bareilly vice-chancellor Prof. K.P. Singh, who is now the VC of DDU, had the disputed land registered in the names of his wife Sanjesh and relatives on 24 January 2025. Son says former deputy tehsildar had demanded ₹10 lakh Bhag Singh has also accused former deputy tehsildar Shobhit Chaudhary of collusion. He said the tehsildar threatened his father in court and demanded ₹10 lakh. He also threatened to have the standing crop destroyed and the land seized with the help of the police. Bhag Singh said his father had planned to complain to the Governor, the district magistrate and the sub-divisional magistrate. Complaints had also been made to the Chief Minister and the senior superintendent of police. The issue had been raised at a press conference around four months earlier. SP says complaints had not been brought to his notice earlier Northern SP Santosh Singh said he had not previously been informed that the aggrieved party had been repeatedly approaching officials. The matter was pending before the court. The process was being carried out solely on the basis of the court's decision. Regarding the complaints made to the DM, SSP, Chief Minister and Governor, as well as the press conference held four months ago, the SP said this information had now come to light. An investigation would be conducted. The SP said it would first be examined why the allegations had been made and against whom. The family members would be spoken to. Further legal action would be taken according to their complaint. Body taken to village after post-mortem On Friday, the farmer consumed poison while going to his brother-in-law's house in Bajpur, Uttarakhand. He was first taken to a private hospital in Bahedi. When his condition became critical, he was referred to Bareilly, but he died on the way. After the post-mortem, the family took the body to the village. A large police contingent has been deployed in the village. MLA Ataur Rahman said: "Our deepest condolences are with the family. May Allah grant him comfort and peace, and grant peace to his family. We also urge the administration to extend its sympathy and provide them with the best possible assistance." Farmer says: Funeral rites will be stopped if FIR is not registered Office-bearers of the farmers' organisation have warned that the last rites will not be performed until an FIR is registered against the accused. They accused the police of delaying the registration of the FIR. The farmers' organisations say the accused are influential. They are preventing the FIR from being registered.

stories.title: Akhilesh takes a swipe at BJP over 'Radhe-Radhe' slogan:Says the party is on its way out, warns new SP members about investigations
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav said, "The people who have left the lotus have joined us. Now the lotus will wilt further. They will have to come up with a new slogan." Akhilesh said: They are now raising the slogan, 'Radhe Radhe, make the lotus bloom'. This means the lotus has wilted. In our tradition, we say 'Radhe Radhe' when bidding someone farewell. This means their departure is approaching. That is why they are saying 'Radhe Radhe'. Akhilesh also said that the SP organises Ramleela events too. He said Dr Rammanohar Lohia had asked artist MF Husain to create posters on the Ramayana. Akhilesh Yadav made these remarks during a press conference at the SP headquarters in Lucknow on Saturday. Several leaders from different political parties joined the SP on the occasion. What Akhilesh Said About Those Joining the SP ‘If We Come to Power, We Will Scrap the Agniveer Scheme’ Akhilesh said, "Whenever the Samajwadis get an opportunity, we will end arrangements such as the Agniveer scheme." He said the SP had launched its website. "At a time when people want to join through technology, they are welcome to do so. Today, getting justice, receiving respect and protecting people's dignity under the Constitution have become major challenges. The BJP is responsible for all these problems. Once the BJP is removed, these problems will go away." Seats Will Be Allocated Based on Winning Prospects Speaking about the 2027 Assembly elections, Akhilesh made it clear that talks with the Congress were continuing. Seats would be allocated based on the prospects of winning. He said removing the BJP was necessary to protect democracy and the Constitution. He described his meeting with Aam Aadmi Party leader Sanjay Singh as a discussion between the two leaders. Questions Raised Over Election Commission and Voter Lists Akhilesh accused the Election Commission of India of working under pressure from the BJP. He took a dig at the Chief Minister's statement that the names of 1.27 crore Hindu voters had been deleted from the electoral rolls. He asked what 'divine vision from heaven' had given the Chief Minister this information after the names were deleted. ‘In 2027, the Lathis Will Lose and Laptops Will Win’ Akhilesh Yadav released a new video with the slogan, 'In 2027, the lathis will lose and laptops will win... A PDA government in 2027'. He said the strength of the PDA had reached the grassroots and had become an issue of social justice, which would lead to the BJP's defeat in the upcoming elections. The SP chief accused the state government of corruption and alleged irregularities in the 'Har Ghar Nal Yojana'. He said everything would come to light in the CAG report. He announced that if the SP formed the government, a 'superconductor' factory would be set up in the state. Police services such as 'Dial 100' would also be made efficient again, as they were earlier. ‘Police and Some Officials Are Working Like BJP Office-Bearers’ Akhilesh said, "We will not hold a press conference on Gorakhpur now. We will do so after two days of mourning. The entire police force and some officials are working as BJP office-bearers." He added, "I had said earlier that I would write to the Election Commission. BJP leaders are sitting in the government and making preparations. They know that the public will remove them. The day the election dates are announced, the BJP will lose." He said, "We will write to the Election Commission with signatures of all our MLAs, MLCs and MPs, giving examples of officials who have worked like BJP workers. These officials have not been removed since the BJP came to power. Their relatives are occupying positions from which we cannot expect justice." Who Is Utpal Rai, Who Has Joined the SP? Utpal Rai, who hails from Mau district, has also contested elections from the Madhuban Assembly constituency. He has served as the vice-president of the Allahabad University Students' Union. He is the younger brother of Nishith Rai, former vice-chancellor of Dr Shakuntala Misra National Rehabilitation University. Utpal Rai was once considered close to Manoj Sinha. He joined the BJP in July 2016. Now, after a decade, he has left the BJP and joined the SP. However, his political career has not been limited to the BJP. He has been associated with different political parties. Utpal Rai also served as a minister of state with independent charge during the BSP government.

stories.title: Apna Dal MLA Vinay Verma hurls abuses from stage:Loses cool at BJP MP Jagdambika Pal's supporters, says, 'Don't do politics here'
stories.summary: In Siddharthnagar, Apna Dal MLA Vinay Verma hurled abuses from the stage on Saturday. He told supporters of the BJP MP who were raising slogans, "You are acting as brokers. Don't do politics here." A video of the incident has also emerged. Supporters of BJP MP Jagdambika Pal and NDA MLA Vinay Verma clashed during the foundation stone-laying ceremony for a community health centre (CHC). They began arguing, and the situation soon escalated into a physical fight. The MLA and MP's supporters kicked and punched each other on the stage. During the clash, one of the MLA's supporters had his kurta torn. Police personnel deployed at the site intervened and brought the situation under control. The incident took place in Badhni block, around 40 km from the district headquarters. According to sources, the BJP MP had not been invited to the foundation stone-laying ceremony. However, he arrived at the event before the MLA. This angered the MLA's supporters, who began raising slogans. Angered by this, the MP's supporters started creating a ruckus. See 2 pictures- The MLA was the chief guest; the MP arrived without prior notice Barhni's primary health centre is to be developed at a cost of ₹19.66 crore. The foundation stone-laying and bhoomi pujan ceremony was scheduled for 10 a.m. on Saturday. Vinay Verma, MLA from the Shohratgarh constituency in Siddharthnagar, arrived as the chief guest. It was reported that Jagdambika Pal, MP from the district's Domariyaganj constituency, was not supposed to attend the programme. However, the MP arrived before the bhoomi pujan. His supporters welcomed him by garlanding him along the way. Amid slogan-shouting, the MP reached the venue with his supporters. MLA's supporters raised slogans; people accompanying the MP grew angry At that point, MLA supporter Pradeep Kamalapuri began raising slogans from the stage: "Long live MLA Vinay Verma, the development-orientated leader." On hearing this, the MP raised his hand and gestured towards Pradeep. The MP's supporters then climbed onto the stage and began assaulting Pradeep Kamalapuri. Chief Development Officer (CDO) Balram Singh, SDM Sadar, several senior officials and police personnel brought the situation under control. MLA called MP's supporters brokers Vinay Verma then arrived on stage with his wife, Babita Verma, and began addressing the gathering. The MP's supporters still did not relent and started making remarks about the MLA. The MLA lost his temper, called the MP's supporters touts from the stage and began hurling abuse. The matter was later brought under control after considerable efforts to pacify both sides. The MLA performed the groundbreaking ceremony with his wife and the MP. MP's representative said - MLA was taking sole credit, angering supporters MP's representative Rinku Pal said, "MLA Vinay Verma wanted to take credit for this programme. As per the rules, there is a provision for inviting the MP to a programme five days in advance. The poster also makes no mention of the MP. When the Health Department released details of the programme on Friday, the MP was informed suddenly. However, his name was still not included on the poster. This was what had angered our supporters."

stories.title: Owaisi receives guard of honour meant for judge:Mix-up after AIMIM chief arrives at circuit house before SC judge
stories.summary: In Saharanpur, police personnel gave Owaisi a guard of honour instead of a Supreme Court judge. The AIMIM chief stood and took the salute at the Circuit House before leaving. A Supreme Court judge was scheduled to arrive at the Circuit House on Saturday, but Owaisi arrived before him. Mistaking Owaisi for the judge, the police personnel gave him a guard of honour. See 2 pictures... First, what is a 'Guard of Honour'? According to former Uttar Pradesh DGP Sulkhan Singh, a 'Guard of Honour' is considered a symbol of the state's sovereign authority and honour. It involves a contingent of the police or armed forces conducting a formal parade and showing respect with a salute. This is neither an emotional decision nor an honour linked to popularity. It is given in accordance with established protocols, rules and constitutional conventions. The purpose of a guard of honour is to formally and officially honour a particular person or occasion on behalf of the state. A police guard salute is entirely a departmental procedure. Outside the department, a guard salute is given only on the occasion of state functions. Under the Uttar Pradesh Guard and Escort Rules, a guard of honour or formal salute is prescribed only for uniformed officers. This includes military officers and military contingents, along with police officers. Apart from this, any other senior official is entitled only to a simple salute from a sentry, not a guard salute. MPs and MLAs cannot be given one The national flag (the Tricolour) is given a National Salute, while officers of the rank of DIG and above are given a General Salute. This formal salute by the guard is called a 'turnout'. It is given to uniformed officers of the rank of Superintendent and above, with the entire guard presenting the salute. In addition, the mortal remains of an officer or employee of the armed forces are given a salute with reversed arms. When State Honours are declared, the mortal remains of other dignitaries are also given a salute. This cannot be given to MPs and MLAs.

stories.title: Wife murdered for refusing to make tea:12-year-old son called police in Gonda, saying, ‘Dad has killed Mom’
stories.summary: In Gonda, a husband murdered his wife with an axe for not making tea. The accused carried out the crime in front of their 12-year-old son on Friday night and fled. The son then called the police and said, "Dad has killed Mum. Her body is lying inside the house." When police reached the scene after receiving the information, they found the blood-soaked body of 35-year-old Suman lying on a charpoy. The dog squad and forensic team collected evidence from the scene. The incident took place in the Kaudia Bazaar police station area, 30 kilometres from the district headquarters. See 2 pictures Now let us understand the entire case step by step The accused, Manoj Kumar Shukla (40), is a resident of Kotia Madara village. His family comprises his wife, Suman (35), son Kishan (12) and daughter Shagun (4). According to neighbours, Manoj was addicted to alcohol. He frequently quarrelled with his wife when she tried to stop him from drinking. His son Kishan said, "At around 11:30 p.m. on Friday night, Dad returned home drunk and insisted that Mum make tea. When she refused, the two began arguing. During the argument, Dad became enraged, picked up an axe lying nearby and attacked Mum, killing her." ASP said - Son informed police ASP Nitesh Singh said that, after receiving information from the son, the station house officer reached the spot with a police team. The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination. Based on a complaint filed by the deceased woman's mother, a murder case has been registered against her husband, Manoj Kumar Shukla, and his mother. Raids are being conducted to find the absconding accused.

stories.title: Murdered father-in-law for not being invited to wedding:Son's wedding procession was underway in Mathura when his body was found covered in blood
stories.summary: In Mathura, a son-in-law slit his father-in-law's throat and killed him after not being given a wedding invitation card. He then dumped the body in a field and fled. After seeing the body in the field, local people informed the police and the family. Police reached the spot and began an investigation. The deceased man's son alleged that his brother-in-law had killed his father. He said that before the wedding, the accused had threatened his father, saying, "Blood will be spilled in your house on the day of the wedding." Based on the son's complaint, police registered a case against the accused brother-in-law. Police teams are conducting raids to arrest him. The incident took place at around 10 p.m. on Friday in the Govardhan police station area. The wedding could not take place after the groom's father was killed. Here is the full case... According to the police, the son of 62-year-old Omprakash, a resident of Basai village in Aligarh's Iglas area, was getting married on Friday. That night, he arrived with his son's wedding procession near the mandi in Govardhan town. The wedding guests were dancing and singing. As soon as the procession reached the entrance, some villagers came running there. They said that the body of the groom's father, Omprakash, was lying in a field some distance away near the bride's house. On hearing this, the groom and his family members reached the spot. They identified the body. Son said-brother-in-law had threatened to kill him People immediately informed the police. The police reached the spot and inspected the scene. They then questioned the family members. The groom, Arvind (22), alleged that his brother-in-law had killed his father. He said his brother-in-law was angry because he had not been given a wedding invitation. He had threatened his father that blood would be shed in his house on the day of the wedding. He had not attended the wedding either. Arvind alleged that he was the one who had killed his father. SSP says accused will be arrested soon SSP Shlok Kumar said the police had received information on Friday night that a man's body was lying in a field. The police reached the spot and inspected the scene.

stories.title: Rain alert covers 13 eastern UP districts:Fog grips western UP as Cyclone Akvan keeps weather unsettled for another day
stories.summary: The weather in Uttar Pradesh is set to change under the impact of Cyclone 'Akvan', which has formed over the Bay of Bengal. An alert has been issued for thunderstorms and rain in 13 districts of Purvanchal today. Winds may blow at speeds of 30 to 40 kmph. Lightning is also likely. Heavy rain is expected in Sonbhadra and Chandauli. Meanwhile, fog enveloped 15 cities, including Pilibhit, Sambhal, Muzaffarnagar, Deoria and Bulandshahr. Visibility in rural areas fell so low that it became difficult to see even 10 metres ahead on the roads. The daytime temperature fell below 30°C. Muzaffarnagar was the coldest, with the night-time temperature recorded at 10.2°C. The Meteorological Department said Cyclone 'Akvan' had weakened and was now moving northwards. This will bring a change in the weather in Purvanchal. There will be rain accompanied by strong winds for two days. The weather will worsen tomorrow. Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said, “Light to moderate rain is possible in some parts of Purvanchal on 21 and 22 November. Temperatures may fall by 3 to 5 degrees, increasing the chill. stories.title: PM shares Bhajan Clubbing pictures on X:Says event in Kashi, city of Baba Vishwanath, captivated everyone
stories.summary: Kashi Ganga Mahotsav began at Namo Ghat in Varanasi on Friday (20 Nov) evening, with bhajan clubbing as the highlight of its opening night. The performance by Kolkata-based siblings Raghav and Prachi captivated the audience. The one-and-a-half-hour programme also drew praise from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who shared photographs of the event on his X account. He wrote, “The bhajan clubbing programme in Kashi, the city of Baba Vishwanath, captivated everyone. My young companions participated enthusiastically in the event held at Namo Ghat. Their enthusiasm was truly remarkable!” More than 15 bhajans performed during 90-minute programme Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared six photographs on X, showing Raghav and Prachi performing alongside their father, Agopi Agarwal. One of the pictures also captured the audience, with BJP state in-charge Jagdish Patel, Minister of State Hansraj Vishwakarma, the BJP Kashi region president and the mayor among those present. During the one-and-a-half-hour programme at Namo Ghat, the brother-sister duo performed more than 15 bhajans. The energy of the audience was incredible After the Bhajan Clubbing event, Raghav said, “We are proud to be in Kashi. The enthusiasm of the young people was incredible. India has 40 crore Generation Z members. They are the future of the country and will take it forward. We are proud to be part of Generation Z as well.” Raghav and Prachi said, “We are from Kolkata. Two and a half years ago, we were sitting on the banks of the Ganga in Kashi with two others, jamming to bhajans at the ghat. That was when we started this initiative. Our biggest achievement is that the Prime Minister himself attended our programme and listened to our Bhajan Clubbing.” Kashi has started feeling like home Raghav and Prachi further added, “A lot has changed, and Kashi has now begun to feel like home to us. We do not contest elections, but we bring young people together and try to connect them with God by encouraging them to move away from their phones. This is what we are doing and will continue to do.”

stories.title: JCB crushes BJP leader’s son to death; police arrest 35:SP leader seeks release of accused in Gorakhpur; murder case names 66 people
stories.summary: Police have added charges of murder and criminal conspiracy in the case involving the death of a BJP leader’s son after he was hit by a JCB machine during a roadshow by Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav in Gorakhpur. Late on Friday night, police carried out raids in several police station areas and detained 35 Samajwadi Party leaders and workers. Party leader Kajal Nishad also reached the AIIMS police station and demanded their release. Five accused sent to jail, main organiser still absconding The five accused arrested on Thursday, including the JCB driver, were questioned and produced before a court on Friday. They were subsequently sent to jail. The main accused, Mrityunjay Yadav alias Bittu, who allegedly organised the roadshow, remains absconding. Police raid several areas across the city Police conducted raids in several areas, including Gorakhnath, AIIMS, Khorabar, Jhangha, Chauri Chaura, Shahpur, Chiluatal and Gulriha. Those arrested include JCB driver Vinod Shahi, a resident of Jhangha; Narsingh Yadav of Raghopatti Tola Failaha; Rahul Yadav of Padri Bazar in Shahpur; Virendra Yadav of Gonarpura in Gulriha; and Shivang of Chiluatal. Police are also investigating the roles of others taken into custody. Search underway for main accused; six other vehicles seized Police have identified Taramanadal resident Mrityunjay Yadav alias Bittu as the organiser of the roadshow. Raids are being conducted at various locations to arrest him. Investigators are also examining the role of the JCB owner and other vehicles involved in the roadshow. Apart from the JCB involved in the accident, police have seized three other JCB machines and two cranes. The investigating officer has recorded statements from 25 people present near the accident site. Footage from more than 50 CCTV cameras collected Police have collected footage from more than 50 CCTV cameras installed along the route from the airport to the AIIMS police station. The DVR of a medical shop's CCTV camera near the accident site has also been seized. The footage reportedly captured the accident. Kajal Nishad demands release of 10 Samajwadi Party leaders Actress and Samajwadi Party leader Kajal Nishad reached the AIIMS police station with her husband, Sanjay Nishad, and party supporters. She attempted to stage a sit-in protest, demanding the release of 10 SP leaders who had been taken into custody. Police personnel persuaded her to call off the protest and leave the premises. Earlier, she had met Cantonment CO Arun Kumar Yash and sought details about those detained. The CO assured her that their roles would be examined based on the evidence after questioning. He added that those found innocent would be released. Death caused by JCB returning from SP roadshow The accident took place near Jharkhandi Mor at around 2 pm on 18 November. Aryavardhan, son of BJP leader Omkar Singh of Awas Vikas Colony in Jharkhandi, was walking towards the crossroads when a JCB involved in Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav’s roadshow hit him, leaving him critically injured. He was rushed to AIIMS, where doctors declared him dead. Aryavardhan was a Class 10 student at Kendriya Vidyalaya, Nandanagar. FIR names SP leaders and 60 unidentified people Based on a complaint filed by Omkar Singh, AIIMS police registered an FIR against the unidentified JCB driver and Samajwadi Party leaders Sadhu Yadav alias Sadhu Bhaiya, Manoj Yadav, Mrityunjay Yadav alias Bittu, Yogesh Yadav and Chand Prakash. The FIR also names 60 unidentified people.

stories.title: Yogi’s younger brother lit their mother’s funeral pyre:CM circumambulated the pyre and bowed before it; broke down in tears while carrying the bier on his shoulder
stories.summary: Yogi’s mother, Savitri Devi, was cremated on Saturday. His youngest brother, Mahendra Mohan Bisht, lit her funeral pyre at Chandi Ghat in Haridwar. Yogi circumambulated his mother’s funeral pyre and bowed before it. Yogi travelled to Haridwar with his mother’s body from their ancestral village of Panchur in Pauri. He broke down in tears during the final journey. He carried his mother’s bier on his shoulder from the house to the ambulance. He also shouldered the bier at Chandi Ghat. Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Ministers Brajesh Pathak and Keshav Prasad Maurya, minister Sanjay Nishad, Baba Ramdev, and more than 50 VIPs and saints were present at the ghat. Yogi posted a photograph of himself carrying his mother’s bier on X. He shared a verse from the Mahabharata, which means: “There is no shade like a mother, no shelter like a mother, no love like a mother, no protection like a mother, and no life-giver in this world like a mother.” After the cremation, Yogi will return to Lucknow to attend an event featuring PM Modi. His mother took her last breath at home at 10.45 am on Friday. She was 91. Yogi stayed beside her body throughout the night and did not eat or drink anything. 3 pictures from the funeral

stories.title: Rajnath Singh to spend two days in Lucknow:To attend Skill convocation and BBD University ceremonies
stories.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will be in Lucknow for a two-day visit from Saturday. During the visit, he will attend two educational events in the city. On Saturday evening, he will attend the fifth Skill Convocation and the National Toppers' Felicitation Ceremony at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan. On Sunday, he will attend the convocation ceremony of Babu Banarasi Das University. In between, he will also visit Dehradun and Haridwar. Will attend the Skill Convocation on Saturday Rajnath Singh will arrive at Lucknow airport at 3:45 p.m. on Saturday. From there, he will go straight to his residence at 5 Kalidas Marg. He will leave the residence at 4:55 p.m. and reach the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan at 5:10 p.m. He will attend the fifth Skill Convocation and the National Toppers' Felicitation Ceremony there from 5:30 p.m. to 6:45 p.m. He will return to his residence at 7:05 p.m. Will attend BBD University's convocation ceremony Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will arrive at Babu Banarasi Das University at 11:30 a.m. on Sunday. He will attend the convocation ceremony here until 12:45 p.m. He will then attend a private programme. At 2:05 p.m., he will leave for Dehradun from Lucknow airport. Rajnath Singh to return after programmes in Dehradun and Haridwar After attending the scheduled programmes in Dehradun and Haridwar, Rajnath Singh will arrive at Lucknow airport at 6:55 p.m. From there, he will go to attend a private programme. He will reach his residence at 5 Kalidas Marg at 7:40 p.m. He will stay in Lucknow on Sunday night as well.

stories.title: Traffic diversions on 35 routes for PM Modi’s visit:Arrangements in Lucknow from noon to 10 pm, he will attend convocation
stories.summary: Traffic arrangements in Lucknow have been changed for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to the city on Saturday. PM Modi will attend the fifth Skill Convocation-2026 under the Skill India, Skilled India initiative. In view of his visit, the traffic police have implemented diversions on 35 major routes across the city. During this period, traffic will be affected around the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan, Gomti Nagar, Kamta, Polytechnic, Shaheed Path and Ahimamau areas. The traffic police have appealed to motorists to use alternative routes. However, ambulances, hearse vehicles and school vehicles will be allowed to use roads under restrictions in an emergency. The administration has issued helpline number 9454405155 for information related to any emergency or diversion during this period. Find out about the city's traffic diversions on 21 November

stories.title: Woman takes wedding procession to boyfriend’s home:Accuses him of breaking 7-year marriage promise; he marries today
stories.summary: A woman from Dehradun reached her boyfriend’s home in Shamli with a wedding procession on November 19, accusing him of refusing to marry her after a seven-year relationship. The woman arrived at the house in Kandhla with traditional music and a banner that read, ‘I have brought the wedding procession for the bride’. She was accompanied by her family members. Her boyfriend, Ankush, works in the Merchant Navy and is currently posted in Delhi. His wedding cards have reportedly been printed, and his wedding procession is scheduled to leave on November 21. The woman has accused him of sexually assaulting her on the promise of marriage. She has also threatened to take her own life if he does not marry her. The matter falls under the jurisdiction of Kandhla police station. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to the woman to understand her allegations and the sequence of events. Woman says relationship began in 2016 The woman, a BSc student living in Dehradun, said she first met Ankush in 2016 at her maternal uncle’s house in Dehradun. His cousin, Naina, was her close friend. She said their conversations initially began as normal interactions but gradually increased. Ankush started messaging her regularly. In 2019, Ankush invited her to his sister Shivani’s wedding by sending her a WhatsApp invitation. Naina also insisted that she attend the wedding. Alleges sexual assault at his sister’s wedding The woman said she first visited Ankush’s village on February 18, 2019. According to her, Ankush expressed his love for her and promised to marry her. She alleged that when he tried to get physically close to her inappropriately, she refused. He allegedly told her that she belonged to him. Later that evening, she was looking for her friend Naina. Ankush told her that Naina was with his sister Shivani and offered to take her there. However, instead of taking her to his sister, he allegedly took her to a room, locked the door and sexually assaulted her. She said she was very young at the time and did not fully understand the situation. She believed that what had happened might be a part of love. Woman says she remained unwell for 18 months According to the woman, Ankush’s family also came to know that something wrong had happened to her. His younger maternal aunt, who lived in Dehradun, later took her back home. She said the incident left her traumatised and she went into depression. She remained seriously unwell for nearly one-and-a-half years. During this period, Ankush allegedly arranged calls through his sister-in-law, who lived in Chandigarh. She was asked not to tell anyone about the incident and was assured that Ankush would marry her. Claims engagement was arranged to withdraw case The woman alleged that Ankush continued to delay the marriage with repeated assurances for nearly three years. In 2021, her health deteriorated, following which her mother filed a police complaint. She said that after the court case began, Ankush’s family tried to persuade them to settle the matter by promising marriage. An engagement ceremony between her and Ankush was also held. However, she alleged that the engagement was arranged only to get the court case withdrawn. Says boyfriend later repeated marriage promise The woman claimed that Ankush later visited her in Dehradun and again assured her that he would marry her. However, she recently learnt that he was preparing to marry another woman. She said she had come to Kandhla with her family because she wanted to marry Ankush and had wanted the same earlier as well. Woman and family spent night outside his house When the woman reached Ankush’s house on November 19, an argument reportedly broke out between her family and his relatives. Police intervened to bring the situation under control. The woman and her family members remained outside the house until late at night. On Friday, they shifted to a hotel in Kandhla. The woman said she would either marry Ankush or take her own life. Meanwhile, Ankush’s brother dismissed the allegations as baseless. Woman submits complaint and threatens suicide The woman has submitted a written complaint at Kandhla police station, accusing Ankush of rape. She alleged that when she reached his house to marry him, his family members misbehaved with her and insulted her. She also wrote a suicide note, holding Ankush, son of Garibdas, and his family responsible for her death. In the note, she wrote that several people had wronged her and accused Ankush of sexually exploiting her for seven years while repeatedly promising marriage. She also blamed the police and administration for not helping her. Police say rape case already registered in Dehradun During the inquiry, police found that the woman and her family had already registered a rape case against Ankush in Dehradun. Police told her that two separate FIRs could not be registered at different police stations for the same incident. They asked her to bring a copy of the existing FIR and visit Kandhla police station along with the investigating officer handling the case in Dehradun. Police assured her that necessary action would be taken in the matter.

stories.title: 'AI cannot take away jobs,' says Modi:Yogi joins Lucknow event after his mother's last rites, speaks to PM on stage
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended the 5th National Skill Convocation Ceremony in Lucknow on Saturday. He honoured national toppers who had arrived from across the country. The PM said, “The skills you have learnt at ITIs are India's strength today, and you will build a developed India. Understand this clearly: no one can take away the employment of someone who has skills.” Before this, PM Modi spoke to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Yogi reached Lucknow in the afternoon after performing the last rites of his mother, Savitri Devi, in Haridwar earlier in the day. PM Modi inaugurates Nitish Setu in Bihar, hugs Nitish Kumar In Bihar’s Vaishali, PM Modi inaugurated the six-lane Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur bridge over the Ganga, named ‘Nitish Setu’ after former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar. Before the inauguration, Modi hugged Nitish Kumar. He later walked along the bridge and waved a gamcha. Addressing a gathering, Modi said Bihar had moved from counting scams to counting investment figures under the NDA government. He also inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 227 development projects worth over ₹34,470 crore. From Lucknow, he will attend the 5th National Skill Convocation Ceremony, where six toppers from Uttar Pradesh and 52 national toppers from across the country will be honoured. PM says Bihar found confidence in good governance under Nitish’s leadership During his 16-minute speech in Vaishali, PM Modi said Bihar had chosen a path of hope and trust nearly three decades ago and found confidence in good governance under Nitish Kumar’s leadership. He said the bridge had been named in Nitish’s honour as a tribute to his dedication and public service. Modi also said 4.3 lakh people in Bihar had been provided with permanent houses. Referring to poverty alleviation, he said 50 crore people had been lifted out of poverty across the country in 12 years, adding that the poor remained the government’s priority. stories.title: Congress seeks maximum 68 seats in western UP:Party seeks to consolidate Dalit-Muslim support; will SP give up its 22 sitting seats?
stories.summary: The Congress has staked a claim to 181 seats ahead of the start of seat-sharing talks with the Samajwadi Party. The party has shown the greatest interest in seats in western Uttar Pradesh, where it has demanded 68 constituencies. This indicates that Congress wants to win back its traditional core voters, Muslims and Dalits. Since 2014, western Uttar Pradesh has largely remained a BJP stronghold. Before the BSP emerged as their main political choice, the Jatav community, the largest Dalit sub-group by population, used to be a committed Congress vote bank. The question is whether the SP will give up 22 seats it currently holds to accommodate an alliance with Congress. Congress has also staked a claim to 12 seats held by the RLD and SBSP, both of which were allies of the SP in 2022. How many seats will the parties be able to agree on in the meeting? Read the report... The Congress list of 181 Assembly seats includes 22 constituencies won by the SP in 2022. Of these, 19 are general-category seats and three are reserved seats. However, it is also true that the political equations have changed in six of these 22 constituencies since 2022. The BJP and its ally Apna Dal (S) wrested Muslim-dominated seats such as Kundarki, Katehari and Suar from the SP in by-elections. Manoj Pandey from Unchahar, Rakesh Singh from Gauriganj and Pooja Pal from Chail have also left the SP and joined the BJP. Will the SP give up the 22 seats it currently holds? According to senior journalist Yogesh Mishra, parties often have to compromise even on seats held by their sitting MLAs when forming an alliance. Of the 181 seats claimed by Congress, 22 were won by the SP in the 2022 elections. These include Bachhrawan, Sareni, Harchandpur and Unchahar in Rae Bareli; Chail in Kaushambi; Kalpi in Jalaun; and Katehari in Ambedkar Nagar. By-elections were subsequently held in Katehari and Kundarki. Meanwhile, leaders such as Manoj Pandey, the MLA from Unchahar, and Pooja Pal, the MLA from Chail, left the SP and joined the BJP. As a result, the SP now has sitting MLAs in only 16 of these 22 constituencies. However, the party remains strong in these seats. If Congress does not withdraw its claim to them, one possible compromise could be for the SP to field its MLAs on Congress tickets. Why has Congress demanded the highest number of seats in western UP? A regional breakdown of Congress's list of 181 Assembly seats shows that it wants to contest the highest number, 68, in western UP, followed by 65 in eastern UP, 34 in central UP and 14 in Bundelkhand. Of the 126 seats in western UP, the BJP won 85 in 2022, while the SP-RLD alliance won 41. The SP alliance swept Shamli and Moradabad. It also gave the BJP a tough fight in Muzaffarnagar and Meerut, while the BJP dominated other districts. At the time, the BSP's core voters were seen as leaning towards the BJP. However, a shift was visible in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The SP-Congress alliance performed well in this belt with the support of Dalit voters. One reason cited for this was that Congress helped bring Dalit votes to the alliance. Congress firebrand leader Imran Masood also managed to win from western UP. He is currently the party's working president. Congress now wants to rebuild its roots in Uttar Pradesh by relying on its traditional core vote bank and the Dalit-Muslim equation in this region. The largest share of the Dalit vote bank is still associated with the BSP. However, Chandrashekhar is also preparing to make inroads into it this time. Congress is trying to establish the narrative that if the BJP has to be defeated, Dalits and Muslims should put their faith in it rather than looking elsewhere. In which regions of UP has Congress demanded more seats? Congress has staked its biggest claims in Assembly constituencies falling under the areas represented by its six sitting MPs. It has also included constituencies under Lok Sabha constituencies that were once its strongholds, including Maharajganj, Kushinagar, Bansgaon, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Kanpur, Jhansi, Sitapur, Rae Bareli, Amethi and Barabanki. The list also includes 39 Assembly constituencies where Congress was leading during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. How many seats will the SP and Congress agree on? Senior journalist Ratanmani Lal says that the biggest weakness of Congress is its organisation. It will need the SP's organisational strength to perform well. In 2017, when the SP contested the elections while in power, it gave Congress 104 seats. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the SP gave Congress 17 seats. At the rate of five Assembly constituencies per Lok Sabha constituency, this works out to 85 Assembly seats. This means that the seat-sharing arrangement between the SP and Congress is likely to be limited to 85 to 104 seats. This number would also be ideal for Congress. In 2022, it contested 399 seats but secured only 2.33% of the vote and won two seats. However, its vote share crossed 9% in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections after it joined hands with the SP. This was one of the factors that caused the NDA its biggest setback in Uttar Pradesh. If the two parties manage to coordinate effectively, Congress could also benefit in terms of vote share and seats in 2027. Congress has entrusted Priyanka with responsibility for seat-sharing talks Congress has formed a five-member committee to hold seat-sharing talks with the SP. Priyanka Gandhi will lead the committee. Its other members are KC Venugopal, UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam, state Congress president Aradhana Mishra and working president Imran Masood. The SP will be represented in the talks by leaders such as Akhilesh Yadav and Ram Gopal Yadav. According to senior sources in both parties, the final round of talks and the decision on seat-sharing will take place at a joint meeting of Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav. Both parties are trying to resolve the seat-sharing issue by 30 November. Congress is set to begin its election campaign in Uttar Pradesh from 10 December.

stories.title: Who benefits if caste dominates UP elections?:BJP, which lost 29 seats in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, wants to fight on Hindutva
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh politics once again appears to be revolving around the divide between caste and Hindutva. This time, the real battle is not about candidates but about deciding the key election issue. The Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance has already made it clear that it will fight the 2027 Assembly elections on the issue of caste. If this happens, the BJP could face greater losses. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the SP-Congress alliance gained 37 seats in Uttar Pradesh by raising concerns over the Constitution being under threat and using the PDA factor. The SP's vote share also increased by 15.48 percentage points. The Opposition wants to contest the next election using the same successful formula. On the other hand, statements by the BJP's top leadership, including Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, make it clear that the party is preparing to take the election beyond caste divisions and fight on the agenda of Hindutva, nationalism, law and order, and the Uniform Civil Code. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the SP-Congress alliance won 43 of Uttar Pradesh's 80 seats with the help of the 'PDA' formula. The BJP, which had won 62 seats in 2019, was reduced to 33. This caste arithmetic also kept the BJP away from the majority mark of 272 seats in the Lok Sabha on its own. The Opposition is preparing to repeat a similar strategy in 2027, which is why Akhilesh Yadav is bringing the election closer to caste-based equations. Rallied support in Agra by calling Dalits 'powerful' On 15 November 2026, Akhilesh Yadav held a major 'Dalit Mahasammelan' in Agra. According to political observers, Dalit-dominated constituencies in western Uttar Pradesh have traditionally been considered strongholds of the BSP. Choosing Agra, a reserved constituency, Akhilesh gave a new meaning to the letter 'D' in the PDA formula, calling it 'Dumdaar Dalit' (powerful Dalit). He said that if his party came to power, it would provide a special package for the Dalit community. He also raised the issues of protecting reservation and the Constitution. Akhilesh makes a calculated move on the 'Social Transformation Front' On 12 November 2026, Asaduddin Owaisi (AIMIM) and Chandrashekhar Azad (Azad Samaj Party) announced the formation of the 'Social Transformation Front'. Instead of directly opposing the new alliance, which is focused on the Dalit-Muslim equation, Akhilesh welcomed it. Akhilesh claimed that the front would reduce the BJP's vote share by 2 to 3%. However, he also made it clear that the 'PDA' remained the biggest option for defeating the BJP. Political analysts believe that Akhilesh's stance is part of his strategy to win over Dalit and Muslim voters. Building ties with non-Yadav OBC and Dalit leaders To make up for the Jat vote in western Uttar Pradesh, the SP leadership has adopted a softer stance towards Chandrashekhar Azad, chief of the Azad Samaj Party. Party leaders have been asked not to attack him directly. In addition, the SP is working on a strategy to move beyond its traditional Muslim-Yadav (MY) base and give priority to non-Yadav backward castes in its organisation and ticket distribution. Akhilesh keeps expanding the meaning of PDA Akhilesh is not limiting the PDA formula to Yadavs, Muslims and Dalits. To strengthen caste-based mobilisation, he has expanded the meanings of its letters. He has said that 'P' stands for 'Pandit', while 'A' can mean 'Agra', 'Aadhi Aabadi' (women), 'Agarwal', 'Adivasi' and 'Annadata' (farmers). The strategy is aimed at making inroads into the BJP's core vote bank. Akhilesh is also planning visits to Ayodhya's Shri Ram Temple and Mathura in December to challenge the BJP on the issue of Hindutva. What is the BJP doing to counter this? Yogi and Shah's counter: 'No curfew, no riots' The BJP's top leadership began preparing its counter to caste-based politics as early as July 2024. The party's brainstorming meeting, being held in Mathura on 16 and 17 November, is also discussing how to shift the election focus away from caste and towards Hindutva, nationalism and law and order. Slogans convey a message of unity Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's slogan, "If we are divided, we will be cut down; if we stay united, we will remain strong", and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's slogan, "If we are united, we are safe", have set the tone for preventing the division of Hindu votes. The RSS is also working to take this campaign to the ground. Major UCC move Union Home Minister Amit Shah has made it clear at a state executive committee meeting that the Uniform Civil Code will be implemented in Uttar Pradesh if the BJP forms the government for a third consecutive term. Yogi's aggressive Hindutva pitch In his speeches, Chief Minister Yogi has adopted an aggressive stance, recalling the riots and alleged appeasement during the SP's rule. His key statements have raised the political temperature: According to senior journalist and political analyst Akhilesh Bajpai, caste equations have always played a decisive role in Uttar Pradesh politics. Whenever elections in the state have been fought on caste lines, the Hindutva card has weakened. The 1993 Assembly elections offer an example. After the Babri structure was demolished in 1992, the Hindutva wave was at its peak across northern India. However, in the 1993 Assembly elections, the SP-BSP alliance mobilised voters along caste lines with the slogan, 'Mulayam and Kanshi Ram have joined hands; Jai Shri Ram has been blown away', and formed a government with a clear majority. On the other hand, SP national president Akhilesh Yadav is also preparing to counter this strategy by inaugurating the Kedareshwar Temple in Etawah before the elections. After that, he will visit Ayodhya to seek the blessings of Ram Lalla, in an attempt to balance the issues being raised by the Opposition camp. Senior journalist Yogesh Kumar says that even after its defeat in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP's central leadership has not yet made it clear that it will not make Hindutva an election issue. This is because the political narrative has to be set in Delhi. The BJP, too, is forming alliances with caste-based political parties. The RLD, SBSP, Apna Dal (S) and Nishad Party are all caste-based parties.
