stories.title: Youth jumps into Gomti after girlfriend's marriage condition:She said he must earn ₹50,000 to marry her, he made a final call to friend in Jaunpur
stories.summary: A young man jumped into the Gomti River in Jaunpur after hearing his girlfriend's condition. The girl had said, "Earn ₹50,000 a month, and only then will I marry you. Otherwise, I will marry someone else." Divers have been searching for the young man for more than 18 hours. His brother has accused a girl from the city of blackmailing him. His brother said, "The two had been having an affair for about a year. At around 12 midnight on Sunday, my younger brother jumped into the river." The incident took place at Shahi Bridge in the Kotwali police station area. Read the full incident in sequence… Rahit Maurya (45) lives with his family in Gopalapur village under the Saraikhwaja police station. His family consists of his wife, Anju Maurya (42), three sons-Satyam Maurya (26), Shivam Maurya (22) and Sundaram Maurya (20)-and a daughter, Kajal (19). Rahit is a post office agent. His elder brother Shivam is married and works as a contractor at a brick kiln. His younger brother Shivam works in land plotting, while Sundaram was a third-year BA student. He video-called a friend and said, "I am going to jump" Sundaram left home at around 9 p.m. on Sunday night. He reached Shahi Bridge, 3 km away, at around midnight. From there, he video-called his friend, Praveen Maurya, and said, "I am going to jump into the Gomti. Tell my family." He hung up after saying this. After receiving the information from his friend, the family rushed to the spot. They immediately called the police as well. The police and divers had been searching for Sundaram since Monday morning. However, even after more than 18 hours, no trace of him could be found. Father says girl used to blackmail his son Sundaram's father, Rahit Maurya, said, "Sundaram had been having an affair for about a year with Naina, a constable's daughter. She used to harass him and pressure him to earn money. My son jumped from Shahi Bridge." The girl used to say, "Earn ₹50,000 a month" Sundaram's brother, Shivam Maurya, said, “A girl named Naina had been harassing my brother for several days. She told him, 'I will marry you only if you earn ₹50,000.'” My brother would tell me, my father and several others every day, "Brother, if you know of any work, please help me get it." City CO Samyak Chaudhary said- The initial investigation suggests that the case is related to a love affair. The complaint has been received. The investigation is underway, and the young man is also being searched for with the help of divers.

stories.title: BJP MLA Chandrabhanu Paswan injured in Ayodhya road accident:Fortuner collides with trailer, suffers serious head injury
stories.summary: Milkipur MLA Chandrabhanu Paswan was injured after his Fortuner car collided with a trailer in Ayodhya. The accident took place near Bhambhwa crossing in Rani Bazar, under the Poorakalandar police station area. Paswan suffered a head injury and was taken to the district hospital for treatment. The cause of the accident is not yet known. District Magistrate Shashank Tripathi reached the district hospital and spoke to officials to get details about the MLA's condition. Police have started efforts to trace the trailer and its driver. See three pictures below : Now read the full account विधायक Chandrabhanu Paswan was on his way to attend the Bharatkund festival. At 8:30 p.m., a trailer travelling from Prabhat Nagar towards Shahganj near Bhanbhawa Crossing in Ranibazar, under the jurisdiction of Purakalandar police station, collided violently with his Fortuner car. The collision struck the side of the car where the MLA was seated. The MLA suffered injuries to his head and leg in the accident. He was admitted to the district hospital after his head began bleeding, and is undergoing treatment there. According to eyewitnesses, the collision was so forceful that the MLA's Fortuner was damaged. After the accident, people ran to stop the trailer, but the driver increased the vehicle's speed and fled the scene. Driver's side used to get him out when gate would not open After the accident, the Fortuner's gate would not open. The MLA was therefore taken out through the driver's side. He was bleeding from the head and had also suffered an injury to his leg. He was then immediately taken to the district hospital. Following information about the incident, Ayodhya District Magistrate and the CO City reached the spot. Police are gathering information about the accident. A search is under way for the trailer and its driver. The MLA's condition is said to be out of danger. As soon as news of the incident spread, BJP leaders, workers and the MLA's supporters began arriving at the district hospital. District officials also reached the hospital and are gathering information about the MLA's health. While gathering information about the accident, police have begun efforts to trace the trailer and its driver. The cause of the accident is being investigated. Traffic around the crossroads was also affected for some time after the accident. Police restored normal conditions at the scene. Victory came in the February 2025 by-election Chandrabhanu Paswan defeated Samajwadi Party candidate Ajit Prasad by 61,710 votes in the by-election for the Milkipur Assembly seat. Paswan received 1,46,397 votes, while Ajit Prasad received 84,687 votes. Ajit Prasad is the son of Awadhesh Prasad, the Samajwadi Party MP from Faizabad. The Milkipur Assembly seat fell vacant after Awadhesh Prasad won the 2024 Lok Sabha election from the Faizabad seat. Notably, in the 2022 Assembly election, Milkipur was the only seat in Ayodhya district where the BJP was defeated. The story is being updated.

stories.title: Soldier dies after being shot 8 days before wedding:Was posted in Kupwara; father says two bullets hit his head
stories.summary: An Army soldier from Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh, died after being shot while on duty in Kupwara, Jammu and Kashmir, on Sunday evening. He was hit by two bullets in the head. The Army informed his family about his death at around 7 am on Monday. The news left the family members in tears. The soldier was due to get married on November 24, while his engagement ceremony was scheduled for November 22. The wedding invitations had already been distributed, and preparations were underway to welcome guests at home. The family had been waiting for the soldier to return home on Monday. Now, they are waiting for his body to arrive at the same house. However, the circumstances in which the soldier died and how he was shot are not yet known. Karan joined the Army in 2020, was posted in Kupwara Pappu Singh, a resident of Sirsa village in the Chharra police station area, works in agriculture. Karan was the youngest of his three children. His elder brother, Sanjay Chaudhary, is also an Army soldier, while his sister is married. Karan Chaudhary, 25, joined the Army in 2020. After completing his training in Ranchi, he was posted to the Leh Glacier for his first assignment. He was later posted to Lohlam in Kupwara, Jammu and Kashmir, for his second and third assignments. He was serving with the 22 Rashtriya Rifles (RR) Battalion. Family members said they had spoken to Karan on 14 November. He told them that he would take a flight from Srinagar on 16 November and reach Delhi. He planned to travel to the village from there. He was also due to receive leave-related documents from the headquarters. Death caused by two bullets to the head; reason unclear His father, Pappu Singh, said the battalion's commanding officer informed him of Karan's death at around 7 a.m. on Monday. He was told that Karan had suffered two bullet wounds to the head. However, no information was provided about how he was shot. The family was only informed that their son had been martyred. As soon as they heard the news of his death, panic swept through the family. His relatives began crying inconsolably. The family is demanding that the Army headquarters and officials clarify the cause of his death. Engagement on 22 November, wedding scheduled for 24 November The father said that preparations for Karan's wedding were almost complete. The match was arranged in April after the girl was shown to the family over a video call. A family meeting and engagement were scheduled to take place in the village on 22 November, while the wedding procession was to depart from a guest house in Atrauli on 24 November. The wedding invitations had been distributed. Preparations for the clothes, other items and decorations had also been completed. Relatives had begun visiting the family. They had hoped that Karan would return home and take part in the wedding preparations. But the house from which the wedding procession was to leave eight days later is now filled with mourning. Body to be brought to Delhi tonight after post-mortem According to information, Karan's body will be brought to Delhi tonight after the post-mortem. It is likely to reach his village, Sirsa, by Tuesday morning. However, the official confirmation of the final timing has not yet been received. Ataruli SDM Saurabh Kumar Gupta said he was informed of the soldier's death on Monday morning. The administration has not yet received the official time for the body to reach the village. Further information will be provided once an update is received. Preparations to welcome athlete Gulveer Singh also affected Sirsa is also the village of international athlete Gulveer Singh. Preparations had been under way for Gulveer's arrival in the village and his welcome. The villagers were excited, but news of Karan's death plunged the entire village into mourning. The villagers are now waiting for the mortal remains of their young son to reach the village.

stories.title: Raja Bhaiya drives Dhirendra Shastri to Raj Bhavan:Grand welcome at airport, Kalash Yatra held in 200 villages of Kunda
stories.summary: Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, head of Bageshwar Dham, arrived at Prayagraj airport at around 5 pm on Monday. He was welcomed by Raghuraj Pratap Singh, also known as Raja Bhaiya, president of Jansatta Dal Loktantrik and MLA from Kunda. Raja Bhaiya then drove Shastri himself to the Raj Mahal in Kunda, Pratapgarh. Dhirendra Shastri will offer prayers at the Hanuman temple before resting at Panchvati. A three-day Shri Ram Katha will begin on November 17 at the parade ground of Benti Raj Bhavan in Kunda. A Divya Darbar will also be held on November 20. Mahant Raju Das of Hanumangarhi in Ayodhya also reached Kunda on Monday. Kalash Yatras pass through 200 villages Ahead of the Shri Ram Katha, grand Kalash Yatras were taken out from eight different locations in eight directions at 8 am. Raja Bhaiya's two sons, Shivraj Pratap Singh and Brijraj Pratap Singh, led the processions in different areas. More than 1,500 vehicles and over one lakh devotees took part in the processions. The yatras passed through around 200 villages and 50 towns. Devotees welcomed the processions at several places, and flowers were showered on them from bulldozers. All the processions reached Benti Raj Bhavan in the evening. First, see the pictures of Prayagraj Airport... See pictures from the urn procession : Shriram Katha to be held across 200 bighas, 1 lakh devotees will be able to listen at once Preparations for the Shriram Katha have been completed at the event venue spread across around 200 bighas in Kunda, Pratapgarh. According to the organisers, around 1 lakh devotees will be able to listen to the Katha at the same time. A 550-foot-long and 100-foot-wide waterproof main tent has been erected for this purpose. In addition, two large tents and a separate tent for the Katha Vyas are being prepared. Tent traders from Banaras are decorating the venue. Parking at 12 locations, 3,000 volunteers to manage arrangements In view of the large crowd of devotees, parking facilities have been arranged at 12 locations around the venue. Around 3,000 volunteers will manage the arrangements. Seating, food, security and traffic arrangements are being made. Around 100 confectioners and artisans and 500 labourers are working in the kitchen, pandal and other arrangements. Food being prepared for 50,000 people daily According to the organisers, food and prasad will be arranged for around 50,000 devotees every day. They will be served vegetarian puri and vegetables. This will require 40 to 50 quintals of potatoes, 12 to 15 quintals of tomatoes, 10 to 15 quintals of seasonal vegetables and 2 to 2.5 quintals of coriander and ginger every day. Raja Bhaiya has instructed the workers that if anyone falls ill in the pandal, they should immediately take the person to a doctor without creating a commotion. Preparations for the event are being carried out in different stages under the leadership of chief organiser Hariom Srivastava.

stories.title: Ankit murder case shooters wore bulletproof jackets before entering UP:Got handcuffed and chained; told judge they feared an encounter by UP Police
stories.summary: Two shooters accused in the murder of Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan were brought to the Kairana court in Shamli at around 12 pm on Monday. Both were wearing bulletproof jackets, handcuffs on their hands and shackles on their feet. They were brought to Shamli from Tihar Jail on the orders of Delhi's Patiala House Court. Around 40 police personnel from Delhi and Shamli were deployed during the hearing. The entire process was also videographed. On November 3, the two accused had sought protection from the Patiala House Court, saying they feared a fake encounter. They told the court that they should be made to wear handcuffs, shackles and bulletproof jackets while being taken to Shamli in Uttar Pradesh, as they feared that the UP Police could stage an encounter. View 2 photos Now, understand the full case Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan was shot dead on the evening of 26 August while returning home from the gym on the Aryapuri Nala track in Shamli. Five days after the incident, on 31 August, police killed two shooters involved in the murder, Mohit and Sumit, in an encounter. Police also named gangster Rakesh alias Pampu, who is lodged in Karnal jail, and Yogesh Tunda, Deepak Dabas and Dinesh Karalia, shooters for the Lawrence Bishnoi and Gogi gangs lodged in Tihar jail, as accused in the conspiracy to murder him. Ordered to be produced on 16 November for remand Last month, Yogesh Tunda and Deepak Dabas, who are lodged in Tihar jail, were produced before the court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate in Kairana. Shamli police obtained their remand in connection with the conspiracy to murder Ankit Baliyan. After this, police submitted an application to the court seeking police custody remand. The court then ordered that both men be produced on Monday, 16 November. Delhi Police also remained deployed Following an order from Patiala House Court, the two were brought from Tihar Jail to Kairana in a prisoner escort vehicle at around 12 noon on Monday. Officials from the Delhi Police, Shamli Police and Kairana Police were present with heavy security arrangements. Taken back under tight security After being taken out of the prisoner escort vehicle, the two shooters were first taken to the court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate. However, as the file had been transferred, they were later produced before the court of the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate. After the court proceedings were completed, the Delhi Police took both of them back to Tihar Jail under tight security. Married 6 Years Ago, Wife Is a Government Teacher Ankit Baliyan was a resident of Bantikhhera village in Shamli. He lived in Sonipat, Haryana. However, he had been living in his village with his family for the past several months. His father, Satbir, is a retired army personnel, while his mother, Amresh, is a homemaker. Ankit was the youngest of four siblings. He married Seema six years ago. Seema is a government teacher in Delhi. The couple had no children.

stories.title: Congress seeks 181 seats from Akhilesh in UP:SP claims 30 seats in Uttarakhand in return; pressure politics ahead of first meeting
stories.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi will launch the party's election campaign in Uttar Pradesh on December 10. An Assembly constituency in the Purvanchal region has been selected for the launch. Senior state Congress leaders have been asked to start preparations. A meeting of senior Uttar Pradesh Congress leaders was held at party president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence in Delhi on Monday. The meeting discussed the strategy for the Assembly elections, strengthening the party organisation, the campaign and seat-sharing with the Samajwadi Party (SP). Priyanka Gandhi given key role in seat-sharing talks After the meeting, state Congress president Aradhana Mishra 'Mona' said that preparations for the Assembly elections were discussed with the party president. She added that the election campaign in the state would begin in December. According to party sources, Congress has formed a special committee to hold formal talks with the Samajwadi Party on seat-sharing. Priyanka Gandhi will lead the committee. Aradhana Mishra 'Mona', Rajendra Pal Gautam and Imran Masood have been included as members. Key meeting with Akhilesh on 17 November According to sources, Rahul Gandhi said at the meeting that the SP is an important ally in the alliance. Therefore, the seats should be divided in a way that allows all the parties to work together and ensures that no one feels they have been treated unfairly. Congress leader Aradhana Mishra 'Mona' said that an important meeting on seat-sharing is scheduled with SP chief Akhilesh Yadav on 17 November. However, it has not yet been decided whether the meeting will be held in Delhi or Lucknow. A decision is also pending on which leaders will attend it. Aradhana Mishra made it clear that no final decision has yet been taken on the seats. The possibility of winning each seat will be discussed at the upcoming meeting. Preparing to Launch Election Campaign from Noida Congress is preparing to create an election atmosphere across Uttar Pradesh from 10 December, travelling through Purvanchal. According to party sources, the campaign could begin from the land of Gautam Buddha. Discussions are under way on holding an event in Purvanchal for this purpose. There are also indications that a senior leader from the OBC community may be given responsibility for preparing the campaign and building coordination among the people. Alongside this, the party also discussed forming an election committee and a campaign committee. Names for these committees are to be sent to the state team. Meanwhile, preparations are also under way to form a new team for the state Congress. In other words, before the election, Congress is working to strengthen its organisation afresh. List of 181 Seats Goes Viral on Social Media Meanwhile, a list of 181 Assembly seats is going viral on social media. It is being claimed that the Congress has handed this list to the Samajwadi Party. However, the Congress has not yet confirmed the list. According to the viral list, it includes 135 general seats, 45 Scheduled Caste seats and one Scheduled Tribe seat. The list also includes the names of all 10 seats in Rae Bareli and Amethi, which are considered traditional Congress strongholds. These include Rae Bareli Sadar, Bachhrawan, Harchandpur, Salon, Sareni, Unchahar, Tiloi, Jagdishpur, Gauriganj and Amethi. In addition, the list names Assembly seats from different parts of Uttar Pradesh: Western UP- Nakur, Saharanpur Nagar, Saharanpur Dehat, Rampur Maniharan, Thanabhawan, Budhana, Purqazi, Meerapur, Barhapur, Dhampur, Najibabad, Moradabad Nagar, Kundarki, Chandausi, Swar, Dhanaura, Naugawan Sadat, Hasanpur, Siwal Khas, Hastinapur, Meerut South, Baghpat, Loni, Modinagar, Dhaulana, Hapur, Garhmukteshwar, Bulandshahr, Shikarpur, Khair, Koil, Iglas, Mant, Mathura, Baldev, Agra Rural, Fatehpur Sikri, Kheragarh, Bah, Tundla and Firozabad. Rohilkhand- Budaun, Dataganj, Meerganj, Nawabganj, Faridpur, Bareilly Cantonment, Aonla, Pilibhit, Puranpur, Tilhar and Shahjahanpur. Central UP- Palia, Gola Gokrannath, Mohammadi, Sitapur, Laharpur, Biswan, Sevta, Mahmoodabad, Sidhauli, Shahabad, Bilgram, Bangarmau, Malihabad, Bakshi Ka Talab, Sarojini Nagar, Lucknow East, Mohanlalganj, Sultanpur, Sadar, Lambhua, Farrukhabad, Auraiya, Akbarpur Raniya, Bilhaur, Bithoor, Govind Nagar, Kidwai Nagar, Kanpur Cantonment, Ghatampur, Kursi, Zaidpur, Dariyabad and Haidergarh. Bundelkhand- Kalpi, Orai, Jhansi Nagar, Mauranipur, Mahrauni, Hamirpur, Rath, Naraini and Manikpur. Purvanchal and other areas- Jehanabad, Bindki, Ayan Shah, Hussainganj, Rampur Khas, Vishwanathganj, Pratapgarh Sadar, Chail, Phulpur, Karachhana, Allahabad North, Allahabad South, Bara, Koraon, Bikapur, Katehari, Balha, Nanpara, Mahsi, Utraula, Balrampur, Gaura, Shohratgarh, Harraiya, Mahadeva, Khalilabad, Pharenda, Nautanwa, Maharajganj, Paniyara, Gorakhpur Rural, Bansgaon, Chillupar, Khadda, Fazilnagar, Rudrapur, Deoria, Pathardeva, Rampur Karkhana, Salempur, Barhaj, Nizamabad, Madhuban, Belthara Road, Ballia Nagar, Badlapur, Jaunpur, Zafarabad, Jakhanian, Zahoorabad, Gyanpur, Aurai, Chhanbey and Dudhi. Preparations for seat-sharing based on feedback According to Congress sources, the party has shortlisted around 181 assembly seats based on ground reports, its performance in previous elections, the state of the organisation and information received from local leaders. Party leaders have also given their views on seats in areas where Aradhana Mishra, Rajendra Pal Gautam and Imran Masood hold influence. Congress claims that the political climate in its favour has changed in several areas over the past few months. According to sources, the party has also prepared a formula for seat-sharing: 2024 Lok Sabha Results and 2022 Assembly Performance Senior Congress leader Pramod Tiwari has cited the party's performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha election in connection with its claims to the seats. According to him, despite the Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance not campaigning extensively in the Lok Sabha election, the alliance won 43 of Uttar Pradesh's 80 Lok Sabha seats. According to the figures for the Assembly constituencies, the Samajwadi Party was leading in 183 seats and the Congress in 39. On this basis, Congress leaders believe that the alliance could be in a strong position in more than 215 seats in the Assembly elections. On the other hand, political sources say that there is confusion within the Samajwadi Party camp over the Congress demanding more seats. The main reason is the Congress's performance in the 2022 Assembly elections. The party received 2.33% of the vote in that election and could win only two seats. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has already said that seat-sharing in the alliance will be based on the likelihood of victory. Senior leaders will take the final decision after discussions between committees of the two parties. Three major alliances for the elections in Uttar Pradesh So far, three major alliances have emerged in the state for the 2027 Assembly elections- 1. NDA alliance- The BJP-led alliance includes Apna Dal (Soneylal), the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD), the Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) and the Nishad Party. According to sources, the BJP is considering a proposal to leave around 60 seats for its alliance partners. 2. SP-Congress alliance- The two parties are in talks to contest the 2027 election together. Discussions on seat-sharing between the two parties are likely to begin from 17 November. 3. Social Change Front- Chandrashekhar Azad's Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) and Asaduddin Owaisi's AIMIM have announced that they will contest the election together. stories.title: 16 IAS transferred in UP; 6 district magistrates changed:Varanasi Kanpur commissioners exchanged positions
stories.summary: The Yogi government transferred 16 senior IAS officers in Uttar Pradesh on Monday evening. The district magistrates (DMs) of Bhadohi, Chandauli, Gonda, Jaunpur, Shravasti and Shamli were transferred as part of the reshuffle. The divisional commissioners of Varanasi and Kanpur were also changed. The chief executive officers (CEOs) of the Greater Noida Authority and the Uttar Pradesh State Industrial Development Authority (UPSIDA) were also exchanged. See the IAS transfer list below : 5 key points from UP's IAS reshuffle: 6 districts get new DMs, Varanasi-Kanpur commissioners exchanged 1. Varanasi and Kanpur get new divisional commissioners K. Vijeyendra Pandian has been shifted from Kanpur and appointed the divisional commissioner of Varanasi. Meanwhile, Varanasi's divisional commissioner, S. Rajalingam, will now take charge in Kanpur. 2. Greater Noida and UPSIDA CEOs exchanged Greater Noida Authority CEO Ravi Kumar NG has been appointed CEO of UPSIDA. Dr Balkar Singh, who was the UPSIDA CEO, will now take charge of the Greater Noida Authority. 3. Six districts get new DMs; Umesh Mishra gets new posting within three days The government has changed the DMs of Bhadohi, Chandauli, Gonda, Jaunpur, Shravasti and Shamli. The Jaunpur posting is notable. On November 13, Umesh Mishra was removed as the DM of Muzaffarnagar and appointed Special Secretary. Just three days later, he was made the DM of Jaunpur. 4. Officers who served as DMs get new responsibilities Dr Samuel Paul N., who was the DM of Jaunpur, has been shifted to the Cooperation Department. Gonda DM Priyanka Niranjan has been posted to the Urban Development Department, while Shravasti DM Annapurna Garg has been moved to the Women and Child Development and Nutrition Department. Chandauli DM Chandra Mohan Garg has been appointed Special Secretary to the Chief Minister. Shamli DM Alok Yadav has been shifted to the IT and Electronics Department. 5. Labour Commissioner Soumya Agarwal gets charge of several organisations Labour Commissioner Soumya Agarwal has been appointed Managing Director of the State Textile Corporation, State Spinning Company, State Yarn Company and Cooperative Spinning Mills Federation. She has also been appointed CEO of the Uttar Pradesh Textile and Apparel Park. Ramesh Ranjan returns as DM after allegations Ramesh Ranjan has been appointed the District Magistrate (DM) of Gonda. Before this, he was posted in Lucknow as Additional Commissioner of Land Management in the Board of Revenue. In April 2026, Ranjan was the DM of Firozabad. During his tenure, the then Tundla tehsildar, Rakhi Sharma, made serious allegations of corruption and harassment against him and some staff members of his office. Sharma had alleged before the media that she was given an iPhone worth ₹1.75 lakh and an Apple Watch in exchange for putting pressure on her in a land-related case and closing an inquiry against her. She also claimed that her salary had been withheld for eight months. She had to approach the Allahabad High Court over the issue. However, the DM office employees' association called the allegations baseless. The matter also reached the court in June 2026. Priyanka Niranjan was in the news during minister's protest in Gonda Priyanka Niranjan has been appointed Special Secretary in the Urban Development Department. She was earlier the DM of Gonda. She came into the spotlight in September 2026 after the murder of businessman Vinod Sahni, who was in the utensils trade. Protesting the murder, Cabinet Minister Dr Sanjay Nishad staged a sit-in at the Gonda Collectorate against his own government and the administration. DM Priyanka Niranjan reached the spot to handle the situation and persuade the minister to end the protest. She sat on the ground with him and held talks. The protest ended after the administration assured strict action against those responsible and support for the victim's family. Niranjan was also in the news for efforts to revive the Noon River in Jalaun and the Manorama River in Basti. The Prime Minister had praised these efforts. Soumya Agarwal was in the news over Shankaracharya-related dispute at Magh Mela Soumya Agarwal has been appointed Managing Director of the Uttar Pradesh State Textile Corporation Limited. She has also been given charge of the State Spinning Company, State Yarn Company and the Cooperative Spinning Mills Federation, among other responsibilities. Before this, she was serving as Labour Commissioner. In January 2026, she came into the political spotlight over a dispute involving Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand during the Magh Mela in Prayagraj. At the time, Agarwal was the Commissioner of Prayagraj division. A dispute had taken place over arrangements at the fair, the bathing of saints and permission for vehicles. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav questioned the administration over the issue. Agarwal later held a press conference to present the administration's side. She denied that any saint had been insulted.

stories.title: Cakes pastries to be inspected in UP:Action to be taken against use of chemicals and banned colours
stories.summary: Food businesses in Uttar Pradesh that make and sell bread, biscuits, cakes, pastries, cookies, chocolates and candies will now face stricter checks. Action will be taken against those using poor-quality raw materials, banned colours or making false claims about products. Units operating in unhygienic conditions will also face action. The Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) has issued instructions for the storage, production, packing and sale of bakery and confectionery products. Manufacturing units, as well as counters at cafes and shops, will be inspected. Raw material quality to be checked Raw materials such as refined flour, flour, cocoa powder, eggs, nuts, margarine and shortening will have to undergo regular quality checks. Materials showing signs of mould, colour changes, bad smell, contamination or adulteration must be separated immediately. Perishable items such as milk, custard and pastry fillings must be stored and transported at the required temperature. Products with a shelf life of less than seven days must also carry a use-by date. Banned colours and chemicals not allowed The use of industrial colours such as Rhodamine B, Metanil Yellow and Sudan dyes to make food products look attractive is prohibited. Chemicals such as potassium bromate, potassium iodate, formalin, boric acid and salicylic acid cannot be used in food products. Only approved food colours and preservatives can be used, and that too within the permitted limits. Clean production areas made compulsory Bakery walls, floors and ceilings must be easy to clean. Proper arrangements for water drainage and waste disposal must also be made. Employees must wear aprons, hairnets and gloves. Only safe drinking water should be used for cleaning. Separate areas must be provided for receiving raw materials, preparation, baking, cooling, packing and storage. This will help prevent contamination between different food products. All equipment, including mixers, ovens, trays and moulds, must be made of food-grade material. Rules for bread ingredients and labels Whole wheat bread must contain at least 75% whole wheat flour out of the total flour used. Multigrain bread must contain at least 20% approved grains other than wheat. Milk bread must have at least 6% milk solids. Bread sold as oat, bran, honey or fruit bread must contain the required amount of the ingredient mentioned in its name. Adding colour to ordinary bread and selling it as brown or whole wheat bread will not be allowed. Complete details must be printed on packets Food packets must carry the product name, list of ingredients, allergen details, nutritional information, vegetarian or non-vegetarian mark, batch number, manufacturing date and expiry date. The 14-digit FSSAI licence number must also be printed on the packet. Information about allergens such as milk, soya, gluten and nuts must be clearly mentioned. Cake boards, paper cups, wrappers and takeaway boxes must be made of food-grade material. Newspapers and printed paper cannot be used to wrap food items. The trans fat content in vegetable fats, margarine and shortening must not exceed 2%. Claims such as sugar-free, preservative-free, organic and healthy will also be checked. Cafe and shop counters also under inspection Unpacked cakes, pastries, muffins, cookies and bread must be kept in glass display cases or covered with food-grade material. This will protect them from dust, flies and direct contact with customers. Cake-cutting knives, trays and other equipment must be cleaned and sanitised regularly. Separate equipment must be used for raw and ready-to-eat food. In cafes, milk must be stored at the required temperature, and safe drinking water must be used in ice makers. Coffee machines, blenders and juicers must also be cleaned regularly. Licences and purchase records to be checked Businesses must have the food safety licence or registration required for their operations. They must maintain purchase bills, batch numbers and supplier details for items such as refined flour, sugar, milk solids, fats, food colours and flavours. Records of product batches, recipes, ingredients and shelf life must also be available for inspection. Officials may also ask for employees' medical records, drinking water test reports, and pest control and temperature records. Businesses must have a system to immediately recall any product found unsafe in the market. They must also maintain complete records of where such products were supplied.

stories.title: Major reshuffle in Gorakhpur Police Range ahead of elections:67 inspectors transferred across 4 districts, most from Gorakhpur; see full list
stories.summary: Large-scale transfers of inspectors have been carried out in the Gorakhpur police range amid preparations for the Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh. On 15 November, Deputy Inspector General Dr S. Channappa ordered 67 inspectors from four districts to be transferred to other districts after completing three years in their current postings. The transferred inspectors include 21 from Gorakhpur, 15 from Deoria, 20 from Kushinagar and 11 from Maharajganj. Kushinagar has gained the most from the transfers. Twenty-four inspectors will arrive there from other districts, while 20 have been sent to other districts. Gorakhpur has seen the departure of the highest number of inspectors, at 21. Of these, 11 have been sent to Deoria, nine to Kushinagar and one to Maharajganj. Eleven inspectors from other districts will arrive in Gorakhpur. The DIG has directed the SSPs and SPs of all the districts to immediately relieve the transferred inspectors. All the inspectors will then take charge in their newly assigned districts. Those who have completed three years of posting in four years to be transferred The DIG office has carried out these transfers under instructions issued by the Lucknow headquarters on 29 October. In view of the elections, inspectors whose three-year posting in the same district over the past four years will be completed by 31 May 2027 have been sent to other districts. The transfer list was prepared on the basis of information received from Gorakhpur, Deoria, Kushinagar and Maharajganj districts. It is believed that preparations are under way to change the postings of police personnel before the Assembly elections to ensure that the electoral process remains fair and transparent. 21 inspectors transferred out of Gorakhpur, 11 to be posted According to the transfer list, 21 inspectors have been transferred from Gorakhpur to other districts. Of these, 11 will go to Deoria, nine to Kushinagar and one to Maharajganj. Meanwhile, 11 inspectors will come to Gorakhpur from other districts. They include Amit Kumar Rai and Santosh Kumar Srivastava from Deoria. Shakil Ahmed, Manoj Kumar Pant, Harshvardhan Singh, Ravindra Nath Singh, Vidyadhar Kushwaha, Manmohan Mishra and Raju Singh have been transferred to Gorakhpur from Kushinagar. In addition, Satyendra Kumar Rai and Manoj Kumar Rai have been posted to Gorakhpur from Maharajganj. 15 transferred from Deoria, 18 inspectors to be posted A total of 15 inspectors have been transferred from Deoria district. Of these, six have been sent to Maharajganj, seven to Kushinagar and two to Gorakhpur. Those transferred from Deoria to Maharajganj include Chaturmuj Pandey, Rahul Singh, Kalyan Singh Sagar, Dileep Kumar Pandey, Rakesh Singh and Durgesh Kumar Singh. Meanwhile, the inspectors sent to Kushinagar include Vijay Pratap Singh, Santosh Kumar, Rambhavan Yadav, Uday Shankar Singh Kushwaha, Vinod Kumar Singh, Sunil Kumar and Shriram Yadav. On the other hand, Deoria will receive 18 inspectors from other districts. These include 11 from Gorakhpur, six from Kushinagar and one from Maharajganj. Kushinagar gets the highest number of 24 inspectors In the transfers, Kushinagar district has received the highest number of inspectors, 24. Twenty inspectors from the district have been sent to other districts. Seven inspectors from Kushinagar will go to Gorakhpur, seven to Maharajganj and six to Deoria. Those arriving in Gorakhpur include Shakeel Ahmad, Manoj Kumar Pant, Harshvardhan Singh, Ravindra Nath Singh, Vidyadhar Kushwaha, Manmohan Mishra and Raju Singh. The inspectors sent to Maharajganj include Divyijay Narayan Rai, Satya Prakash Singh, Bhaiya Chhavinath Singh, Anil Kumar Yadav, Sanjay Dubey and Ramchandra Ram, among others. Kushinagar will receive nine inspectors from Gorakhpur, seven from Deoria and eight from Maharajganj. Maharajganj sends out 11, receives 14 new inspectors A total of 11 inspectors have been transferred from Maharajganj district to other districts. Eight have been sent to Kushinagar, two to Gorakhpur and one to Deoria. Meanwhile, 14 inspectors from other districts will arrive in Maharajganj. They include one from Gorakhpur, six from Deoria and seven from Kushinagar. At a glance - how many were sent from each district District | Sent | Received | Where the most were sent Gorakhpur | 21 | 11 | Deoria - 11 Deoria | 15 | 18 | Kushinagar - 7 Kushinagar | 20 | 24 | Gorakhpur - 7, Maharajganj - 7 Maharajganj | 11 | 14 | Kushinagar - 8 Total: A total of 67 inspectors have been transferred, and 67 will arrive from other districts. Instructions issued to relieve them immediately; sub-inspectors may be next The DIG office has directed the SSPs and SPs of all four districts to immediately relieve the transferred inspectors and send a report on this.

stories.title: Two senior SP leaders clash at party meeting in Gorakhpur:Outgoing district president Brijesh Gautam and Dakku exchange heated words, nearly coming to blows
stories.summary: The dispute within the Samajwadi Party in Gorakhpur shows no sign of ending. Infighting among the party leaders has now come out into the open. During a meeting on Sunday, former city president Zafar Amin Dakku and outgoing district president Brajesh Gautam got into a heated argument. The two first exchanged insults before the matter escalated into a physical altercation. Other SP leaders present at the spot intervened and separated them. The situation calmed down afterwards. Samajwadi Party national president Akhilesh Yadav is scheduled to visit Gorakhpur on 18 November. He is scheduled to attend an event in Devkahi village in the Chauri Chaura Assembly constituency. He will attend a condolence meeting organised here to mark the 10th death anniversary of Vinay Kumar Singh Binnu, former general secretary of the Gorakhpur University Students' Union. He will also unveil a statue of Bandhu Singh, a hero of the 1857 uprising. Party leaders have stepped up preparations for the programme. As part of the preparations, a meeting was convened at the office of Vinay Kumar Singh Binnu's younger brother, Ajay Kumar Singh Tappu, on Sunday. Former city president Zafar Amin Dakku and outgoing district president Brajesh Gautam also attended. During the meeting, the resentment that had been brewing between the two surfaced. It is being reported that during the conversation, Dakku asked Brajesh Gautam about his displeasure over his photograph not being printed on the hoarding. He said Brajesh had described the absence of his photograph on the hoarding as an insult because he was a Dalit. During this, Dakku addressed Brajesh as "tum". Brajesh Gautam objected to this. An argument then broke out between the two over the issue. The verbal exchange quickly escalated and the matter turned physical. Leaders present at the spot intervened and managed to bring the situation under control. Dakku said: Tappu Singh's event was a private affair Former metropolitan president Zafar Amin Dakku said that at the meeting held on 13 November, Brajesh Gautam had expressed displeasure over his photograph not being included on the hoarding. According to Dakku, this is Ajay Kumar Singh Tappu's personal programme. The national president has appointed him as the programme's in-charge. Therefore, responsibility for the programme rests with him. He also described the allegations of hijacking the programme as baseless. Brajesh says, 'He had objected to being addressed as 'tum'' Meanwhile, outgoing district president Brajesh Gautam said that he had objected to Zafar Amin Dakku addressing him as 'tum'. He rejected the allegation that he had expressed displeasure over his photograph not being included on the hoarding. However, Brajesh Gautam denied having any kind of dispute with Dakku. Vijay Bahadur and Dakku given responsibility for the public meeting Former MLA Vijay Bahadur Yadav and Zafar Amin Dakku have been assigned responsibility for making Akhilesh Yadav's proposed programme a success. The two leaders have been tasked with mobilising crowds for the public meeting and overseeing the programme's arrangements. Ajay Kumar Singh Tappu said the national president himself had asked that these leaders be given responsibility for the programme. Hoardings are being put up in the city and surrounding areas to publicise the programme. They prominently feature the national president Akhilesh Yadav's photograph and name. He said preparations for the 18 November programme were almost complete.

stories.title: Queues stretch for 1 km outside KGMU OPD:Patients sit on the ground waiting for their turn; crowds had been thinner during the festive season
stories.summary: Patients poured in after the OPDs at the medical university and government hospitals in Lucknow opened on Monday. At KGMU, patients began queuing as early as 5 a.m. A queue stretching for around 1 kilometre formed outside the new OPD. Before this, patient numbers in the OPDs had remained low for nearly a week due to Diwali and Chhath Puja. Large numbers of patients reached the campus early in the morning After the OPD building opened at 8 a.m., patients and their attendants began entering. They then had to struggle to obtain tokens and see the doctor. The heavy crowd led to chaotic conditions in the OPD. Long wait for registration Doctors were on duty in almost all the major departments at KGMU, but the number of patients was so high that many had to wait for hours. Patients who had come from distant areas and their attendants faced the greatest difficulties. Before that, registration had taken considerable time.

stories.title: Why was Azam Khan arrested? High Court questions ED:5-hour hearing ends, verdict on bail tomorrow
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court heard Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan’s bail plea for five hours on Monday. His son Abdullah also appeared in court. The ED and Kapil Sibal argued over whether the grounds of arrest had been communicated to Azam. Sibal said Azam had not refused to accept the documents. However, ED advocate Hussain said the refusal had been recorded in the remand application and the panchnama. He said that when they asked Azam to provide details of his relatives while explaining the grounds of arrest, he replied that all his relatives had passed away. The ED also showed a video in court. Calling it a case of political vendetta, Sibal said there was an attempt to keep Azam in jail until the 2024 elections earlier and now until the 2027 elections. Hussain argued that the arrest had been made in accordance with the law. The investigation identified Azam as the founder and chairman of the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust. He had complete control over the university, Hussain said. The court has directed the ED to file an affidavit by 17 November. It has asked the agency to mention in it that it had offered to provide the grounds of arrest and that Azam had refused to accept them. The court will pass an appropriate order tomorrow. Earlier, a special PMLA court in Ghaziabad sent Azam to judicial custody until 26 November. He was produced before the court around five hours before the end of his four-day ED remand. During this time, Azam waved at his supporters and acknowledged their greetings. Akhilesh Yadav posted on X in support of Azam Khan. He said: Azam is being subjected to continuous injustice. The people of not just Uttar Pradesh but the entire country will respond to this when the time comes. Power does not remain in anyone's hands forever.

stories.title: Mother and son carrying father's ashes killed in Barabanki:Dumper runs over them and drags them 300 metres; father died 8 days ago
stories.summary: A mother and her son died in Barabanki on Monday while travelling to immerse the ashes of the family's deceased patriarch. The father had died eight days ago. On Monday, the son was taking his mother to Ayodhya on a motorcycle with his father's ashes. On the way, a speeding dumper truck hit their motorcycle head-on. The impact was so severe that the bike got trapped under the truck's wheels and was dragged for 300 metres. The son's one leg was severed, while the mother's body was crushed against the road. The accident took place near Bhanmau Crossing in the Kothi police station area, 15 km from the district headquarters. Police reached the spot after receiving information. They had to scrape the mother's remains off the road and collect them in a polythene bag. The son's severed leg was found 10 metres away from his body. The deceased have been identified as Sarvesh Verma (36) and his mother, Sharmavati (65). They had left their home in Paradipu village in the Zaidpur area in the morning to immerse the ashes in the Saryu river. The accident occurred just 10 km from their home. See pictures of the incident Here is the complete sequence of events Shiv Kumar (70), a resident of Paradipu village in the Nanmau police station area, died on 7 November after a prolonged illness. He is survived by his wife, Sharmavati, and five sons. The sons performed their father's last rites the day after his death. On Monday, the family was to travel to Ayodhya to immerse his ashes. Sarvesh, the third son, left home on a motorcycle with his mother in the morning. However, on the way, an out-of-control dumper truck loaded with soil ran them over. Just half an hour later, the family received news of their deaths. The household was plunged into grief, and relatives were inconsolable. The bodies are currently being sent for post-mortem examination. News is being updated.....

stories.title: Son masterminds theft at former Ranji player's home:Dispute over cricket with father; friends steal jewellery and cash worth ₹11.50 lakh
stories.summary: The conspiracy behind the theft at the Meerut home of a former Ranji player was hatched by his 14-year-old son. He did not want to pursue a career in cricket, while his father was pressuring him to play the sport. The two had been arguing over this. In anger, the father had warned his son that he would disinherit him. Upset by this, the boy planned the theft with two of his friends. The boy gave his friends the keys to the house. The two then stole ₹11.50 lakh in cash and jewellery from the house. After the incident, the boy himself called his father and informed him about the theft. Police solved the case within three hours late on Sunday evening. The incident took place under Nauchandi police station. Police detained the minor boy and both his friends and recovered the stolen goods. See 3 pictures... Now read the full details of the case.. Former Ranji Trophy player Ashu Sharma, a resident of Shastrinagar Sector 13, is employed by the Railways under the sports quota. He is currently posted at Hapur railway station. His family comprises his wife, a 12-year-old daughter and a 14-year-old son. He owns a three-storey house. At around 12:40 p.m. on Sunday, Ashu Sharma went to the Hapur Road market on a scooter with his wife and daughter to buy some items. The main door of the house was locked from the outside, while his son was sleeping on the second floor. Meanwhile, two minors reached the house, committed the theft and fled. The incident was captured on a CCTV camera installed in the lane. Son hatched a conspiracy after being reprimanded by his father According to the police, Ashu Sharma wanted his son to become a cricketer too, but the son did not want to. This often led to arguments between the father and son. The father had warned him that he would disinherit him in anger. The son was very upset about this. He therefore had his friends carry out the theft at the house. Son himself called his father to inform him about the theft Some time after the incident, the son called his father and told him that the belongings in the room were scattered and the cupboard was open. He said thieves had broken in and taken everything. Hearing this, Ashu Sharma immediately reached home. After finding the belongings scattered, he went to the police station and informed the police. The police reached the spot and carried out an investigation. When they examined footage from a CCTV camera installed nearby, two suspects were seen entering the house. The police then began investigating, and the son's role emerged. After taking him into custody and questioning him strictly, the son disclosed everything. The police subsequently detained both his friends. They recovered ₹11.50 lakh in cash and stolen jewellery from them. City SP Vinayak Bhosale said- “Three minors have been detained in the case. The preliminary investigation suggests that they were upset over their father's scolding. Further action is under way.”

stories.title: Muslim woman performs Chhath Puja after her son recovers:Ravi Kishan carries the 'daura'; devotees in UP complete 36-hour fast by offering Arghya to the Sun
stories.summary: Devotees in Uttar Pradesh worshipped the rising sun on the fourth and final day of the Chhath festival. Women observing the fast offered arghya to the Sun God while singing Chhath songs. This brought their 36-hour waterless fast to an end. From 4 a.m., crowds of devotees began gathering at more than 4,000 ghats across the state. Large numbers of people arrived to offer arghya. Traditional songs dedicated to Chhathi Maiya echoed across the ghats, where fireworks were also set off. The women applied sindoor to one another. They stood in water up to their knees and waited for sunrise. As soon as the sun rose, they performed the puja amid chants in praise of Chhathi Maiya. In Kushinagar, Muslim woman Afsana Khatun observed the Chhath fast after her ailing son recovered. She reached the ghat with her husband, Ali Mohammad, and son, and offered arghya to the Sun God. In Gorakhpur, MP Ravi Kishan reached the ghat carrying a daura on his head. He also sang the song, "Chhathi Maiya, bestow your blessings, let the bahangi sway..." French tourist Tania arrived in Kashi to witness the Chhath festival. She said, "We had read about this festival on the internet, but now we have seen it." See the pictures-

stories.title: Devotees offer Arghya to the rising Sun in Gorakhpur:MP Ravi Kishan carries a Chhath basket on his head and sings a song
stories.summary: On Monday, the fourth and final day of Chhath, the great festival of popular faith, women observing the fast completed their 36-hour waterless fast by offering arghya to the rising sun in Gorakhpur. As dawn broke, crowds of devotees began gathering at various ghats and reservoirs across the city. During this, MP Ravi Kishan also reached the ghat carrying a Chhath Puja daura on his head. He performed the prescribed rituals and worshipped Chhathi Maiya, and also sang the traditional song, "Chhathi Maiya, grant your blessings, let the bahangi sway..." Holding sup and daura decorated with offerings in their hands, the women stood in the water waiting for sunrise. As soon as the sun appeared, the fasting women offered arghya to the Sun God while singing traditional songs dedicated to Chhathi Maiya, and prayed for the family's happiness and prosperity, the well-being of their children and a long life. From around 5 a.m., devotees had begun arriving at the city's main Chhath ghats, including Rajghat, Bheem Sarovar at Gorakhnath Temple and the ancient Mansarovar Temple in Andhiyari Bagh. At the ghats, women were seen singing Chhath songs, while at other places family members danced to the beats of drums and manjiras and traditional songs. Children and other family members who accompanied the women observing the fast also joined in the celebrations of the major festival. The four-day Chhath festival concluded with devotees offering arghya to the Sun. MP Ravi Kishan arrived at Bhim Sarovar carrying a daura A large crowd of devotees had gathered at Bhim Sarovar in the Gorakhnath Temple complex since morning. During this, MP Ravi Kishan arrived at the ghat carrying a daura on his head. He worshipped Chhathi Maiya and sang the traditional Chhath song, "Chhathi Maiya, bless us, may the bahangi sway..." His singing sparked enthusiasm among the devotees present there. At Bhim Sarovar, women observing the fast offered arghya to the rising Sun and prayed for the happiness, peace and prosperity of their families. Women praised the arrangements at Rajghat Thousands of devotees arrived at Rajghat. After offering arghya, the women returning home from the ghat praised the cleanliness, security and other arrangements there. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Sapna, a resident of Mirzapur, said the atmosphere was very good. Security arrangements had improved considerably after the Yogi government came to power. Good arrangements had also been made for women. All kinds of facilities were available at the ghat. Children, women and men were all safe. Kalyani Gupta, who had come from Mirzapur, said the atmosphere was very good and sacred. The Chhath festival was the biggest religious festival in India. Chhath Mata fulfilled everyone's wishes. Her only prayer was that her husband, children and father remained happy, healthy and long-lived. Another woman said she had been observing the Chhath fast for 15 years. Chhathi Maiya had fulfilled her wish. She said she had four daughters. After the birth of her four daughters, she was blessed with a son by Chhathi Maiya. She said the arrangements at the ghat were very good and there was no shortcoming of any kind. Police manage crowds, help women cross the road safely Police and administrative teams remained on alert at Rajghat in view of the large gathering of devotees in the morning. As large numbers of devotees left the ghat together after offering arghya, police personnel took charge of the situation. Police personnel helped the women returning from the ghat and the family members accompanying them cross the road safely. Along with controlling the crowd, special attention was paid to ensuring the smooth movement of devotees. Cleaning and surveillance operation continued overnight To ensure that devotees faced no inconvenience on the final day of the Chhath festival, teams from the municipal corporation, police, district administration and the NDRF remained deployed at the ghats. A cleaning and surveillance operation continued throughout the night. Arrangements for cleanliness, security and devotees' convenience at the ghats were monitored. Amid the presence of security personnel at the water bodies and ghats, women observing the fast offered arghya to the rising sun. The four-day Chhath festival concluded in an atmosphere of faith, joy and devotion.

stories.title: Fire breaks out in 5-storey Kanpur apartment, 2 dead:Child burnt alive, woman dies after jumping from 30 feet; 10 people leap from balconies
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out at a five-storey apartment in Kanpur early on Monday, killing two people and leaving 8-10 others with burn injuries. Scooters and motorcycles parked in the parking area were gutted. The apartment has 12 flats, housing around 50-60 people. Eyewitnesses said the fire broke out in a ground-floor flat at around 4.30 am. It quickly spread throughout the building. The staircase leading downstairs filled with smoke, forcing residents to run around in panic as they tried to save their lives. A two-storey house stands opposite the apartment, which is located in a lane just 5-6 feet wide. Residents on the upper floors climbed down towards the second floor using sarees and bedsheets. Those on the lower floors went upstairs using the staircase. They then used wooden planks to reach the roof of the neighbouring house. Out of fear, 8-10 people jumped from their balconies and suffered injuries. The deceased have been identified as Rakhi Sahu (48) and Pranjul Batham (15). Pranjul died after being burnt alive. Rakhi jumped from the third floor and fell on Vaibhav Gupta, who was standing below. Rakhi died on the spot, while Vaibhav suffered a fractured spine. Police said a short circuit may have caused the fire. The incident took place at Radhika Apartment in the Patkapur outpost area under the jurisdiction of the Filkhana police station, in the heart of the city. See pictures of the incident- 'Everyone was asleep when the fire broke out' Mahesh Tiwari said, "I live on the third floor of Radhika Apartment. Everyone was asleep in the morning when we suddenly heard people shouting. When I opened the door, there was smoke and fire everywhere. Panic broke out, and we ran to save our lives. We climbed down from the third floor to the second floor using a dhoti. From there, we placed a wooden plank and crossed over to the roof of the building opposite." He said, "The apartment is owned by Mohit Tiwari. There are no fire safety arrangements here. Fire brigade vehicles also arrived quite late. By then, several people, including us, had already managed to get downstairs." Advocate's wife jumps from third floor, dies Apartment built two years ago in a lane just 5-6 feet wide Local residents said the apartment (house number 9/74) is located in Ramnarayan Bazaar. It was built around two years ago in a lane that is just 5-6 feet wide. The building has only one exit, which is also very narrow. Residents alleged that they called the emergency helpline 112 after the fire broke out, but no one answered for a long time. ACP Kotwali Amit Pandey said, "We received information about the fire at the apartment in the morning. The building has 12 flats. Some residents managed to escape by using the walls of neighbouring houses. The fire brigade team rescued the others. They included an elderly person, some women and a child." 'All buildings should be inspected at least once' A local resident said, “All the buildings constructed here should be inspected at least once. It should be checked whether they were built according to the prescribed standards and under what conditions. Permission is granted to construct three or four floors, but buildings are being built up to five floors. The entire matter should be investigated immediately. The families of those who lost their lives in the incident and the affected people should receive compensation. It should also be established who is responsible for the incident and who should be held accountable.” One woman in critical condition, suffers 40% burns Dr Shubham Jain of Ursala Hospital said, "Four people were brought to our hospital. Rakhi and Pranjul had already died. Pranjul's body was completely burnt. Vaibhav Gupta suffered a spinal injury. He may have jumped while trying to escape the fire. He has been referred to the neurology department at Hallet Hospital. Pranjul's mother, Neeta, has suffered around 40% burns. Her condition is critical." This report is being updated…

stories.title: BJP booth president brutally assaulted in Varanasi:Attackers beat him outside his house and hurled abuses; suffers serious injuries to face and neck
stories.summary: Armed attackers assaulted a BJP booth president who had played an active role in the Prime Minister's election on Sunday night. The attackers cornered the businessman and BJP booth president outside his home and began beating him. The attackers knocked him to the road, beat him and left him badly bleeding. When people from the surrounding area gathered and tried to rescue him, the attackers fled while hurling abuses. The victim, a BJP leader, informed office-bearers of the organisation about the incident and reached the police station with local residents to file a written complaint. Although the police registered a case late at night, the accused are still absconding. BJP booth president covered in blood in pictures First, know the full story Anuj Shukla, the BJP booth president for booth number 304 in Jangambari, Ward 89 of Varanasi, is a resident of Ganesh Mahal and has been active in the BJP for a long time. Anuj runs a shop selling leaf bowls and plates from his home. On Sunday night, Anuj Shukla was brutally beaten by men over an old enmity, who also threatened to kill him. At around 11 p.m., he was unloading goods from an e-rickshaw and putting them inside the shop. Meanwhile, Sunny Yadav suddenly arrived there and began abusing him. When Anuj objected, Sunny Yadav assaulted him. The accused also threatened to kill him. Anuj suffered injuries to his face and neck in the attack. Dashashwamedh police station in-charge Santosh Kumar Singh said an FIR had been registered against Sunny Yadav on charges including assault, criminal intimidation and other offences. Anuj Shukla comes from an economically weaker family and lives in a rented house with his elderly widowed mother and brother. The entire family has been living in fear since the incident.

stories.title: Husband arrested in BKT woman’s suicide case:Confesses to murder; mother-in-law says she spoke to another man on phone
stories.summary: Police have arrested the woman's husband in connection with her suicide in Lucknow's BKT area. During questioning, he confessed to killing her. The couple had quarrelled on the day of the incident, after which he killed her. The woman's parental family had accused her in-laws of killing her and destroying evidence. Ashok's mother, Ramkumari, meanwhile, said that her daughter-in-law Sunita used to speak to another man on the phone. This had led to an argument between the husband and wife. The husband and wife had quarrelled before the incident Sunita, aged around 35, was found hanging in Achramau village under the BKT police station area on the night of 16 November. Her in-laws said that Sunita had hanged herself. After this, her in-laws cremated Sunita without waiting for her maternal family to arrive. Her family had alleged that she was murdered. They had married 17 years ago Police registered a case based on a complaint by Sunita's father, Panchu, and arrested Ashok. Sunita was a resident of Udatpur Majra Raipur Raja village under the Itaunja police station area. She had married Ashok Gautam of Achramau village around 17 years ago. Ashok worked as a labourer. The couple have two sons, Aakash (13) and Adarsh (10). Ashok's mother, Ramkumari, and his two brothers also live in the family. All three brothers live separately with their respective families. 'There was never any dispute between the two' Mohammad Fuzail, a resident of the village, said that there had never been any dispute between Sunita and Ashok. They had been married for around 16 years. According to him, everyone in the family had a good nature. The villagers were shocked when they suddenly learnt that Sunita had hanged herself.
