stories.title: UP STF kills shooter Naseem Durrani in encounter:Wanted in Delhi minister Kapil Mishra's office murder case
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) killed shooter Naseem Durrani (37) in an encounter in Bulandshahr. A reward of ₹50,000 had been announced for his arrest. He was wanted in connection with the murder of a man outside Delhi minister Kapil Mishra's office four days ago. The STF and Delhi Police had received information that Durrani was hiding in Bulandshahr and planning to flee. When the teams surrounded him, he opened fire. Around 15 to 20 rounds were fired from both sides. Durrani was killed in the retaliatory firing after being hit by two bullets in the chest. The encounter took place at around 1 am on Thursday in the Sikandrabad police station area. Durrani, a resident of Delhi, had 26 criminal cases against him, including four murder cases. He was also in contact with underworld don Chhota Shakeel. In 2017, Shakeel had allegedly given him a contract to kill Chhota Rajan, who was lodged in Tihar Jail at the time. Durrani was also accused of conspiring to murder Pakistani-origin writer Tarek Fatah. Opened fire fearing arrest; killed in retaliatory firing Noida STF Additional SP Rajkumar Mishra said Durrani was escaping on a motorcycle. When the team surrounded him, he opened fire at the police, fearing arrest. He was hit by a bullet in the retaliatory firing and fell to the ground. He was rushed to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Police recovered a motorcycle and two .32-bore pistols from the spot. Three pictures of encounter… Three major crimes linked to Durrani 1. Killed a man in Delhi four days ago On November 16, Durrani shot dead a man named Sameer in Sonia Vihar, under the Khajuri Khas police station area of Delhi. He fled after the incident. During the investigation, police examined CCTV footage from the surrounding area, while crime and forensic science laboratory (FSL) teams collected evidence from the spot. Durrani emerged as the main accused, following which Delhi Police launched a search for him. 2. Killed another man in May 2026 On May 26, 2026, a shooting took place in Delhi's Khajuri Khas area. A man named Raja Mewati was shot. Police took him to JPC Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. During the investigation, Durrani, also known as Rizwan, was identified as the main shooter in the murder. 3. Shot at a woman in Ghaziabad a year ago Additional SP Rajkumar Mishra said Durrani had opened fire at a woman in Loni, Ghaziabad, in 2025. She was injured but survived after receiving treatment. Ghaziabad Police had announced a reward of ₹50,000 for information leading to his arrest in this case. Durrani was married and had three sisters Naseem, also known as Rizwan, was the son of Islamuddin, alias Budhu. He originally belonged to Rajiv Gandhi Nagar in New Mustafabad, Delhi. His family included his father Islamuddin, mother Nafisa, wife Zeba and three sisters — Rubina, Rani and Zeenat. According to police, Durrani had been involved in criminal cases since 2010. More than 22 cases were registered against him in Delhi and Uttar Pradesh, including murder, robbery, dacoity, Arms Act violations and attacks on police personnel. Second encounter in UP in three days Two days before Durrani was killed, contract killer Wahid Ansari (35) was killed in an encounter in Ambedkar Nagar. He was allegedly a major arms supplier in eastern Uttar Pradesh and carried out murders for money. Police surrounded him on Tuesday night, following which he opened fire. He was hit by four bullets in the chest and leg and fell on the road. Two police personnel were injured in the encounter. SP Prachi Singh narrowly escaped after a bullet hit her bulletproof jacket. 259 criminals killed in encounters in eight years According to the state government, UP Police killed 266 criminals in encounters between March 2017 and October 2025. During this period, more than 16,000 police encounters took place. Over 31,000 criminals were arrested, while more than 10,000 were shot and injured.

stories.title: Daughter asked, ‘What would I say if I got lost?’:Father demands accused nephew be burnt alive; 4-year-old girl was raped murdered
stories.summary: A father in Uttar Pradesh’s Hardoi has demanded the death penalty for his 20-year-old nephew, who allegedly raped and murdered his four-year-old daughter. He said the accused should either be killed in a police encounter or burnt alive in front of the family. “The man who killed my daughter should be killed in an encounter. Otherwise, pour petrol over him and burn him alive in front of us. He should be made to suffer before being killed so that no such monster emerges in the area again. What happened to us today could happen to another family tomorrow. He must not be allowed to remain alive,” the grieving father said. The girl went missing from outside her home on 13 November. Her body was found in an orchard on 15 November, around 2 km from the village. The accused, identified as Rizbi Yadav, was the girl's cousin uncle. He had joined the family in searching for her and even dug the pit for her burial. A Dainik Bhaskar team travelled 37 km from the district headquarters and spoke to the family to piece together the sequence of events. First, know what happened... A four-year-old girl went missing from outside her home in a village under Lonar Kotwali police station on 13 November. Her family searched for her throughout the day but failed to find her. They subsequently lodged a missing-person complaint at the police station that night. Teams from the Special Operations Group (SOG), surveillance unit and dog squad, along with police personnel from six police stations, were deployed to trace the child. On the evening of 15 November, her body was found in bushes in an orchard around 2 km from the village. There was a cut mark on her neck, and rape was suspected. The incident triggered anger in the village. During the investigation, police identified the girl's cousin uncle, Rizbi Yadav, as the accused. He allegedly raped her and killed her to prevent her from disclosing the crime. Police arrested him on 18 November and sent him to jail. Now read what the father said... The girl's father, who works as a Provincial Armed Constabulary (PRD) personnel, said he also works in farming in the village. He has three daughters and two brothers. “On 13 November, before leaving for the fields in the morning, I ate a rasgulla and gave some to both my daughters. I saw the girl playing once in the afternoon. In the evening, I received a call at home saying she was missing,” he said. My cousin searched for her everywhere with us The father said the family searched throughout the village and also took his father to the police outpost. Police teams immediately joined the search and continued looking for the girl through the night. He said the accused also pretended to help them find her. “He went with me and my paternal uncle's sons to search for her as far as Bareilly, Turia and Bawan. He did not speak much to anyone, so we never suspected him,” the father said. Family did not suspect him The father said the accused appeared equally distressed after the girl went missing. “Everyone in the family was dejected, and he also looked sad. We thought he was grieving as a family member. We had no idea that he was stabbing us in the back,” he said. He added that after the girl's funeral, the Circle Officer (CO) and a police team in plain clothes took the accused away. The police have not yet brought him face to face with the family. Daughter often asked what she should do if she got lost The father recalled that his daughter would often ask him, “Dad, what will I say if I get lost somewhere?” “She would then answer innocently, ‘I will tell them my father's name and my grandfather's name. Then someone will bring me back and drop me in my village’,” he said. He added that the family had lost their newborn son just a month and a half earlier and was still coping with that grief when the girl was killed. “My wife is in a very bad condition. She has to take medicines every day. Our only demand is that this monster should be burnt alive after being doused in petrol, or the police should kill him in an encounter,” he said. Mother is distraught since girl's death The girl's mother has been inconsolable since her daughter's death and reportedly loses consciousness several times while speaking about the incident. She said the accused should be made to suffer even more than her daughter did before being killed. Only then, she said, would her daughter's soul and her own find peace. “On the morning of the incident, my daughter told me, ‘Mummy, I am going out to play.’ I gave her some tea before she left. In the afternoon, I called out to her, but she was nowhere to be found,” the mother said. She described her daughter as cheerful and playful. Recalling the Diwali celebrations, she said the child had burst several firecrackers and the family had never imagined that such a tragedy would strike. “My only demand is that the person who did this should be tortured to death,” she said. Grandfather demands that accused be shot The girl's grandfather said he was on duty in Sandila when the incident took place. “He has committed such a despicable act against our family and must be punished.” He added, “If he is spared today because he is considered a family member, he could target another child tomorrow. Just shoot him. We have nothing to do with him, whether he is a relative, a villager or anyone else.” Accused misled family even after murder The grandfather alleged that Rizbi continued to mislead the family after killing the girl and accompanied them to the police outpost. “He searched for her everywhere with us but never told us anything about the place where he had committed the crime. When my sons saw the body, they screamed,” he said. The grandfather further alleged that the accused dug the pit himself and took part in the last rites. He also accompanied the police when the inspector called him. “He stood there calmly. Our only demand is that he should be hanged,” the grandfather said. Both parents of accused are dead Rizbi Yadav, 20, has lost both his parents and is the eldest of four brothers. All four brothers live in Delhi, where Rizbi works in the water supply sector. His house in the village is close to the girl's home. He had returned to the village for Diwali. According to the account of the incident, Rizbi saw the girl playing alone on the afternoon of 13 November and took her to a field on the pretext of feeding her. He allegedly raped her there. Fearing that she would tell her family about the assault, he strangled her and left her body in the field before returning home. Father named him after a constable Villagers said Rizbi's father had frequently faced police action over disputes and had been jailed several times. A constable named Rizbi would arrest him and take him away. His father reportedly liked the constable's name so much that he named his son after him. Police confirm arrest Harpalpur CO Praveen Kumar Yadav said a missing-person report was registered on 13 November and the girl's body was recovered during the search. “The post-mortem confirmed rape. The investigation revealed that her cousin uncle, Rizbi Yadav, was responsible for the murder. He has been arrested and sent to jail,” he said.

stories.title: Woman arrives at boyfriend's house with wedding procession:Says, 'We were together for 7 years, but he is now marrying someone else'
stories.summary: A woman from Dehradun arrived at her boyfriend's house in Shamli with her mother and family members, accompanied by a wedding procession with drums and music. She was carrying a banner that read, 'I have brought a wedding procession to take the bride home'. The woman alleged that her boyfriend had been in a relationship with her for seven years and repeatedly promised to marry her. However, he is now set to marry another woman on November 21. Her unexpected arrival with the procession drew a crowd outside her boyfriend's house. The incident took place at around 6 pm on Thursday in the Elam town area under Kandhla police station limits. First, see two pictures.... Here is the full story… Sonia, who lives in Dehradun, is a BSc student. Her boyfriend, Ankush, serves in the Merchant Navy and lives in Elam town in Shamli. The two had stopped communicating over the past few days. During this time, Sonia learnt that Ankush's marriage had been arranged with another woman and that he was due to get married two days later. She was distressed after learning about his upcoming marriage. They met at a wedding seven years ago Sonia said she first met Ankush in 2019 at his sister's wedding. They initially became friends, but their friendship gradually developed into a relationship. They continued talking and meeting, while Ankush repeatedly promised to marry her. He had also created a wedding invitation card with her and sent it to her on WhatsApp, she claimed. Allegedly behaved inappropriately with her on the pretext of introducing her to his sister Sonia alleged that Ankush once took her along in Dehradun on the pretext of introducing her to his sister and a friend. She claimed that he took her to another room and behaved inappropriately with her. He continued promising to marry her during this period, she alleged. According to Sonia, Ankush's family members were also aware of their relationship. Learnt about his wedding after finding out about the invitation Sonia said she recently learnt that Ankush's marriage had been arranged with another woman and that his wedding procession was scheduled for November 21. She tried contacting him but received no response. She then informed her family about the entire matter. After this, she travelled to Elam with nine family members, including her mother and sister. "I have come here to make him fulfil the promise of marriage he made to me. I remained in this relationship for so many years because I trusted him. The entire incident has caused me mental distress, and my health has also suffered. I will marry Ankush," she said. Crowd gathers outside boyfriend's house as procession arrives When Sonia and her family reached Ankush's house carrying the banner, a crowd gathered in the neighbourhood. A team from the Elam police outpost reached the spot after receiving information about the incident. However, Sonia and her family were not satisfied with the police's initial response. They returned to Ankush's house and demanded strict action. ASP Sumit Shukla said police personnel were sent to the spot after receiving information. The police are gathering details about the matter, and further action will be taken after an investigation.

stories.title: Agra student drowns in Ganga in Rishikesh:Was bathing in river with friends; 32 students had arrived on a school trip
stories.summary: A 15-year-old student from Agra was swept away by the strong current of the Ganga while bathing in the river in the Laxman Jhula area of Rishikesh. He had visited the town on an excursion with 32 other students and five teachers from his school. The student was bathing with his companions at a ghat when the strong current swept him away. His fellow students raised an alarm after witnessing the incident. Search operation launched, student remains missing Following the incident, the water police, local residents and the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) launched a search operation. However, the student remained missing until late evening. PHOTOS from the rescue operation... Class 10 student swept away while bathing with friends Ansh (15), a Class 10 student and son of Rajkumar Sharma, a resident of Rohta in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, had arrived in Rishikesh on an excursion on Thursday (19 Nov). His group reached a ghat near the Laxman Jhula bridge, where Ansh went to bathe in the Ganga with other students. He was swept away by the river's strong current. Water police and locals attempt rescue After Ansh was swept away, the students accompanying him raised an alarm. Hearing their cries, water police personnel and local residents at the spot attempted to rescue him. However, the strong current carried him further downstream. On receiving information about the incident, an SDRF rescue team from the Dhalwala post reached the spot. Deep divers were deployed to search for the missing student. Search operation suspended after dark The SDRF team conducted an extensive search in the Ganga but could not locate Ansh. The operation was temporarily suspended after dark as it became difficult to continue the search at night. The search will resume on Friday. Laxmanjhula police informed the student's family about the incident. Teams from the Laxmanjhula police station and the water police remained at the site.

Currently, her legal team is appealing this decision, as the ruling's implications may significantly impact both the right of way and her financial obligations.

stories.title: A birdwatcher in Canada spotted a rare songbird absent from his county for over five years
stories.summary: In September, Canadian birdwatcher Paul Jones made a remarkable discovery in Ontario when he spotted an endangered loggerhead shrike. This bird, known for its striking appearance, had journeyed 30 miles from where it was released. This incident is pivotal for conservation initiatives focused on increasing the population of this declining species.

stories.title: A new snake found near the China-Nepal border looks like an earthworm
stories.summary: A new species of blind snake named Indotyphlops gyirongensis has been identified in Gyirong County, China. The specimen was found at a high elevation under a stone in August 2025. This snake is adapted to a life underground and has several unique physical traits. Researchers used both physical examination and genetic analysis to establish its distinct lineage. Further studies are needed to understand its distribution, population, and dietary habits.

stories.title: Illinois motorcyclist's $27.5 million verdict cut by $10 million on appeal
stories.summary: In a notable personal injury verdict, an Illinois motorcyclist was awarded $27.5 million for severe injuries sustained in a crash, only for the Fifth District Appellate Court to later trim the amount to $17.5 million. The court deemed the initial sum excessive, allowing the rider the choice to accept the lower amount or request a new trial, underscoring the significant effect appellate reviews can have on trial outcomes.

stories.title: Warren Beatty and Annette Bening's LA mansion is up for sale for $14.9M
stories.summary: Listed at $14.995 million, this exquisite mansion boasts a rich Hollywood heritage, having been owned by the iconic Warren Beatty and Annette Bening for twenty years. The expansive 10,594 square foot estate features seven bedrooms, twelve bathrooms, and a swanky 17-seat theater named after Beatty himself. With modern finishes and a prime location that balances seclusion with easy access to Los Angeles, this property represents luxurious living at its finest.

stories.title: Hershey's is bringing back its original five-cent chocolate bar price for one day on November 25, with limited offers through Walmart, Amazon and its own stores ahead of a film about the company's founder
stories.summary: To honor its rich heritage and usher in a new film, Hershey is bringing back its iconic five-cent chocolate bar for a limited time. This nostalgic initiative reflects Milton Hershey's dream of making chocolate readily available to everyone in America. Starting from November 25, fans can indulge in this sweet treat at select retailers like Walmart and Amazon.

stories.title: Winter Gardens Restoration: Heritage Fund awards £10 million; reopening planned for December 2029
stories.summary: A £10 million grant is set to transform the People's Palace and Winter Gardens in Glasgow into a vibrant community hub. This initiative aims to enhance accessibility and create educational spaces that celebrate the city's rich history and culture. The project, anticipated to conclude by December 2029, will connect the glasshouse with the museum, ensuring a cohesive visitor experience while preserving these iconic landmarks.

stories.title: Iowa court upholds will giving son 477 acres and daughters 107 each
stories.summary: In a complex case from Iowa, a 2003 will created significant disparities among an estate's four heirs, culminating in legal battles. After stumbling upon the will in 2014, the daughters sought resolution but were hindered by an unenforceable family agreement. The Iowa Supreme Court ultimately ruled that their contest was submitted after the allowable deadline, highlighting the critical importance of acting promptly when challenging wills to prevent similar estate disputes.

stories.title: Warren Beatty and Annette Bening's former Beverly Hills home lists for $14.995 million
stories.summary: The iconic Beverly Hills residence of Warren Beatty and Annette Bening is now available for nearly 15 million dollars. Initially acquired for 6.7 million dollars in 2012, extensive renovations worth 5 million dollars have modernized its Mediterranean allure. Among its features are a custom home theater repurposed from the original office and a range of outdoor amenities, making it a perfect retreat steeped in cinematic history.

stories.title: Food regulator FSSAI sanctions prosecution of Bisleri, 4 other firms
stories.summary: Licences Of Two Others Suspended

stories.title: Why did a small GTA 6 streamer break down in tears after Ibai Llanos joined his Twitch stream?
stories.summary: Dicrim_RD69 saw a remarkable surge in viewership after the popular streamer Ibai Llanos featured him during a GTA 6 livestream. What started as a nearly empty stream transformed into a bustling hub of activity, drawing in fans thanks to Ibai's influence. Overwhelmed with gratitude, Dicrim opened up about his earlier struggles in streaming, demonstrating how even a simple gesture of support can profoundly affect a creator's path.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi 'clarifies' after allies criticise remark on Hamas and Israel

Art collector Agnes Gund's collection brought in $25.7 million at a New York auction to benefit her charitable foundation; a portrait she called her Mona Lisa fetched $1.1 million, setting an artist record
stories.summary: Agnes Gund's remarkable auction of her art collection amassed an impressive $25.7 million, all directed toward her charitable foundation. Among the highlights was a record-setting painting by Jim Nutt. With initiatives like the Art for Justice Fund, her philanthropy champions criminal justice reform and underscores her unwavering dedication to both art and educational accessibility.

stories.title: India, Nepal set to ink pacts on energy, infra, tech on Balen Shah's 1st visit
NHAI puts 50,000 km of highways under dashcam watch, to automate penalties for contractors
Wyoming court upholds $101,232 award in dispute over family ranch and proposed hospital sale
stories.summary: A family ranch battle among three siblings resulted in serious legal challenges. The dispute revolved around access paths and a failed sale of a hospital. Suellen Davidson's involvement disrupted her siblings' agreement with Platte Valley Healthcare Project. The Wyoming Supreme Court confirmed a damages award for this interference, illustrating the complexities faced in family property disputes that intertwine personal relationships with business transactions.

stories.title: Goldie Hawn joins 1,700 at Atlanta luncheon raising $1.08m for women and girls
stories.summary: The 30th annual Numbers Too Big To Ignore Luncheon in Atlanta successfully raised over $1 million, benefitting various community programs. Goldie Hawn shared her insights on parenting, kindness, and children's mental health, highlighting how adults significantly impact young lives. The event featured generous contributions from attendees and a matching donation from The Coca-Cola Foundation, with proceeds directed towards enhancing opportunities for women and girls in the metro Atlanta area.

stories.title: A British shopper paid just £20 for a painting at a charity shop, then an expert identified it as a 160-year-lost Nicholas Chevalier landscape; it is now expected to fetch up to £20,000 at a December auction
stories.summary: A British shopper found a painting attributed to 19th-century artist Nicholas Chevalier for only £20 in a charity shop. After purchase, the buyer sought an expert's opinion which confirmed the painting's significance. The artwork, named Cape Schanck, Victoria, had been lost for around 160 years. This discovery reconnects the painting with Chevalier's historical records, offering a glimpse into his artistic process.

stories.title: Atlanta's abandoned prison farm, with crumbling buildings and a former zoo-animal cemetery, could become a public park and memorial; the city has unveiled plans but must first relocate a bomb range
stories.summary: Atlanta is set to transform the historic prison farm site into a public park and memorial. The project aims to preserve the history of forced labor while creating green spaces for the community. Proposed features include walking trails, a museum, and educational facilities for visitors. The city faces challenges, including relocating a bomb detonation range on the property.

stories.title: Indian Navy allows marriage for Agniveers opting for 2-year service extension
Ladakh chief secretary cites cites 70% panchayat poll turnout, sticks to December 4 hill council voting
Could IShowSpeed have a future beyond YouTube? Usain Bolt weighs in after surprising 100m performance
stories.summary: In a thrilling showdown, IShowSpeed took on legendary sprinter Usain Bolt in a 100-meter race, finishing with a time of 10.352 seconds, as showcased in a captivating YouTube video on November 22, 2026. Although his achievement doesn't eclipse Bolt's remarkable world record, it certainly highlights Speed's untapped potential in sprinting. Bolt himself noted Speed's capability, igniting discussions about his possible future in the world of professional athletics.

stories.title: Kaiga nuclear unit-1 attains criticality again, gets a second life
Ohio appeals court rejects stepson's bid to control stepmother's estate after trust dispute
Mansion Relisted At $38.495 Million: Jenner relists estate; nearly $10 million below original price
stories.summary: Kylie Jenner's Holmby Hills mansion has returned to the market at a new asking price of $38.495 million, down from its previous listing of $48 million over a year ago. After purchasing the estate for $36.5 million in 2020, this marks her third attempt to find a buyer. The luxurious property boasts numerous amenities, including a basketball court and a home theatre, showcasing a blend of elegance and entertainment.

stories.title: The Conservation Fund protects North America's largest gathering site of Pacific walruses
stories.summary: As climate change continues to threaten the Pacific walrus population, significant steps have been taken to protect their habitat. A 47,473-acre conservation easement around Point Lay, Alaska, has been established to minimize human impact during walrus haul-outs. This initiative not only safeguards these mammals but also allows local Indigenous communities to retain access to vital resources, symbolizing a harmonious balance between conservation and community needs.

stories.title: A firefly not seen since 1983 has been found again after scientist recognised its amber flashes
stories.summary: Exciting news emerged in 2026 when a firefly, thought to have vanished since 1983, was rediscovered in Delaware and Virginia. Its unique amber flash patterns caught the attention of researchers, confirming its survival. Habitat loss is suspected to have led to its absence from earlier records. Community engagement significantly aided in this rediscovery, prompting further surveys to assess the firefly's population and habitat requirements.

stories.title: San Francisco mansion resells for $24M after five months
stories.summary: A five-bedroom mansion in Presidio Heights sold for $24 million after a previous purchase of $21 million. The property was originally listed in June and returned to the market in November at $19.9 million. It was sold within three days of being re-listed due to high demand for luxury homes. The house spans 8,000 square feet and features extensive renovations while preserving its original craftsmanship.

stories.title: A teenage girl found headless in a Northern Ireland bog in 2023 died up to 2,300 years ago, and a mock coroner’s inquest in Belfast has now pieced together her height, diet and how she was struck
stories.summary: Recent findings of the Ballymacombs More Woman's remains in a Northern Ireland bog are unlocking fascinating details about her life in the Iron Age, circa 343 BCE to 1 BCE. An in-depth analysis reveals she suffered a violent decapitation, likely part of a ritualistic act. Such research is crucial as it provides a greater understanding of the social and cultural practices of ancient communities.

stories.title: '90 seats, one crore votes': Revanth Reddy sets Congress' 2028 Telangana target
stories.summary: Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy expressed confidence in Congress winning 90 out of 119 Assembly seats. He indicated that the party's leadership was devising a strategy for this goal. Reddy criticised the Bharat Rashtra Samithi for spreading false narratives about the Congress government. The state government is preparing an action plan for potential drought conditions influenced by El Niño.

stories.title: In 1884, an Erie family built a Queen Anne mansion; 142 years later, the 360,000-pound home has been restored after a seven-hour move and renamed for the businessman who rescued it, with a university now leasing it
stories.summary: The Olds-Norman House, a historic mansion built in 1884, was rescued from the wrecking ball and moved 250 feet in Erie, Pennsylvania. Now called the Thomas B. Hagen House, it’s found a new life thanks to Gannon University. This Queen Anne-style beauty has witnessed a lot over the years and is now being preserved for future generations.

stories.title: Scientists find 156-million-year-old horned reptile fossil in Wyoming sandstone
stories.summary: A remarkable discovery in Wyoming has unearthed a fossil of a diminutive dinosaur-like creature, dating back 156 million years to the Jurassic era. Advanced imaging techniques uncovered this skeleton entombed in sandstone. Researchers classify it as an early reptilian branch, enhancing our understanding of evolutionary history. Analysis indicates it inhabited freshwater environments and may have fallen prey to a larger predator.

stories.title: SCO Civilisational Dialogue at Purana Qila concludes with 'Indraprastha Communique' affirming to respect every civilisation as an 'equal voice'
Texas inheritance fight over ranches, yacht and millions leads to asset freeze limits
stories.summary: A high-stakes inheritance battle in Texas involves Lonnie K. Ledbetter Jr.'s significant estate, featuring sprawling ranches and luxury cars. Following the Texas Second Court of Appeals ruling, assets have been temporarily frozen, impacting his wife, Tawni Ledbetter. Disputes continue over Lonnie's mental capacity during key document signings, while some assets await judicial clarification. A court-appointed receiver will oversee daily expenses and management as the case progresses.

stories.title: BJP leader, Shiv Sena MLA clash at public event in Palghar; minister steps in
Prince William plans to strip Prince Harry, Meghan of royal titles: Report
'He's not America's friend in Ukraine': US spy chief on Putin days after Trump's praise
Bangladesh unrest: Bengal CM Suvendu to write to EAM, may push to extend minority entry cut-off
stories.summary: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari is set to contact external affairs minister S Jaishankar regarding violence in Bangladesh. He indicated that the state government may seek an extension for religious minorities fleeing Bangladesh to enter India. Adhikari mentioned significant public concern in West Bengal due to the unrest across the border. Meanwhile, the BJP leader has called for protests against the violence in Bangladesh.

stories.title: NY court rejects 3 brothers’ bid for access across sibling’s farm
stories.summary: Four New York brothers who jointly ran a family farm ended up in court after their business relationship broke down. An appeals court rejected three brothers' demand for a route through their sibling's land, finding they had failed to prove it was essential to reach their gravel pit and timber areas. The court also upheld the decision to award their brother a 1988 Chevrolet Suburban under their property settlement.

stories.title: California drone operator spots great white near swimmer and alerts fisherman to danger
stories.summary: While fishing off the California coast, a fisherman faced a frightening close call with a great white shark. Oblivious to the danger lurking below, he was saved when a drone operator spotted the shark and warned him. The struggling fish near the boat likely caught the predator's interest. Such encounters underline the need for heightened awareness among water enthusiasts in the ocean's depths.

stories.title: Ohio court upholds father's child-support cut from $1,745 to $141 a month after custody change
Absence of COP31 cover decision does not pause climate action in India, says Bhupender Yadav
stories.summary: At COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, Bhupender Yadav, the Union environment minister, articulated India's dedication to climate change initiatives. He shared insights on India’s substantial advancements in solar power and renewable energy. Emphasising equity and climate justice, he voiced regret over the failure to achieve consensus on the cover decision. India’s proactive engagement with other nations showcases its resolve to address climate issues through collaboration.

stories.title: COP31 ends without climate pact as countries fail to reach consensus over fossil fuel omission and empty finance promises
'Make Nishant Bihar CM': Pappu Yadav slams BJP over'Nitish Setu', accuses BJP of betraying ex-CM
Terry Farrell’s last home hits the market for £525,000 in historic Kent mansion
stories.summary: Terry Farrell's former apartment in Great Maytham Hall, Kent, is now on the market priced at £525,000. The historic property features a significant past, as it was once home to author Frances Hodgson Burnett. Architect Edwin Lutyens redesigned the hall for the Tennant family in the early 1900s. The apartment boasts high ceilings and views of extensive grounds. Potential buyers will need to address the property's energy performance certificate rating.

stories.title: Now, pilots’ body raise safety concerns for SpiceJet; seek urgent assessment of airline by DGCA
'Destroyed credibility of polls': Congress alleges gaps in voting data across 200 seats in Lok Sabha polls
Vancouver police discontinue pay of Punjab-origin officer Kalwinder Dosanjh facing theft and fraud charges
Marty Fox buys A$4.2 million home; says softer conditions favour buyers
stories.summary: Marty Fox, known from The Block, purchased a five-bedroom home in Burleigh Heads for A$4.2 million. The property is set for major renovations and is located near the beach. Fox believes the current market presents an excellent buying opportunity despite declining prices. He emphasizes a new investment strategy that focuses on renting fully renovated homes. His previous home will transition into a luxury holiday rental, contributing to his adjusted approach.

stories.title: 'Boycott him, get him treated': Cong's Ajay Rai slams Dhirendra Shastri over Lord Krishna remark
Former England football captain David Beckham praises Madhya Pradesh teen who stopped her marriage
'India cherishes special friendship with Nepal': Jaishankar meets Nepal PM Balen Shah
stories.summary: S Jaishankar met Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah to foster bilateral relations during his visit to India. The discussions will focus on enhancing cooperation in areas such as trade and connectivity. Shah's delegation includes key ministers and a separate business group aiming to strengthen ties. Both leaders are expected to explore new agreements that benefit both nations. Shah's visit marks his first foreign bilateral trip since taking office in March.

stories.title: FSSAI sanctions prosecution against Bisleri over unsafe packaged drinking water
'Haven't been invited to discuss Indus': Pakistani minister dodges question on 'cut off hands' threat
'Some people still hesitate': PM Modi takes swipe at opposition over World Bank report on poverty
Luana Lopes Lara built Kalshi into a $40 billion prediction market giant; now faces US gambling law battle
stories.summary: Luana Lopes Lara, 30, became the world's youngest self-made female billionaire after co-founding Kalshi with Tarek Mansour in 2021. The prediction market platform is now valued at $40 billion. Known for working up to 16 hours a day, Lara built the company through years of regulatory battles. Now, Kalshi faces legal challenges over whether its event contracts violate US state gambling laws.

stories.title: Former Oregon interim police chief fired after criticising city leaders wins $935,000 in retaliation case
stories.summary: Sean Lundry, who formerly held the position of interim police chief in Oregon, has been awarded $935,000 by a federal jury. The verdict recognized that city officials penalized him for exercising his First Amendment rights, particularly after he raised concerns about the police chief recruitment process in January 2024. His criticisms included issues related to public records and alleged financial misconduct by the city.

stories.title: No bilateral talks with Pakistani minister on sidelines of SCO event: Culture secretary
Wife's support during husband's medical training becomes key in divorce asset battle
stories.summary: An Alabama appeals court reversed a divorce property settlement after finding that a lower court wrongly excluded a surgeon's medical-business interests, acquired during his marriage, from marital assets. His wife had supported the household while he completed medical training. The case has been sent back for a fresh valuation and division of the couple's property.

stories.title: PMLA case against suspended DIG: ED summons seven serving and retired Punjab officials, including IAS, IPS officers
Evening newswrap: Rahul Gandhi targets BJP-RSS with Ardhanareshwar image; Revanth Reddy’s swipe at own MLAs spark row & more
North Carolina farmer Noah Ranells has permanently protected 63 acres of his farm
stories.summary: Noah Ranells has taken a significant step by permanently conserving 63 acres of Fickle Creek Farm in Alamance County, North Carolina. This proactive move comes after a concerning decline in local farmland over the past decade. The farm is dedicated to producing meat, eggs, and vegetables for its community, ensuring a robust connection to local food sources.

stories.title: In the late 1800s, drainage and a new river channel altered Florida's Ocklawaha Prairie
stories.summary: The Ocklawaha Prairie Restoration Area spans 6,301 acres in Florida, focused on revitalizing wetlands and promoting wildlife habitats. Key restoration efforts have led to improved water quality and increased capacity for floodwater storage. Complementing these efforts is a Chornobyl Memorial Forest honoring victims of the 1986 nuclear disaster. Visitors can enjoy hiking, fishing, and primitive camping, while seasonal waterfowl hunting adds to the area's recreational appeal.

stories.title: 'Grand theft without auto': Shashi Tharoor tries hand at GTA 6, takes swipe at Modi govt
'Failed to communicate double-engine govt's work': Union minister on BJP's poor show in Rajasthan panchayat polls
New York court orders insurer to pay bar owner's legal fees after rejecting assault exclusion defence
Trump reposts ‘TrumpCare’ proposal from democrat he previously called a ‘jihadist’
'Mandal adhyakhsh is enough for you': Nitin Nabin rubbishes Rahul Gandhi's debate challenge to PM Modi
Ladakh dialogue to resume after December 15; elected representatives, LAB, KDA to be involved, says chief secretary
Guo Wengui's $67.5 million New York apartment sells for just $8 million to billionaire's son
Neighbours' safety fears put 100-acre Kansas deer-hunting business under zoning rules
stories.summary: A Kansas appeals court has ruled that a 100-acre deer-hunting business run by a couple cannot be treated as an agricultural operation and must obtain a special-use zoning permit. The ruling followed objections from two neighbouring couples, who raised safety concerns about commercial hunting taking place close to their properties.

stories.title: Wisconsin’s $1.1M Barbie Dream House goes under contract
stories.summary: In Hudson, Wisconsin, a charming pink Victorian house constructed in 1900 has made a remarkable transformation from its original Goth style. Recently listed at $1.1 million, the property is now under contract. Featuring seven bedrooms and four bathrooms, the home boasts inviting spaces for gatherings and rentals. The creative homeowner painted it pink and opened it up for various uses, showcasing its versatility.

stories.title: Historic gold dredging damaged a California river used by salmon and steelhead
stories.summary: Major funding has been secured for restoration initiatives aimed at revitalizing the salmon habitat along the Tuolumne River. The project will reestablish 20 acres at La Grange, improving conditions for salmon and steelhead. With new side channels and a historic floodplain, the area will become conducive for salmon spawning. Collaborative efforts by various organizations since 2020 highlight an ongoing dedication to ecological preservation in this region.

stories.title: Titanic survivor Lucy, Lady Duff Gordon’s diamond ring sells for £150,000 after staying in family for generations
stories.summary: A diamond ring belonging to Titanic survivor Lucy, Lady Duff Gordon, sold for £150,000 at auction. The ring was expected to fetch around £80,000 but achieved a much higher final price. Lady Duff Gordon wore the ring during the sinking of the Titanic, which occurred in 1912. Other Titanic memorabilia, including a rare ticket and a postcard, were also sold at the auction.

stories.title: UP polls: SP names four-member panel for seat-sharing talks with Congress from Monday
Phoenix man's 2015 deed had wrong address; court upheld invalidation of rival deeds
stories.summary: A property dispute arose in Phoenix, Arizona, due to a mistake in a property's street address. Robert Olsen received a quitclaim deed from his father, which included incorrect address details but correct property descriptions. Bonitas Casitas LLC later claimed ownership and filed a lawsuit, leading to competing claims over the property. The Arizona Court of Appeals upheld the lower court's ruling, reaffirming the validity of Olsen's original deed.

stories.title: Chef Jose Andres rescues Baltimore's 45-year-old Thanksgiving food tradition
stories.summary: Cynthia Brooks' efforts to continue her mother Bea Gaddy's 45-year-old Thanksgiving food tradition in Baltimore faced a setback after donations fell short, leaving her with only eight turkeys days before the event. Celebrity chef Jose Andres World Central Kitchen and the Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services stepped in with food and resources, helping save the annual dinner that began in 1981.

stories.title: Marshall’s 700 Meals: Family keeps holiday dinners going; her home serves hundreds in need
stories.summary: Carolyn Marshall honors her late mother, Reverend Annie Woodridge, by preparing festive meals for those in need. Overcoming various obstacles, she turned her home into a hub for food prep, drawing support from volunteers who help package and deliver meals. This initiative has blossomed into a cherished family and community effort, reinforcing the values of kindness and remembrance associated with her mother's legacy during the holidays.

stories.title: Adirondack Mountain Rescue: Becky’s arrival triggered search; rescuers found owner alive
stories.summary: When a basset hound named Becky showed up unaccompanied at a mountain lodge, it triggered an urgent search for her owner, a 69-year-old man living with dementia. Spending a night in the frigid wilderness, he was finally located by a hunter. Thanks to Becky's unexpected arrival, the rescue effort commenced quickly, potentially saving her owner's life.

stories.title: China’s secret AI chip hunt: How its spyverse is helping firms bypass US curbs
Phone numbers, QR code: Punjab BJP's new push to seek public input for 2027 'people's manifesto'
'Lotus has withered': Akhilesh Yadav's swipe at BJP over 'Radhe Radhe Kamal Khila De' slogan
Factory Fire: Seven bodies recovered; about 50 workers remain unaccounted for
stories.summary: A massive fire erupted at a candy factory in Cikande, Indonesia, resulting in the recovery of seven body bags. Authorities reported that around 50 workers remain unaccounted for as rescue efforts continue. The factory owner indicated that approximately 300 workers were present during the incident, which occurred on Saturday evening. Investigation teams are working to determine the cause of the fire while assessing the damage.

stories.title: 'Uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists’: Rahul shares Ardhanareshwar image to target BJP-RSS
'This is new India's response': BJP takes swipe at Pakistan over its minister's applause at Purana Qila
stories.summary: BJP criticized Pakistan by sharing a video of Minister Musadik Malik applauding Indian cultural presentations. This event took place at the three-day SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum hosted in Purana Qila, India. The BJP's montage highlighted contrasting statements made by Pakistani officials regarding Kashmir and India's culture. During the forum, Malik referenced historical figures associated with the Purana Qila fortress.

stories.title: 'Population up in 40 China-border villages': Amit Shah reaches out to Arunachal amid dam protests
stories.summary: Amit Shah unveiled key development initiatives in Arunachal Pradesh as part of the Vibrant Villages Programme, noting a population increase in 40 border villages that has curbed migration. He highlighted the need for self-reliance in food production while assuring local leaders of the Centre's ongoing support for development projects. Additionally, the Arunachal Pradesh Cooperative Vision 2047 was introduced, focusing on future growth strategies.

stories.title: Opposition questions US policy after report flags China’s support to Pakistan during Op Sindoor
Maine court upholds $1 million museum donation 14 years after collector's death
stories.summary: A charitable trust from Maine faced a legal battle over a donation intended for another museum. The Supreme Judicial Court determined that this donation did not violate any prior agreements. While the trust was obligated to fulfill its financial duties to the original museum, it could also manage its assets.

stories.title: Delta Seat Lawsuit: Judge lets claims proceed; airlines may face scrutiny over seat descriptions
stories.summary: Passengers have raised concerns, claiming Delta Air Lines sold them window seats that lacked actual windows. A New York federal judge recently gave the green light for a class-action lawsuit against the airline. This issue emerged when a traveler discovered his seat had no window, prompting Delta to argue that seat assignments aren’t guaranteed. United Airlines is facing similar complaints about windowless seating as well.

stories.title: Karthigai Deepam row: Tamil Nadu govt moves SC against one-time lamp lighting permission atop Thiruparankundram hill
Galloo Island Conservation Easement: TILT protects 1,410 acres; Patten family retains ownership
stories.summary: A landmark conservation deal has been executed for Galloo Island, safeguarding 1,410 acres of pristine land. The Thousand Islands Land Trust has joined forces with Galloo Island Farms and the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation to enforce permanent land use restrictions aimed at preserving the island's ecological integrity.

stories.title: Carnegie Museum will prepare three sauropods in public; researchers study rare skin samples
stories.summary: Three sauropod fossils from Wyoming, nicknamed Daisy, Lucky, and Lucy, are headed for Pittsburgh. A $5 million donation from Ken Griffin will construct a public fossil preparation laboratory at the Carnegie Museum of Natural History. Visitors will be able to observe the cleaning and studying process of these 150-million-year-old dinosaurs. Additionally, research will focus on rare fossilized skin samples associated with the fossils.

stories.title: COP31: Backlash after Türkiye's draft agreement omits fossil fuels
‘Bitten by dogs’: Revanth Reddy’s swipe at dissenting MLAs sparks row in Telangana Congress
'No such proposal': India dismisses reports of seeking Nepal's airspace for military flights
stories.summary: Reports claiming India sought permission from Nepal for military aircraft usage have been clarified as false. Sources have stated that there is no proposal regarding such military access to Bagdogra. This clarification coincides with discussions on air connectivity ahead of Prime Minister Balendra Shah's visit to India. During his visit, Shah will engage in talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi to strengthen bilateral relations.

stories.title: Nepal PM Balen Shah arrives in India for first visit; talks with PM Modi on Monday - top developments
'No place for hate in cricket’: Congress leader rejects Masood’s religious bias charge over Siraj
‘Vote Chori’ allegations: Nitin Nabin to lead BJP's Hyderabad rally to counter criticism
stories.summary: BJP president Nitin Nabin will lead a rally in Hyderabad to counter criticism about the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Union minister Bandi Sanjay Kumar supports this event, claiming it to be historic, and anticipates a large turnout. Kumar accused opposition parties, including Congress and BRS, of collaborating to impede BJP's growth in Telangana. He argued that only Indian citizens should have the right to elect their leaders.

stories.title: Sabarimala pilgrimage: Kerala puts security, transport arrangements in place amid devotee rush
stories.summary: The Sabarimala Lord Ayyappa Temple has commenced its much-anticipated annual Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage. This year, the influx of devotees is met with extensive security measures and administrative support. The Kerala government has undertaken significant infrastructure upgrades, enhancing roads and transport services. Throughout the pilgrimage, police will be actively deployed to ensure safety and manage traffic. This first phase will last until December 27, followed by festivities for Makaravilakku.

stories.title: After first-ever foreign office talks, Jaishankar calls for deeper India-Lebanon ties
stories.summary: S Jaishankar, India’s External Affairs Minister, sent heartfelt National Day wishes to Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Raggi and the people of Lebanon. With a focus on deepening diplomatic relations, both countries recently initiated their first foreign office consultations. These discussions emphasized political, security, and economic partnerships, reflecting India's vital contributions to peacekeeping in Lebanon. The intent is to foster stronger ties via consistent high-level dialogues and collaborative efforts.

stories.title: Iran says 428 children killed in two wars, Red Crescent chief calls for independent probe into Minab school attack
US sells Jammeh-linked mansion, returns $2.5 million to Gambian victims
Trump moves to limit congressional scrutiny before Democrats take power of Congress
Flatbush Collapse Lawsuit: Tenant alleges landlord ignored cracks; claims remain unproven
stories.summary: In the wake of a devastating building collapse in Brooklyn that claimed eight lives, a musician has taken legal action against the landlord for ignoring warnings about visible cracks weeks prior. The lawsuit also raises alarms about nearby construction projects lacking proper structural support. Authorities are now probing the oversight of such projects in densely populated neighborhoods, questioning the responsiveness to residents' concerns before the tragic incident occurred.

stories.title: Former US President George Washington's hair sells for $4,000
stories.summary: At a recent auction, a rare lock of George Washington’s hair sold for an impressive $4,000. This fascinating artifact once belonged to John Gadsby, who shared a meal with Washington shortly before his passing. Gadsby’s granddaughter later cherished the lock alongside a portrait of the first president, making it a remarkable piece of history. Notably, Washington's hair has previously commanded prices nearing $40,000 at auctions, alongside other treasured memorabilia.

Ohio landlord mistakenly throws away tenant's loved belongings; court upholds $6,000 award

stories.title: More than 8,000 people applied to be NASA astronauts last time and just 10 were picked
stories.summary: NASA is currently accepting applications until December 3, 2026, for aspiring astronauts who dream of exploring outer space. To qualify, applicants must be U.S. citizens possessing a master's degree and relevant experience. Those with medical certifications or extensive flight backgrounds are particularly encouraged to apply. Selected astronauts will undergo rigorous training before embarking on missions to the Moon and Mars, with final candidates expected to be revealed by late 2027.

stories.summary: After a lengthy shutdown in 2025 due to property issues, Original Pantry Cafe in Los Angeles has triumphantly reopened! With new management from Hope the Mission, the cafe will utilize its profits to bolster homelessness services. Diners can still indulge in the beloved classic menu while also enjoying fresh additions. Although hours have shifted, there are plans to bring back 24-hour service.

stories.title: As ice receded on a Swiss Alpine pass, archaeologists discovered a 4,000 years old bronze neck ring
stories.summary: A remarkable discovery at Lötschen Pass has unearthed a 4,000-year-old bronze neck ring, making it the first metal artifact found at this significant historical site. While previous discoveries were primarily organic materials preserved in ice, this find suggests that ancient peoples may have practiced mobility through Alpine passes, connecting various regions. Experts speculate that the ring could have served as a ritual offering or token of gratitude.

Asmongold's infamous house controversy returns after GTA 6 livestream with girlfriend Kaise

Kaise jokingly compared the digital mess to Asmongold's real-life living situation, prompting laughs and nostalgia about Asmongold's cleanliness challenges. Even with improvements noted in 2026, his home remains a hot topic among viewers, fueling the ongoing chatter about his infamous house saga.

stories.title: IShowSpeed teases huge announcement after completing GTA 6 following 52-hour livestream
stories.summary: IShowSpeed celebrated a remarkable achievement by completing GTA 6's story mode in just 52 hours, far surpassing his initial plan of a 12-hour stream. His enthusiasm led him to extend the session, and upon finishing, he expressed heartfelt thanks and hinted at exciting future plans. Although a PS5 crash presented some obstacles, his progress was secure, keeping fans on the edge of their seats for his next move.

stories.title: Indiana man paid $9,489 towards condo debt after $9,213 judgment, but court says he still owes more
stories.summary: Onnie James Florence Jr. encountered significant legal troubles stemming from his failure to pay homeowners' association fees for his condominium in Indiana. After acquiring the unit, he neglected to keep up with payments while residing in Illinois. The Meridian Arch Owners Association successfully secured a default judgment against him for the overdue fees. Despite making a partial payment later, additional fees remained unpaid, prompting ongoing legal action.

stories.title: Dua Lipa's £6.75 million London home renovation set to finish in 2027
stories.summary: Dua Lipa is making waves with the transformation of her Victorian home in Hampstead, which includes an ambitious plan for a luxurious basement pool. After encountering numerous setbacks, the project received the green light to commence construction in 2024. Local environmental concerns have prompted strict adherence to regulations, pushing the anticipated completion to 2027. With an investment estimated at around £3 million, this renovation underscores its intricate and grand vision.

Scientists flew drones through humpback whales' breath off Canada and sequenced entire genomes
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of St Andrews have pioneered a groundbreaking technique to harness whale DNA through the use of drones. This method captures genetic material from the whales' breath, often referred to as whale snot. Their findings successfully sequenced complete genomes from specimens gathered off the coast of British Columbia.

Texas Fraud Charges: Man allegedly won 70 contracts; counterfeit gear raises concerns

He allegedly misrepresented his military background, impersonated government officials, and manipulated suppliers to stifle competition. Furthermore, investigators found he sold counterfeit military gear, mislabeling it as American-made but failing to meet specifications. He faces several charges as the investigation proceeds.

stories.title: Beverly Hills penthouse sells for $21M, with rooftop pool and $18,740 monthly dues

The fortunate buyer also saved over $1 million in transfer taxes by opting for Beverly Hills over Los Angeles.

stories.summary: Jerry and Joanne Braun donated approximately 77 acres of land to the Town of Newburgh. This land donation aims to protect the drinking water supply sourced from the Chadwick Lake Reservoir. The couple requested reimbursement for subdividing the land, not seeking payment for it. Residents will still have access for passive recreational activities like hiking and enjoying nature.

stories.summary: Tŷ Hafan, a remarkable children's hospice located in Wales, has triumphed by surpassing its fundraising goal during the Every Precious Life campaign. The initiative offers $1 million in prizes to student teams from high schools and universities. Teams will focus on areas like power generation, life-support systems, and astronaut safety to address the complexities of lunar living. Registration for the competition is open until January 25, 2027, to eligible educational institutions.

stories.summary: In a tragic turn of events, Cheryl Lynn Rhines suffered a severe stroke while driving and was mistakenly arrested for intoxication. stories.summary: In a significant legal move, a federal grand jury has charged leaders of the La Nueva Familia Michoacana cartel along with 19 associates. Prominent figures Johnny Hurtado Olascoaga and Jose Alfredo Hurtado Olascoaga are on the run, purportedly using violence and bribery to grow their criminal empire and engage in human smuggling.

After her passing, her husband, Warren Lewis, tirelessly advocated for revisions to the university's body donation policy. This advocacy birthed a collaboration with Macquarie University, enabling weekend donations and ensuring that future donors' wishes are honored, despite bureaucratic hurdles. stories.summary: David and Sara LeBlanc have taken legal action against Ogunquit, Maine, after being penalized for setting up rooster sculptures outside their home. Adams' own experiences fuel his drive to give back, fostering a spirit of community as Thanksgiving Heroes continues to grow.

stories.title: 3 killed as minibus plunges into 100-foot gorge on Kodaikanal-Palani Ghat Road
stories.summary: Three people were killed, and several others were injured after a minibus carrying 24 passengers plunged into a 100-foot-deep gorge near Savarikkadu on the Kodaikanal–Ghat Road in Dindigul district. The passengers were returning from a wedding function in Kodaikanal. Rescue teams rushed to the spot and shifted the injured to nearby hospitals.

Virginia court rules on lakeside home disputed by widow and her late husband's children
stories.summary: A complex legal battle unfolded over a lakeside property in Virginia involving a widow and the children of her deceased husband. The court has decided that the widow retains a fifty percent ownership stake, while her husband’s children will inherit the remaining half. This ruling reversed a prior decision and provided clarity on property rights, paving the way for future partition proceedings while maintaining the widow's current living situation.

stories.title: Rupert Grint wins approval to build 15 homes on former £6 million estate
stories.summary: Rupert Grint has successfully secured planning permission to create an eco-village at his Kimpton Grange estate in Hertfordshire. This sustainable project will feature six apartments, nine additional homes, a public park, and contribute to local infrastructure improvements, particularly for schools. Earlier concerns from residents regarding wildlife preservation have been addressed, showcasing Grint's commitment to balancing development with environmental care, marking a departure from his previous intent to sell the estate.

stories.title: Partner Loan Remains Payable: Davis forgave family debts; Schriefer’s loan stays due
stories.summary: The estate of Clive Davis, valued at over $50 million at the time of his passing in June, highlights a complex legacy. His will notably forgives the debts of several individuals while specifically excluding his long-time partner Greg Schriefer from such leniency. After the will was admitted to probate, Davis' impressive Manhattan residence hit the market, adding to his extensive real estate and personal property portfolio.

This necessitates urgent investments in youth services and reproductive health to fulfill their future aspirations. Despite economic concerns, young individuals exhibit remarkable optimism, reflecting evolving societal norms and women's choices regarding family size.

Teacher fired for refusing Covid tests wins as court says school board cannot skip dismissal hearing
stories.summary: Neal Follman, a dedicated teacher from Philadelphia, faced termination after he declined to participate in mandatory Covid-19 testing set by the school district. He challenged this dismissal, claiming that the hearing was improperly conducted. The Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled in his favor, underscoring that no elected board members were present during his hearing.

stories.title: 3 leopards found dead in North Kashmir, poisoning suspected
The Euclid space telescope has spotted 31 ancient quasars, including two record-breakers
stories.summary: The Euclid space telescope has made a groundbreaking discovery by identifying 31 ancient quasars, significantly contributing to the field of astronomy. Notably, two of these quasars hold the record for their vast distances, originating when the Universe was just 670 million years old. Their light journeyed over 13 billion years to reach Earth, offering unparalleled insights into the early stages of cosmic history.

This estate is not only historically rich, with ties to Mick Jagger during the filming of Ned Kelly, but also exemplifies sustainable farming practices that have garnered international praise. With its working farm and agricultural opportunities, this estate promises to attract diverse potential buyers, merging history with farming viability.

Illinois woman was murdered in 1966; family friend who carried her coffin convicted 60 years later
stories.summary: In a harrowing case that spanned nearly six decades, eighteen-year-old Karen Snider lost her life in her home, leaving her infant daughter nearby. A breakthrough in DNA evidence recently led to the conviction of family friend James Barbier for her murder. The long-awaited justice has brought a sigh of relief to Karen's daughter, who now has answers about her mother's untimely death.

stories.title: Satellite images 38 years apart show Indonesia's Puncak Jaya glaciers shrinking to tiny ice patches
stories.summary: Puncak Jaya has lost nearly all its glacier ice due to rising temperatures and changing weather patterns. Recent satellite images reveal a stark reduction in glacier coverage over the past decades. The melting glaciers impact local climates and contribute to global challenges despite their small size. Research indicates that the remaining ice also holds important climate history, which will soon be lost.

This decision ensures equal pay for both foreign and Indian medical interns, adhering to the National Medical Commission's guidelines issued earlier this year. Several government medical institutions are set to adopt this stipend without delay, marking an important step in supporting foreign medical professionals.

stories.title: Washington landowner's dam repairs led to neighbour's pond filling with sediment; what the court said
stories.summary: In a pivotal decision, a Washington state court upheld a significant $554,000 judgment against Robert Shawn Noecker due to extensive property damages linked to unauthorized construction on a malfunctioning dam. This mishap not only unleashed water and debris but was further exacerbated by drainage modifications that redirected water onto his land.

stories.title: Pennsylvania finds Walmart child labour violations; retailer agrees to pay $7.8m after injuries
stories.summary: Walmart has reached a settlement in response to a Pennsylvania investigation that uncovered serious breaches of child labour laws. The probe identified instances of young workers facing excessive hours and lacking work permits across various locations. As part of the settlement, Walmart will incur penalties of $7.8 million and must adopt stricter compliance protocols to safeguard young employees, setting a crucial benchmark in tackling child labour issues in the state.

stories.summary: In De Pere, Wisconsin, a family faces a contentious dispute with their homeowners association regarding a fence. The association has spread the financial burden among property owners, many of whom have failed to contribute.

stories.summary: A dedicated conservation initiative along the Breekkrans River is tackling the dangers of invasive spotted bass. The project aims to safeguard the critically endangered doring fiery redfin, which is currently struggling for survival. By eradicating these invasive fish, the redfin’s habitat will expand, giving it a better chance of thriving. Innovative removal methods are employed while also creating job opportunities for the local community, thereby bolstering freshwater conservation efforts.

stories.title: Zeynab Javadli, ex-wife of Dubai prince Sheikh Saeed, alleges UAE officials drugged her, took daughters
stories.summary: Zeynab Javadli, former wife of Dubai prince Sheikh Saeed bin Maktoum, has approached the United Nations seeking an investigation into allegations that UAE officials assaulted and drugged her during a raid in which her three daughters were taken away. Her legal team has also raised concerns over her alleged torture in custody and the children's whereabouts.

The Elms Experience: Newport opens 20-room multisensory tour; scents and projections evoke Gilded Age

stories.summary: Amit Shah emphasized the need for international cooperation in the fight against terrorism and organized crime, specifically calling for the return of offenders hiding abroad. He pointed out important milestones, such as the dismantling of the Popular Front of India network. The ongoing two-day Anti-Terror Conference aims to foster intelligence sharing and strengthen investigations, ultimately enhancing inter-agency collaboration to tackle evolving security threats.

Mahadev betting app case: Kingpin Saurabh Chandrakar sent to judicial custody till December 2

The Enforcement Directorate indicated that it does not require further custodial interrogation at this point. Chandrakar was extradited from Oman earlier this month and produced before the court after a CBI operation. With Packer having moved on from the U.S.

stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday urged industry leaders to prioritise employee compensation and expand their workforce. PM Modi also emphasised the importance of maintaining high product standards, and reducing reliance on imported pharmaceuticals to fortify local industries.

stories.summary: In British Columbia, a woman's legal complaint against her neighbors' scented laundry products was dismissed after the strata council's investigation failed to pinpoint the odor's source. stories.title: Next door, worlds apart: India's child malnutrition puzzle
stories.summary: Child malnutrition is shaped by several factors, including maternal education and household wealth. While India's stunting rate has declined nationally, problems such as child wasting persist. A closer look at the latest survey data reveals striking differences even between neighbouring districts and raises questions about what lies behind these gaps.

India, Italy target €20bn trade by 2029, explore economic corridor linking Asia and Europe
stories.summary: India and Italy aim to elevate their bilateral trade to €20 billion by 2029, establishing dedicated task forces in both nations to help local businesses tackle bureaucratic hurdles more effectively. stories.summary: Sukhdev Singh Kang has purchased the ancestral home of Sonia Gandhi located in Italy and intends to open a museum. The property, identified as Sonia Gandhi's birthplace, has garnered significant interest from Indian visitors. Although he sought a physical division to continue living there, the Arkansas Court of Appeals ultimately deemed his appeal moot after the property was sold to a third party. This case highlights the complex challenges heirs may encounter in property disputes.

stories.summary: Recently, the elusive Awá tribe, famed for their isolation, reached out to a neighboring settlement in the Arariboia Indigenous territory. In search of food and assistance, their visit exposed the severe impacts of illegal land encroachments. Local villagers documented the meeting, bringing attention to the perils that Indigenous people face. Advocacy groups are demanding stronger safeguards and acknowledgment of the rights of uncontacted tribes to preserve their way of life.

stories.summary: The ministry of road transport and highways recently unveiled revised regulations concerning pollution under control certificates. The new guidelines offer longer validity for BS-VI vehicles based on their age and usage while mandating more frequent emission checks for older vehicles. Furthermore, there will be a standardised validity period for older emission categories throughout India, enhancing compliance and promoting uniformity in emission standards.

Shivakumar referred to her as the 'Iron Lady,' praising her pivotal roles in sectors such as agriculture and banking, and underscoring her enduring influence on the country’s political landscape.

stories.title: 'Use of natural resources boomerang-ing back to bite': India accuses Pakistan of self-aggrandisement
stories.summary: India flagged Pakistan's military establishment of exploiting the country's natural resources for personal gain and fomenting conflict with neighbours at a UNSC meeting. stories.title: Kandinsky painting sells for record $85.8 million, nearly doubling artist's previous auction high
stories.summary: Wassily Kandinsky’s painting Betonte Ecken achieved a record-breaking price of $85.8 million at Christie’s New York. The auction event generated a total of $627 million and included numerous notable artworks. Competitive bidding was evident, with multiple collectors participating for high-value pieces. Other artists like Gustav Klimt and Pablo Picasso also saw substantial sales. The results indicate a vibrant market for modern and Impressionist art continues to thrive.

Malaysia to not remain visa free for Indian visitors from Jan 1, 2027

The High Commission of India in Kuala Lumpur has issued warnings regarding these violations of immigration rules. Indian nationals must obtain a valid visa prior to travelling to Malaysia from this date onward.

'Not inclined to interfere': Supreme Court rejects ED plea against Azam Khan's interim bail

stories.summary: Elton John's iconic Yamaha piano, which has graced St Pancras International since 2016, is set to be auctioned soon to support the Elton John AIDS Foundation in honor of World AIDS Day. This rare item not only represents a significant moment in British music history but also offers bidders a chance to contribute to a vital cause.

stories.summary: In downtown Los Angeles, the partially completed Oceanwide Plaza is getting a makeover as graffiti is being removed. With $850 million pledged by KPC Group and Lendlease, this project is set to offer luxury residences, a hotel, and retail spaces. Positioned as a key component of the city's strategy to uplift the downtown area for the 2028 Summer Olympics, community engagement will be central to these revitalization efforts.

stories.summary: In Tasmania, two bushwalkers found themselves in a perilous situation due to unexpected weather changes, prompting them to activate their personal locator beacon for assistance. While emergency services launched a rescue mission, harsh conditions hindered helicopter access, leading a search-and-rescue team to trek through difficult landscapes to reach the hikers.

stories.summary: Recent satellite observations reveal striking similarities between the anticipated 2026 El Niño and the notorious 1997 event. Elevated sea levels across the Pacific are raising alarm among scientists regarding its expected severity. This climatic shift could drastically alter global weather patterns, with countries like India potentially facing erratic monsoon conditions. Experts estimate an 83% likelihood of heightened intensity in early 2027, posing significant risks for various regions.

Notably, admissions at Sri Venkateshwaraa Medical College are currently on hold per the court’s interim order.

stories.title: Alex Trebek's former 578-acre California winery ranch heads to December auction
stories.summary: Creston Manor, a majestic estate formerly belonging to Alex Trebek, is now up for auction following an unsuccessful private sale. Initially listed at $7 million, the price has been lowered, with online bidding commencing on December 4, leading to a live auction later that month.

stories.title: A great horned owl in Pennsylvania survived being struck by a tractor-trailer travelling at 65 mph
stories.summary: In an incredible tale of survival, a great horned owl in Pennsylvania endured a harrowing journey after being struck by a truck and wedged in its air dam. Traveling roughly 70 miles, the owl was finally found by trucking terminal employees. Despite sustaining an eye injury, it was otherwise unharmed.

stories.title: Metal detectorist Daniel Crowe found a Viking hoard on the Isle of Man
stories.summary: Daniel Crowe made an astonishing discovery of a Viking hoard on the Isle of Man, revealing a trove of jewellery and weapons that shed light on the social hierarchy and burial customs of the early Viking Age. This remarkable collection offers crucial insights into the roles women played in Viking society, with artefacts showcasing intricate designs and suggesting links to extensive trading networks across the British Isles.

stories.title: Researchers discovered a new scorpion species in Odisha's Similipal Tiger Reserve
stories.summary: A newly documented scorpion species has been unveiled, representing the first instance of Liocheles in Odisha. Researchers designated this species as Liocheles similipalensis following an in-depth analysis of its physical traits. With this addition, the total number of recognized Liocheles species globally rises to seven, and four of these have been discovered in India.

stories.title: Hong Kong Case Dropped: Prosecutors cite unreachable witnesses; captain faces deportation
stories.summary: The Hong Kong authorities have chosen to drop the prosecution against Captain Wan Wenguo for the Balticconnector gas pipeline damage, citing challenges in reaching essential witnesses from mainland China. Although he pleaded not guilty, Captain Wan accepted responsibility for safety violations. Evidence connected his vessel to the pipeline incident, leading to expectations of his deportation to mainland China.

stories.title: Major KFC franchisee files for bankruptcy protection, may shut more outlets
stories.summary: A major KFC franchisee, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection citing financial difficulties. The company seeks to restructure its operations and avoid losing its franchise agreement with Yum Brands. Tasty Chick’n has closed 44 restaurant locations this year and may shut down more in the future. The franchisee owes approximately $16 million in unpaid royalties to its parent company, Yum Brands.

stories.title: ‘Revolution, not election’: SP's Azam Khan, on interim bail, predicts 'deluge' in upcoming UP polls
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan, after receiving interim bail, declared the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls a revolution. He criticized constitutional bodies for diminishing public faith and referenced historical educationists to highlight injustice. Khan emphasized that voters will focus on real issues rather than religion and caste in the elections. He expressed readiness to fight for constitutional rights and justice once SP forms a government.

stories.title: Construction Halt: Judge extends arch pause 14 days; court weighs longer ban
stories.summary: US District Judge Tanya Chutkan has granted an extension on the temporary halt of the memorial arch's construction, prolonging it for an additional 14 days. stories.title: GTA 6 has an India connection, partly built by developers in Bengaluru: BJP's Tejasvi Surya
stories.summary: Tejasvi Surya from the Bharatiya Janata Party emphasized Bengaluru's role in developing the highly anticipated video game Grand Theft Auto VI. Over 1,600 developers at Rockstar India's Bengaluru studio worked on the game, showcasing the city's gaming ecosystem. The game marks a return to Vice City, featuring two protagonists in an open-world narrative. It has received multiple nominations at the upcoming 2026 Game Awards scheduled for December 10.

stories.title: Court reopens British mother's fight against daughter's adoption after her life turnaround
stories.summary: A British mother has begun to reclaim her life, overcoming a challenging past marked by substance abuse and domestic violence. stories.summary: In a significant stride for land conservation, Florida's Commissioner of Agriculture, Wilton Simpson, revealed plans to safeguard three distinct properties spanning DeSoto, St. Johns, and Polk counties. These initiatives focus on sustaining agricultural lands while protecting valuable natural resources.
